english: Your skin is your largest organ, and it's important to take care of it both inside and out. Here are some tips for healthy skin:

english: * Drink plenty of water: Water is essential for healthy skin, as it helps to keep your skin hydrated and soft. Aim to drink eight glasses of water per day.
ga: * Nuu nu pii: Nu he hia ha gbɔmɔtso wolo kpakpa, koni ewa gbɔmɔtso wolo lɛ ni ewo fɔ ni efee bɛdɛɛ. Feemɔ akɛ obaanu nu glase kpaanyɔ daa gbi.

english: * Eat a healthy diet: Eating a healthy diet rich in fruits, vegetables, and whole grains can help to improve your skin's appearance.
ga: * Ye hewalɛ niyenii: Hewalɛ niyenii ni aduawai, baai, kɛ ŋmaa eyi mii ma ni ayeɔ baanyɛ ni ewa ohewolo ni efee fɛo.

english: * Get regular exercise: Exercise can help to improve your circulation and promote healthy skin. Aim for at least 30 minutes of moderate-intensity exercise most days of the week.
ga: * Na kpojiaŋgbɔlemɔ daa: kpojiaŋgbɔlemɔ waa ola tsɔɔ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni eha ohewolo feɔ fɛo. Feemɔ kpojiagbɔlemɔ ni naa wa fioo minitii 30 yɛ otsii lɛ mli.

english: * Get enough sleep: When you don't get enough sleep, your body produces more of the stress hormone cortisol, which can lead to inflammation and skin problems. Aim for 7-8 hours of sleep per night.
ga: * Wɔ jogbaŋŋ: Kɛji onaaa wɔ pii lɛ, ogbɔmɔtso lɛ jieɔ tɔlɛ yibii cortisol, ni haa fuumɔ baa kɛ hewolo saji. Wɔ 7-8 ŋmɛlɛtswai daa gbɛkɛ.

english: * Protect your skin from the sun: The sun's UV rays can damage your skin and lead to premature aging, wrinkles, and skin cancer.
ga: * Buu ohewolo he kɛjɛ hulu: Hulu lɛ UV reys banyɛ ni efite ohewolo ni etsɔɔ dalɛ oya, hewolonɔ akũa, kɛ hewolo kansa.

ga: Hetsɔi diŋŋ eha egbɔmɔtso he, ni eyitso yɛ tɔrɔmɔɔ, bɔɔlu kokro.

english: It has no eyes, but I can see two large, pointed ears.
ga: Ebɛɛɛ hiŋmɛ, shi ma nyɛ mana toi agbo, kakadaŋŋ.

english: “What are we going to do?” I ask.
ga: "Mɛni wɔ baa fee?" Mi bi.

english: “We need to get out of here,” Mum says. “Now.”
ga: "Esa ni wɔ shi biɛnɛ," Ma kɛɛ. "Bianɛ nɔɔ."

english: We run out of the kitchen and into the living room.
ga: Wɔ jofoi kɛjɛ kpataashi kɛtee asa lɛ mli.

english: “Mum! Dad!” I cry. “There’s something outside!”
ga: "Ma! Da!" Mi fo. "Noko yɛ kpo lɛ nɔ!"

english: Dad looks up from the TV. “What is it?” he asks.
ga: Da kwɛ ŋwɛi kɛjɛ TV lɛ. "Mɛni ni?" ebi.

english: “I don’t know,” Mum says. “But it’s big and it’s coming this way.”
ga: "Mi leee," Ma kɛɛ. "Shi eda ni eebaa nɛkɛ gbɛ."

english: Dad gets up from the couch.
ga: Da teshi kɛjɛ sɛi lɛ mli.

english: “We need to get out of here,” he says.
ga: "Esani wɔ shi biɛ," ekɛɛ.

english: We all run for the front door.
ga: Wɔ fɛɛ wɔ jo foi kɛ tee shinaa hiɛ.

english: Mum unlocks it and we rush outside.
ga: Ma gbele ni wɔ kɛ oya tee kpo lɛ nɔ.

english: The creature is right behind us.
ga: Adebɔɔ lɛ damɔ wɔ sɛɛ tuutu.

english: It’s so close I can feel its hot breath on the back of my neck.
ga: Ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ akɛ manyɛ ma nu emumɔ ni edɔ yɛ mi kuɛ sɛɛ.

english: We run to the car and get in.
ga: Wɔ jo foi kɛ tee car he ni wɔ bote mli.

english: Dad starts the engine and we peel out of the driveway.
ga: Da su tsɔne lɛ ni wɔ shi gbɛjegbɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: The creature chases after us, but we’re too fast.
ga: Adebɔɔ lɛ tsaa wɔshi, shi wɔ fee oya.

english: Movies have long been a powerful force in shaping our culture and our values.
ga: Sini efee shimɔ hewalɛ nii ni jajeɔ wɔ kusum kɛ wɔ jeŋbai.

english: They can influence our beliefs about everything from love and romance to war and violence.
ga: Amɛ baanyɛ ni amɛ na hewalɛ yɛ wɔ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ kɛjɛ suɔmɔ kɛ eyeli kɛ tee taa kɛ basabasafeemɔ.

english: And they have a particularly strong influence on our ideas about gender roles.
ga: Ni amɛ yɛ hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ ko yɛ wɔ susumɔi kɛha hii kɛ yei anifeemɔi.

english: For decades, Hollywood has perpetuated the stereotype of the ideal wife as a beautiful, submissive, and domestic woman who puts her husband and children first.
ga: Afii nyɔŋmai abɔ nɛ, Hollywood eha bɔni esa akɛ ŋamɛi he afee fɛo, amɛ ba ahe shi, kɛ shia yei ni kɛ amɛ wu kɛ bii baa dani nɔfɛɛ nɔ.

english: This image is often reinforced by the way that female characters are portrayed in movies.
ga: Anaa mfoniri nɛɛ yɛ bɔni ajieɔ yei sini jielɔ kpo yɛ sini mli.

english: For example, a study by the Geena Davis Institute found that in the top 100 films of 2017, only 30% of female characters had speaking roles, and only 12% of those characters were working outside the home.
ga: Nɔkwɛmɔnɔ, Geena Davis Institute nikasemɔ ko na akɛ yɛ sinii 100 ni afee yɛ 2017 ni nyiɛ hiɛ lɛ, emli yei 30% pɛ na wiemɔ nitsumɔi, ni amɛ mli 12% tsu nii yɛ shia kponɔ.

english: The majority of female characters were portrayed as either romantic interests or mothers.
ga: Ajie yei sini jielɔ pii akɛ suɔlɔi loo nyɛmɛi.

english: This narrow representation of women in film sends a powerful message to viewers about what it means to be a woman.
ga: Yei sini jielɔi akpo jiemɔ yɛ sini mli ha hewalɛ sane kɛha kwɛlɔi yɛ bɔni yei yɔɔ.

english: It suggests that women's primary role is to be attractive and nurturing, and that their success is measured by their relationships with men and children.
ga: Ekɛɔ akɛ yei anitsumɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ji he fɛo kɛ tsɔsemɔ, ni akɛ amɛ gbalashihilɛ kɛ amɛ wumɛi kɛ bii susuɔ amɛ omanye yeli.

english: This idealized image of the wife can be harmful to women in several ways.
ga: Nɛkɛ jwɛŋmɔ ni ayɔɔ yɛ ŋmamɛi ahe baanyɛ ni efee naagba sane kɛha yei yɛ gbenɔi babaoo.

english: Patient: Doctor, I've been having this terrible stomach pain for the past few days.
ga: Helatsɛ: Datrɛfonyo, mi naa musu piŋmɔ ni ehiii kraa bei fioo ni eho nɛɛ.

english: It's so bad that I can't eat or sleep.
ga: Enaa wa waa akɛ mi nyɛɛɛ ma yenii loo ma wɔ.

english: It's a sharp, stabbing pain that comes and goes.
ga: Eji piŋmɔ ni yɛ oya, ni etsulɔɔ mi ni baa ni eyaa.

english: Doctor: Can you tell me more about the pain? Where is it located?
ga: Datrɛfonyo: Ani obaanyɛ ni okɛɛ mi piŋmɔ lɛ he sane? Higbɛ eyɔɔ?

english: Patient: It's mostly in my lower abdomen, right around my belly button, but it sometimes radiates to my back.
ga: Helatsɛ: bei pii lɛ eyɛ mi musu, shi bei komɛi lɛ ejɛɔ mi sɛɛ.

english: Doctor: Does anything make the pain worse?
ga: Datrɛfonyo: Ani noko haa piŋmɔ ewaa ohe fe nine?

english: Patient: Eating seems to make it worse, especially fatty or greasy foods.
ga: Helatsɛ: Niyeli haa ewaa mihe fe nine, titri fɔ niyenii loo niyenii ni ewo fɔ.

english: Doctor: And does anything make it better.?
ga: Datrɛfonyo: Ani noko haa ehiɔ lo.?

english: Patient: Lying down seems to help a little.
ga: Helatsɛ: Shikãmɔ haa ehiɔ fioo.

english: Doctor: Does the pain come and go, or is it constant?
ga: Datrɛfonyo: Ani piŋmɔ lɛ yaa ni ebaa, loo ehiɔ jɛmɛ daa?

english: Patient: It's constant. It's just a dull ache, but it's really uncomfortable.
ga: Helatsɛ: ehiɔ jɛmɛ daa. Enaa waaa kɛkɛ, shi ehaaa mi he ajɔɔ mi.

english: Doctor: Have you had any other symptoms? Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea?
ga: Datrɛfonyo: Ani onaa okadii krokomɛi lo? shwee aba, shwee, musuŋtsɔmɔ?

english: Patient: No, just the pain.
ga: Helatsɛ: Daabi, piŋmɔ kɛkɛ ni.

english: Doctor: I see. Well, it sounds like you're having a case of gastritis.
ga: Datrɛfonyo: Mina. Ojogbaŋŋ, etamɔ oona musu mɔmɔ hela.

english: Gastritis is inflammation of the stomach lining.
ga: Musu mɔmɔ hela ji musu lɛ miifuumɔ.

english: It can be caused by a number of things, including eating spicy or fatty foods, drinking alcohol, or taking certain medications.
ga: Nibii pii baanyɛ eha eba, niyenii ni shaamɔ loo niyenii ni ewo fɔ, daa numɔ, loo tsofa kɔmɔ fatahe.

english: Patient: Is it serious?
ga: Helatsɛ: Eji hiɛdɔɔ sane lo?

english: Doctor: It can be, but in most cases it's not.
ga: Datrɛfonyo: Ebaa nyɛ efee, shi bei pii lɛ jeee nakai.

english: I'm going to prescribe you some medication to help relieve the pain and inflammation.
ga: Mi ŋma bo tsofa ni ewa kɛ piŋmɔ shibaa kɛ fuumɔ.

english: You should also avoid eating spicy or fatty foods, and drink plenty of fluids.
ga: Esa ni okpa niyenii ni shitɔ yɔɔ mli loo niyenii ni ewo fɔ, ni onu nu pii.

english: Ingredients:
ga: Nibii:

english: * 1 cup all-purpose flour
ga: * Ashikiŋsha kɔɔpoo 1

english: * 1 cup almond flour
ga: *Almond ashikishaŋ kɔɔpoo 1

english: * 1/2 cup granulated sugar
ga: *sikli kɔɔpoo 1/2

english: * 1/4 cup packed light brown sugar
ga: *sikli asarasu ni ato kɔɔpoo 1/4

english: * 1/2 teaspoon baking powder
ga: * nishãa paada tii awale 1/2

english: * 1/4 teaspoon baking soda
ga: * nishãa soda tii awale 1/4

english: * 1/4 teaspoon salt
ga: * ŋoo tii awale 1/4

english: * 1/2 cup (1 stick) unsalted butter, at room temperature
ga: * bɔta ni ŋoo bɛ mli (tso 1) kɔɔpoo 1/2, yɛ tsu mli dɔlɛ

english: * 1 large egg
ga: * wuɔ wɔlɔ agbo 1

english: * 1 large egg yolk
ga: * wɔlɔ yok agbo 1

english: * 1 teaspoon almond extract
ga: * almond mli nu tii awale 1

english: * 1/2 cup milk
ga: * mliki kɔɔpoo 1/2

english: Instructions:
ga: Gbɛtsɔɔmɔi:

english: 1. Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease and flour an 8-inch round cake pan.
ga: 1. Dɔɔ flɔnɔɔ lɛ mli kɛya shi 350 degree F (175 degrees C). Wo 8 waotalɔi keeki pan kokroo mii fɔ kɛ ashikishaŋ.

english: 2. In a medium bowl, whisk together the flours, granulated sugar, brown sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
ga: 2. Yɛ fioo tsinii ko mli lɛ, tswaa ashikishaŋ, sikli, sikli asarasu, nishãa paada, nishãa soda, kɛ ŋoo.

english: 3. In a large bowl, cream together the butter and egg until light and fluffy. Beat in the egg yolk and almond extract.
ga: 3. Yɛ tsinsii agbo mli lɛ, kreamimɔ bɔta kɛ wuɔ wɔlɔ kɛyata ni ebaa fee flɔfi. Tswa wɔlɔ yok kɛ almond mli nu lɛ.

english: 4. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, alternating with the milk. Mix until just combined.
ga: 4. Fioo fioo kɛ ehe nibii ni egbi lɛ afata nibii ni efɔ lɛ, kɛ mliki lɛ ashi mli. Taa mli ni efutu jogbaŋŋ.

english: 5. Fold in the almond flour until evenly distributed.
ga: 5. Taa almond ashikishaŋ afutu mli ni fɛɛ amɔ.

english: It was a hot summer day in July when I finally turned 16 years old.
ga: Latsaa be mli gbi ni edɔ yɛ Maawɛɛ be ni mi ye afii 16.

english: I had been eagerly anticipating this day for as long as I could remember, and now that it was finally here, I couldn't wait to get started on my road to freedom.
ga: Mi hiɛ kã gbi nɛ nɔ waa kɛ tsɛ, ni agbɛnɛ ni eshɛ lɛ, mi nyɛɛɛ ma mɛɛ ni ma je mi heyeli gbɛ lɛ shishi.

english: The first step was to take the written test.
ga: Kaa ni aŋmaa lɛ ji gbɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nɔ.

english: I studied hard for weeks, and I was confident that I would pass.
ga: Mi kase nii waa otsii pii, ni mi na nɔminaa akɛ ma bɔmɔdɛŋ.

english: On the day of the test, I arrived at the DMV early and took my seat in the waiting room.
ga: Yɛ kaa gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ, mi shɛ DMV lɛ mra ni mi ta shi yɛ mɛhe lɛ.

english: After a few hours, my name was called, and I was ushered into a small room with a computer.
ga: ŋmɛlɛtswaa fioo sɛɛ lɛ, atsɛ mi gbɛi, ni akɛ mi tee tsu bibioo ko no kɔmpiuta yɔɔ mli.

english: The test was surprisingly easy, and I finished it in no time.
ga: Eyɛ naakpɛɛ akɛ kaa lɛ waaa kraa, ni etsɛɛɛ tsɔ ni mi gbe naa.

english: A few days later, I received a letter in the mail informing me that I had passed the written test.
ga: Gbii fioo sɛɛ lɛ, mi nine shɛ wolo ni aŋma yɛ post ɔfis adeka mli ni mikɛɛ mi akɛ miye kaa lɛ nɔ.

english: The next step was to schedule a driving test.
ga: Nɔ ni tsanɔ ji akɛ ato tsɔne kudɔmɔ kaa lɛ.

english: I called the DMV and made an appointment for the following week.
ga: Mi tswa DMV ni mi to be kɛha otsi ni baa lɛ.

english: The day of my driving test arrived, and I was more nervous than I had ever been in my life.
ga: Mi tsɔne kudɔmɔ kaa lɛ shɛ, ni mi tsui fa waa fe mi wala be amli fɛɛ.

english: I drove to the DMV with my mom, who would be accompanying me on the test.
ga: Mi kudɔ tsɔne lɛ kɛ tee DMV lɛ kɛ mi nyɛ, ni baa jie Mr gbɛ yɛ kaa lɛ nɔ.

english: "Heartbreak," sighed the poet, "is the cruelest of afflictions.
ga: "Tsui kumɔɔ mɔ," lalafolɔ lɛ hao, " eji henumɔi yiwaa ni naa wa.

english: It is a pain that pierces the soul and leaves us feeling empty and alone.
ga: Eji piŋmɔ ni tsuɔ susuma lɛ ni eha wɔ fee shwɛm kɛ shoofeemɔ.

english: It is a fire that burns from within, consuming us with its flames.
ga: Eji la ji shãa kɛjɛɔ mli, la ni kpãtãa wɔ hiɛ.

english: It is a storm that tears us apart, leaving us broken and scarred.
ga: Eji ahum ni gbala wɔ teŋ, ni ekumɔɔ wɔ ni ehaa atswã baa.

english: But even in the midst of our heartbreak, there is hope.
ga: Shi yɛ wɔ tsui ni ekumɔ mli po lɛ, hiɛnɔkamɔ yɛ.

english: For even as our hearts are broken, they are also made new.
ga: Ejaakɛ wɔ tsui ekumɔ lɛ, amɛ fee ehee hu.

english: We are given the opportunity to learn from our mistakes and to grow stronger.
ga: Aha wɔ hegbɛ ni wɔ kase nii kɛjɛ wɔ tɔmɔi ni wɔ da waa.

english: We are given the chance to find love again, even if it is different than the love we have lost.
ga: Aha wɔ hegbɛ ni wɔ na suɔmɔ ekoŋŋ, kɛji ekɛ suɔmɔ ni wɔ yɔɔ momo lɛ yɛ srɔto.

english: So let us not despair in our heartbreak.
ga: Hewɔlɛ nyɛ haa wɔ najiaŋ aka je wui yɛ wɔ tsui kũ mli.

english: Let us instead embrace it as a part of life.
ga: Moŋ lɛ nyɛ haa wɔ fuaa lɛ akɛ efata shihilɛ he.

english: Let us learn from it and grow from it.
ga: Nyɛ haa wɔ kase nii kɛjɛ mli ni wɔ daa kɛtsɔ mli.

english: And let us never give up on the hope of finding love again"
ga: Ni nyɛ ka haa wɔ nijiaŋ je wui yɛ hiɛnɔkamɔ ni akɛ taoɔ suɔmɔ ekoŋŋ"

english: Judaism and Kosher Kosher is a set of dietary laws in Judaism.
ga: Yuda jamɔ kɛ Kosher Kosher ji niyenii he mlai henɔi ko yɛ Yuda jamɔ mli.

english: These laws define which foods are permissible to eat and which are not.
ga: Nɛkɛ mlai nɛɛ tsɔɔ niyenii ni aŋmɛ gbɛ ni aye kɛ nɔni aŋmɛ ko gbɛ ni aye.

english: Kosher foods are those that are considered to be fit for consumption according to Jewish law.
ga: Kosher niyenii ji nɔni asusu akɛ ehi ni aye taakɛ Yudafoi amlai lɛ.

english: The laws of kosher are based on the Torah, the first five books of the Hebrew Bible.
ga: Kosher mlai lɛ damɔ Torah lɛ nɔ, klɛŋklɛŋ woji enumɔ ni yɔɔ Hebri Biblia lɛ mli.

english: These laws prohibit the consumption of certain animals, such as pigs and shellfish, as well as the consumption of blood and meat from animals that have not been slaughtered in a specific way.
ga: Nɛkɛ mlai nɛɛ tsĩɔ kooloi komɛi ayeli, tamɔ kplootoo kɛ ŋshɔŋlooi, agbɛnɛ la kɛ koolooi aloo yeli ni agbeee yɛ gbɛ pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ.

english: Kosher foods are also subject to a number of other regulations, such as the separation of dairy and meat products.
ga: Mlai krokomɛi yeɔ Kosher niyenii anɔ, tamɔ nibii ni akɛ mlikii fee kɛ loo nibii amli gbalamɔ.

english: Kosher food is prepared in a way that ensures that it is fit for consumption according to Jewish law.
ga: Ahoɔ Kosher niyenii yɛ gbɛ ni tsɔɔ akɛ ehi kɛha niyeli taakɛ Yuda jamɔ mlai lɛ.

english: The observance of kosher laws is an important part of Jewish religious practice.
ga: Kosher mlai anɔ yeli fata Yuda jamɔŋ nifeemɔi ni he hia waa.

english: For many Jews, eating kosher food is a way to show their devotion to God and to connect with their heritage.
ga: Kɛh Yudafoi babaoo lɛ, kosher niyenii yeli ji gbɛ nɔ ni amɛ tsɔɔ amɛ suɔmɔ kɛha Nyɔŋmɔ ni amɛ kɛ amɛ gboshinii afee tsakpaa.

english: There are a number of reasons why Jews observe kosher laws.
ga: Yiŋtoi babaoo yɛ hewɔ ni Yudafoi yeɔ kosher mlai anɔ.

english: Some of these reasons are based on religious beliefs, while others are based on practical considerations Religious reasons Jews believe that God gave the Torah to Moses at Mount Sinai.
ga: Yiŋtoi nɛɛ ekomɛi damɔ jamɔ mli hemɔkɛyeli, be mli ni ekrokomɛi damɔ susumɔi Jamɔ yiŋtoi Yuda hemɔkɛyeli akɛ Nyɔŋmɔ kɛ Torah ha Mose yɛ Sinai gɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: "I'm telling you, this is going to be the funniest thing ever," said Tom.
ga: "Miŋ kɛɛ bo, enɛ baa fee ŋɔnɔ nii fe fɛɛ," Tom kɛɛ.

english: "Just wait until you see the look on people's faces when they see my new tattoo!"
ga: "Mɛɛ ni okwɛ mɛi ahiɛ kɛji amɛ na nibii ni atɛŋ yɛ mi gbɔmɔtsohe!"

english: "I don't know, Tom," said his friend, Ben.
ga: "Mileee, Tom," Ben, enaanyo lɛ kɛɛ.

english: "A green question mark on your forehead seems like it could be a bit of a risky move."
ga: "Sanebimɔ okadi yɛ ohiɛnaa baafee tamɔ oshara gbɛ nɔ finished."

english: "That's what makes it so funny," said Tom "People are going to be so confused.
ga: "Noni haa ni eyɔɔ ŋɔnɔ," Tom kɛɛ "Ebaa futu mɛi.

english: They'll be asking themselves all sorts of questions, like 'What does it mean?' or 'Why did he do that?'"
ga: Amɛ baa bi amɛ he saji srɔtoi pii, tamɔ 'Mɛni ji shishi?' aloo 'Mɛni hewɔ efee nakai?'"

english: "Or they'll just think you're an idiot," said Ben.
ga: "Aloo amɛ baa jwɛŋ akɛ kwashiai ji bo," Ben kɛɛ.

english: "Nah, they'll get it," said Tom. "Trust me."
ga: "Daabi, amɛ baa ná," Tom kɛɛ. "Kɛ ohiɛ afɔ minɔ."

english: So Tom got the tattoo, and sure enough, people were confused.
ga: Hewɔlɛ Tom atɛŋ yibii ewo egbɔmɔtso he, ni lɛɛlɛŋ hu, efutu mɛi.

english: They asked him all sorts of questions, and he loved every minute of it.
ga: Abi lɛ saji srɔtoi pii, ni esumɔ eminitii fɛɛ.

english: He even started a blog about his tattoo, where he would post pictures and answer questions from his readers.
ga: Ebɔi niŋmaa yɛ intanɛt ɛ nɔ yɛ nibii ni etɛŋ yɛ egbɔmɔtso he, he ni ebaa posti mfoniri ni ebaa ha saji ni enikanelɔi ebibii hetoo.

english: Indira Gandhi was the first and only woman to serve as Prime Minister of India.
ga: Indira Gandhi ji yoo klɛŋklɛŋ ni ye nɔ akɛ maŋsɔɔlɔ yɛ India.

english: She was born in 1917 into a prominent political family, and her father, Jawaharlal Nehru, was the first Prime Minister of India.
ga: Afɔ lɛ yɛ 1917 bei amli awo maŋkwramɔ weku ni hiɛ gbɛi, ni etsɛ, Jawaharial Nehu, ji maŋsɔɔlɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni ye nɔ yɛ India.

english: Indira Gandhi was educated in India and England, and she married Feroze Gandhi in 1942.
ga: Atsɔse Indira Gandhi yɛ India kɛ England, ni ekɛ Feroze Gandhi bote gbala mli yɛ 1942 be amli.

english: They had two sons, Rajiv and Sanjay.
ga: Amɛ fɔ hii enyɔ, Rajiv kɛ Sanjay.

english: Gandhi began her political career in 1955, when she was elected to the Indian Parliament.
ga: Gandhi bɔi emaŋkwramɔ nistumɔ yɛ 1955 bei amli, ni awo lɛ yɛ Indian Ajinafoi agwabɔɔ mli.

english: She served in various ministerial positions in the government of her father, and in 1966 she became Prime Minister after his death.
ga: Esɔ̃mɔ yɛ sɔɔlɔ nitsumɔi srɔtoi yɛ etsɛ maŋ nɔyeli be amli, ni yɛ 1966 beaŋ lɛ ebafee maŋsɔɔlɔ ni etsɛ gbo lɛ.

english: Gandhi was a controversial figure, and her policies were often criticized.
ga: ŋwanejee gbɔmɔ ji Gandhi, ni awieɔ ashiɔ emlai be pii.

english: She was accused of being authoritarian and of suppressing dissent.
ga: A folɔ enaa akɛ moko ni nyɔɔ mɔ nɔ kɛ awrɛhoyeli shitee-kɛ-woo.

english: However, she was also a popular leader, and she is credited with modernizing India and improving the lives of its people.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, lɛ ji hiɛnyiɛlɔ ni ale waa, ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ lɛ ekɛ India ba ŋmɛnɛ be amli ni eha mɛi ashihilɛ hi fe bɔni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Gandhi was assassinated by her Sikh bodyguards in 1984.
ga: Gandhi Sikh hebulɔ gbe lɛ yɛ 1984.

english: She was succeeded by her son, Rajiv Gandhi.
ga: Ebi nuu Rajiv Gandhi, ye esɛɛ.

english: Gandhi's life and career were marked by many challenges, but she never gave up on her dream of a better India.
ga: Gandhi shihilɛ kɛ enitsumɔ kadi nagbaai babaoo, shi enijiaŋ ejeee wui yɛ elamɔ ni ji India kpakpa ko.

english: Global warming is the long-term heating of Earth's climate system observed since the pre-industrial period (between 1850 and 1900) due to human activities, primarily fossil fuel burning, which increases heat-trapping greenhouse gas levels in Earth's atmosphere.
ga: Jeŋ dɔlɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni mii dɔ ni etsɛ ni ana kɛjɛ tsu maa shishijee bei amli (yɛ 1850 kɛ 1900 teŋ) adesa anifeemɔ hewɔ, sũ mli nibii ni ana hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ mli ashãa, ni haa kɔɔyɔŋ nibii ni haa jeŋ dɔɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni ebɔle shipkɔŋ lɛ efaa.

english: The term is frequently used interchangeably with the term climate change, though the latter refers to both human- and naturally produced warming and the effects it has on our planet.
ga: Be pii lɛ akɛ wiemɔ lɛ tsakeɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ wiemɔ lɛ, eyɛ mii akɛ nɔni ji enyɔ nɔ tsɔɔ dɔlɛ ni adesa kɛ jeŋ kɛbaa kɛ enaagbai ni eyɔɔ yɛ wɔ shipkɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Since the pre-industrial period, human activities are estimated to have increased Earth's global average temperature by about 1 degree Celsius (1.8 degrees Fahrenheit), a number that is currently increasing by 0.2 degrees Celsius (0.36 degrees Fahrenheit) per decade.
ga: Kɛjɛ tsu maa shishijee be amli lɛ, ato adesa nifeemɔi akɛ eha Shikpɔŋ fɛɛ dɔlɛ mlijaa etee ŋwɛi tamɔ 1 degree Celsius (1.8 degree Fahrenheit), yibɔ ni amrɔnɛɛ mii ya ŋwɛi 0.2 degree Celsius (0.36 degree Fahrenheit) daa afii nyɔŋma.

english: Most of the current warming trend is extremely likely (greater than 95 percent probability) the result of human activity since the 1950s and is proceeding at an unprecedented rate over decades to millennia.
ga: Dɔlɛ nibii ni yaa nɔ ni naa wa pii yɛ mli akɛ (eda fe mlijaa 95) ejɛ adesa nifeemɔ kɛjɛ 1950 be amli ni ebaba tamɔ anako eko dã yɛ afii nyɔŋmai kɛtee afii akpei ni eho.

english: The largest human influence on climate change has been the emission of greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide, methane and nitrous oxide.
ga: Adesa hewalɛ ni da fe fɛɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ nɔ efee kɔɔyɔŋ nibii ni haa jeŋ dɔɔ lɛ jiemɔ tamɔ carbon dioxide, methane kɛ nitrous oxide.

english: The primary source of these emissions is from burning fossil fuels for electricity, heat and transportation.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ he ni nibii ji ajieɔ awoɔ kɔɔyɔŋ mli lɛ jɔɔ ji sũ mli nibii ni anáa hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ mli ni shãa kɛha srawa hewalɛ, dɔlɛ kɛ gbɛfãa.

english: The portfolio was heavy, and the line was long.
ga: Nitsumɔi wolo lɛ mli tsii, ni lain ɛ kɛɛ.

english: I stood there, aching with pain, and wondered if I would ever get to the front.
ga: Mi damɔ jɛmɛ, he waamɔ kɛ piŋmɔ, kɛ ni jwɛŋ akɛ ani ma shɛ hiɛ po lo.

english: Finally, my turn came, and I presented my portfolio to the woman at the counter.
ga: Naagbee lɛ, eshɛ minɔ, ni mikɛ mi nitsumɔ wolo lɛ ha yoo lɛ yɛ okpɔlɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: She looked at it for a moment, then shook her head.
ga: Ekwɛ bei fioo, ni ewoso eyitso.

english: "I'm sorry," she said. "We can't accept this portfolio. It's not up to our standards."
ga: "Kɛ ke mi," ekɛɛ. "Wɔ nyɛɛɛ wɔ he nitsumɔ wolo nɛɛ. Eshɛɛɛ wɔ shishitoo mlai lɛ he."

english: I felt a wave of despair wash over me.
ga: Mi nu akɛ najiaŋwujee ko ba ha mi he.

english: All my hard work, for nothing.
ga: Mi nitsumɔ ni mitsu ni wa fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, efolo.

english: I took the portfolio back and started to walk away.
ga: Mi he nitsumɔ wolo lɛ ni mi bɔi nyiɛmɔ ketee.

english: "Wait," the woman called "I can see that you've put a lot of effort into this. Why don't you take a seat over there and I'll see what I can do."
ga: "Mɛɛ," yoo lɛ tsɛ̃ "Ma nyɛ ma na akɛ okɛ hewalɛ babaoo wo enɛ mli. Tashi yɛ jɛmɛ ni ma na nɔni manyɛ ma fee."

english: I sat down and waited.
ga: Mi ta shi ni mɛ.

english: A few minutes later, the woman came back.
ga: Bei fioo sɛɛ lɛ, yoo lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: "I've talked to my manager," she said.
ga: "Mi kɛ mi nitsumɔ onukpa ewie," ekɛɛ.

english: "We're willing to make an exception for you. We'll accept your portfolio, but you'll have to pay a processing fee."
ga: "Wɔ baa jie bo pɛ kɛjɛ mli. Wɔ baa he onitsumɔ wolo lɛ, shi obaa wo enifeemɔ he nyɔmɔ."

english: I sighed.
ga: Mi hao.

english: It was a lot of money, but I didn't have any other choice.
ga: Shika babaoo ni, shi mi bɛɛɛ halamɔ koŋkro ko.

english: In the 2006 teen comedy She's the Man, Amanda Bynes plays Viola Hastings, a high school student who disguises herself as a boy in order to play on the boys' soccer team.
ga: Yɛ 2006 oblahiiaŋ ŋmɔnɔ sini She's the Man, Amanda Bynes shwɛ akɛ Viola Hastings, nɔtsamɔ skul nikaselɔ ni etsake ehe efee nuu koni etswa bɔɔlu yɛ hii abɔɔlutswaa kuu mli.

english: The film is full of laugh-out-loud moments, thanks to Bynes's spot-on comedic timing and delivery.
ga: ŋmɔnɔ ehi sini lɛ mli ma, shidaa aha Bynes ŋmɔnɔ sini jiemɔ nifeemɔ ni esusu ni eha pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: She is able to perfectly capture the awkwardness and uncertainty of a teenage boy, while still maintaining her own unique brand of humor.
ga: Enyɔɔ emɔɔ oblanuu hiɛgbele kɛ yeyeeye-feemɔi, be mli ni eyanɔ ekwɛ eŋmɔnɔ ni yɔɔ pɔtɛɛ.

english: The supporting cast is also excellent, with Channing Tatum, Laura Ramsey, and Vinnie Jones all giving memorable performances.
ga: Sini bii ni fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ hu yɛ kpakpa waa, kɛ Channing Tatum, Laura Ramsey, kɛ Vinnie Jones fɛɛ miiha sini nifeemɔi ni hiɛ kpaaa nɔ.

english: The film's director, Andy Fickman, does a great job of balancing the humor with the drama, creating a film that is both funny and heartwarming.
ga: Sini lɛ mli onukpa, Andy Fickman, bɔmɔdɛŋ ni ŋmɛ ŋmɔnɔ kɛ drama pɛpɛɛpɛ, ebɔ sini ni yɛ ŋmɔnɔ ni eha miishɛɛ.

english: She's the Man is a classic teen comedy that is sure to please fans of the genre.
ga: She's the Man ji oblahiiaŋ ŋmɔnɔ sini ko ni ale jogbaŋŋ ni baa ha kwɛlɔi ni sumɔɔ nakai sini lɛ miishɛɛ.

english: Bynes's performance is a standout, and the film is full of laugh-out-loud moments.
ga: Bynes sini jiemɔ lɛ damɔ shi, ni sini lɛ eyi kɛ ŋmɔnɔ babaoo.

english: If you're looking for a fun and entertaining movie to watch, I highly recommend checking out She's the Man.
ga: Kɛji otao sini ni yɔɔ miishɛɛ kɛ hiɛtserɛjiemɔi ni okwɛ, Ma wo ŋaa akɛ okwɛ She's the Man.

english: In addition to being a great comedy, She's the Man is also a film with a strong message about gender equality.
ga: Kefata he akɛ ŋmɔnɔ sini kpakpa ni lɛ, She's the Man hu ji sini ni jieɔ nuu loo yoo bɔyeli sane ni mii wa.

english: Viola's decision to disguise herself as a boy in order to play on the boys' soccer team is a powerful statement about the importance of breaking down gender stereotypes.
ga: Viola yiŋkpɛɛ akɛ ebaa tsake ehe ni etsɔ koni etswa bɔɔlu yɛ hii abɔɔlu tswaa kuu lɛ mli ji hewalɛ sane ko yɛ bɔni ehe hia ni akumɔ nuu kɛ yoo nifeemɔi ni aŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ lɛ.

english: The film shows that girls can be just as good as boys at sports, and that they should not be held back by their gender.
ga: Sini lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ yei baanyɛ abɔmɔdɛŋ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kpɔiaŋgbɔlemɔ tamɔ hii pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni akɛ aka tsì amɛ gbɛ akɛ yei ji amɛ hewɔ.

english: She's the Man is a film that is both funny and inspiring.
ga: She's the Man ji sini ko ni yɛ ŋmɔnɔ kɛ mumɔ tsirɛmɔ.

english: It is a great choice for anyone who is looking for a feel-good movie with a message.
ga: Eji halamɔ kpakpa kɛha mɔfɛɛmɔ ni miitao sini ni haa miishɛɛ ni sane kpakpa yɔɔ mli.

english: Albert Einstein was a German-born theoretical physicist who developed the theory of relativity, one of the two pillars of modern physics (alongside quantum mechanics).
ga: Albert Einstein ji moko ni afɔ lɛ yɛ German ni adebɔɔ mlai ahe nilelɔ ji lɛ ni ekɛ theory of relativity ba, ŋmɛnɛ adebɔɔ mlai ahe nilee enyɔ mli ekome (enyiɛ quantum mechanics masɛi).

english: His work is also known for its influence on the philosophy of science.
ga: Ale enitsumɔ hu kɛya hewalɛ ni eyɔɔ yɛ jeŋ nilee nɔ.

english: Einstein is best known in popular culture for his mass–energy equivalence formula E = mc2 (which has been dubbed "the world's most famous equation").
ga: Ale Einstein waa yɛ kusum ni ale kɛha eakuntaabuu ni ale waa E = mc2 (ni aŋma akɛ " akuntaabuu ni ale fe fɛɛ yɛ je lɛŋ mli").

english: Einstein was born in Ulm, in the Kingdom of Württemberg, German Empire, on 14 March 1879.
ga: Afɔ Einstein yɛ Ulm, yɛ Württemberg maŋtsɛwe, German Empire, yɛ Otsokrikri 14 1879.

english: He showed an early aptitude for mathematics and physics.
ga: Etsɔɔ hesaa kɛha akuntaabuu kɛ adebɔɔ mlai ahe nilee mra.

english: In 1905, at the age of 26, Einstein published four groundbreaking papers that transformed physics.
ga: Yɛ 1905, yɛ afii 26 lɛ, Einstein kala woji ejwɛ ni tsake adebɔɔ mlai ahe nilee.

english: These include his special relativity theory, which introduced the concepts of space and time as a single unified continuum, and his general relativity theory, which proposed that gravity is not a force, but is instead a curvature of spacetime.
ga: Erelativity theory pɔtɛɛ fatahe, ni jie ŋwɛiniiaŋ kɛ be saji kpo akɛ unified kontinuum kome, ni edaa relativity theory, ni kɛ susumɔ ba akɛ nigbalamɔ lɛ jeee adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni, shi moŋ lɛ ŋwɛiniiaŋ be ni.

english: Einstein's work led to a new understanding of the universe, and had a profound impact on the development of modern physics.
ga: Einstein nitsumɔ lɛ kɛ jeŋ lɛ shishinumɔ hei ba, ni ena hewalɛ ni sa kadimɔ yɛ ŋmɛnɛ adebɔɔ mlai ahe nilee ba.

english: He received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1921 for his explanation of the photoelectric effect.
ga: Ena Nobel Prize yɛ adebɔɔ mlai ahe nilee yɛ 1921 kɛha emfoniri kane sɛɛnamɔi ni egbala mli.

english: Einstein was a pacifist and a strong advocate for social justice.
ga: Einstein ji moko ni teɔ shi ewoɔ noko kɛ hewalɛ fãlɔ kɛha jalɛ shihilɛ.

english: Many people wake up before sunrise to start their day's work.
ga: Mɛi pii teɔ shi dani hulu lɛ koni amɛ je amɛ gbi nitsumɔ lɛ shishi.

english: Farmers may rise before dawn to milk their cows or tend to their crops.
ga: Okwaafoi baanyɛ ateshi gbetsɛremɔ koni amɛ ŋaa amɛ tsinai afɔfɔ naa loo akwɛ ŋmɔshinii.

english: Fishermen may go out to sea before the sun comes up.
ga: Wuolɛɛmɛi baanyɛ aya wuo dani hulu lɛ ateshi.

english: People who work in the city may also wake up early to catch the bus or train to work.
ga: Mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ maŋ lɛ mli hu teɔ shi mra koni amɛ kɔ bɔs ɛ loo oketeke kɛya nitsumɔ.

english: Once people are up, they typically eat a simple breakfast of porridge, bread, or tea.
ga: Kɛji gbɔmɛi teshi lɛ, amɛ yeɔ leering niyenii ni ji koko, bloodo, loo tii.

english: Then they get ready for the day.
ga: Kɛkɛ lɛ amɛ bua amɛ he kɛha gbi lɛ.

english: Many people in The Gambia wear traditional clothing, such as long dresses or skirts for women and long pants or shirts for men.
ga: Mɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ Gambia woɔ blema ataadei, tamɔ ataadei kakadaŋŋ aloo skɛɛti kɛha yei kɛ trɔɔs kakadaŋŋ aloo shɛɛt kɛha hii.

english: They may also wear a headscarf or cap.
ga: Amɛ baanyɛ amɛ wo duku loo fai hu.

english: After breakfast, people go about their daily activities.
ga: Yɛ leebi niyenii sɛɛ lɛ, mɛi feɔ amɛ daa gbi nifeemɔi.

english: Children go to school, while adults go to work.
ga: Gbekɛbii yaa skul, be mli ni onukapai yaa nitsumɔ.

english: Many people in The Gambia work in agriculture, fishing, or tourism.
ga: Mɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ Gambia tsuɔ okwaayeli, wuo yaa, loo shisharamɔ nitsumɔ.

english: Others work in government, business, or education.
ga: Ekomɛi tsuɔ nii yɛ maŋ nɔyeli, nihɔɔmɔ nitsumɔ, loo tsɔsemɔ.

english: In the afternoon, people may take a break from work to relax or socialize.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, mɛi baanyɛ amɛ na hejɔɔmɔ kɛjɛ nitsumɔ ni amɛ jɔɔ amɛ he loo henaabuamɔ.

english: They may go for a walk, visit friends and family, or play games.
ga: Amɛ baa ya nyiɛmɔ, sara nanemɛi kɛ wekumɛi, loo shwɛmɔi.

english: In the evening, people often eat dinner with their families.
ga: Yɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ, mɛi fɔɔ gbɛkɛ nii yeli kɛ amɛ wekumɛi.

english: Dinner is typically a simple meal of rice, vegetables, and meat or fish.
ga: Gbɛkɛ niyenii ji omɔ, aduawai, kɛ kooloo loo aloo ŋshɔ mli loo.

english: The gadgets and utensils of the kitchen are a language, a means of communication between cook and food.
ga: Kpatashi tsɔji kɛ tsinsii ji wiemɔ, gbɛnɔ ni nihoolɔ kɛ niyenii wieɔ.

english: The whisk, the tongs, the ladle, the spatula - each has its own meaning, its own purpose.
ga: Wiski, nibɛɛnii, awale ato, awale - fɛɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ shishi numɔ, amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ yoŋtoi.

english: To use them well is to understand the language of cooking, to season the dish with the flavors of experience and skill.
ga: Koni okɛ baa tsu ni ojogbaŋŋ lɛ Esa ni onu nihoomɔ wiemɔ lɛ shishi, ni owo niyenii lɛ he kɛ niiashikpamɔ kɛ he saa ni haa ni eŋɔɔ.

english: The whisk is a whisk, the tongs are tongs, and the ladle is a ladle.
ga: Wiski ɛ wiski ni, nibɛɛnii ji nibɛɛnii, ni awale ato lɛ awale ato ni.

english: But in the hands of a skilled cook, they become something more: they become extensions of the cook's own body, tools that allow him or her to express creativity and passion.
ga: Shi yɛ nihoolɔ ni he esa yɛ nihoomɔ mli nine lɛ, efeɔ noko pii: amɛ tsɔɔ nihoolɔ gbɔmɔtso fã diɛŋtsɛ, nibii ni haa lɛ gbɛ ni ejie edebɔɔ kɛ suɔmɔ.

english: With a whisk, the cook can whip up a frothy batter or emulsify a delicate sauce.
ga: Kɛ wiski ɛ, nihoolɔ baanyɛ ni etswa bɔta ni efee frufru loo ehoo flɔ ni he yɔɔ sɛɛ namɔ.

english: With tongs, he or she can flip a steak or turn a roast.
ga: Kɛ nibɛɛnii lɛ, ebaanyɔ etsɔ tsina loo aloo estɔ nɔni ashã.

english: With a ladle, he or she can ladle out a steaming bowl of soup or sauce.
ga: Kɛ awale ato lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsɔ wonu loo flɔ ni mii edɔ awo tsinsii mli.

english: The gadgets and utensils of the kitchen are more than just tools.
ga: Kpataashi tsɔji kɛ tsinsii fe nihoomɔ nibii kɛkɛ.

english: They are a means of expression, a way to create something beautiful and delicious.
ga: Amɛ ji gbɛnɔ ni jieɔ he na, gbɛ nɔ ni abɔɔ noko ni yɔɔ fɛo ni ŋɔɔ.

english: A seed is a small, dormant plant embryo that is capable of developing into a new plant under the right conditions.
ga: Dumɔ wu ji tso kukulii bibioo ko, ni yɔɔ diŋŋ ni baanyɛ ekwɛ̃ ni etsɔ tso ehe yɛ shihilɛ kpakpa shishi.

english: When a seed sprouts, it begins to grow roots and shoots.
ga: Kɛji dumɔ wu ko kwɛ̃ lɛ, shishifãi kɛ tsɛ̃rɛ̃i jeɔ shishi edaa.

english: The roots anchor the plant in the soil and absorb water and nutrients from the ground.
ga: Shishifãi lɛ fiɔ tso lɛ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ sũ lɛ mli ni eji ejie nu kɛ sũ mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ.

english: The shoots grow upwards towards the sun, and the leaves begin to photosynthesize, producing food for the plant.
ga: Etsɛ̃rɛ̃ lɛ daa kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ ya hulu lɛ, ni baa lɛ jeɔ fotosintɛsis shishi, niyenii feemɔ kɛha tso lɛ.

english: As the plant grows, it develops a stem, leaves, flowers, and fruit.
ga: Be ni tso lɛ mii da lɛ, ejeɔ teŋtso, baai, fɔfɔi, kɛ aduawai.

english: The flowers produce seeds, which are dispersed by wind, water, or animals.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ dumɔ wui, ni kɔɔyɔŋ, nu, loo kooloi gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: When a seed lands in a suitable location, it can germinate and begin the process of growth all over again.
ga: Kɛji dumɔ wui ya gbee he ko ni hi waa lɛ, ebaanyɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ni eje dalɛ nifeemɔ lɛ shishi ekoŋŋ.

english: The process of seed germination is a marvel of nature.
ga: Dumɔ wu akwɛ̃mɔ ji naakpɛɛ adebɔɔ nii.

english: It is a testament to the power of life and the resilience of the natural world.
ga: Eji wala kpaŋmɔ hewalɛ kɛha wala kɛ jeŋ adebɔɔ shifimɔ.

english: When a seed sprouts, it is a sign of hope and new beginnings.
ga: Kɛji dumɔ wu kwɛ̃ lɛ, eji hiɛnɔkamɔ kɛ shishijee ehei okadi.

english: You have been warned.
ga: Abɔ bo kɔkɔ.

english: You have been given a clear and concise warning.
ga: Abɔ bo kɔkɔ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kɛ kuku.

english: You have been told that if you continue to engage in this behavior, you will be banned.
ga: Akɛɛ bo akɛ kɛji osha nɔ ojie subaŋ olo ɛ, abaa gu bo.

english: You have now had two chances to correct your behavior, and you have failed to do so.
ga: Agbɛnɛ ona hegbɛi enyɔ ni osaa osubaŋ, ni efeee.

english: As a result, you will now be banned from this forum.
ga: Nɔ ni ejɛ mli eba ji akɛ, aguuu bo kɛjɛ forɔm lɛ nɔ.

english: This ban is permanent, and you will not be allowed to create a new account or participate in this forum in any way.
ga: Gu nɛɛ baya naanɔ, ni aŋmɛɛɛ bo gbɛ ni obɔ akaunt ehe loo ofata forɔm nɛɛ he yɛ gbɛ fɛɛ ko nɔ.

english: We hope that this ban will serve as a warning to others who may be tempted to engage in similar behavior.
ga: Wɔ hiɛnɔkamɔ ji akɛ gu nɛɛ baa damɔ shi akɛ kɔkɔ kɛha mɛi krokomɛi ni aatao ni ajie subaŋ ni tamɔ nɛkɛ.

english: We will not tolerate this type of behavior on our forum, and we will take action to protect our community from it.
ga: We heee subaŋ nɛɛ wɔ wooo mli yɛ wɔ forɔm ɛ nɔ, ni wɔ kɔ gbejianɔtoo ni wɔ kɛ buu wɔ akutsoŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ lɛ.

english: If you have any questions about this ban, please do not hesitate to contact us.
ga: Kɛji oyɛ sanebimɔ yɛ gu nɛɛ he lɛ, ofainɛ kaashashaoo ni otswa wɔ.

english: Thank you for your cooperation.
ga: Oyiwaladɔŋŋ akɛ okɛ wɔ fee ekome.

english: "What the hell are you doing, you idiot?!"
ga: "Mɛni ofeɔ, bo kwasiai?!"

english: "Excuse me?"
ga: "Miikpào fai?"

english: "You cut me off! You almost made me crash!"
ga: "Ofo me yɛ ohe afɔ! Eshwɛ fioo kulɛ oha mi shi nii!"

english: "I'm sorry, I didn't mean to. I was just trying to get around that slow-moving truck."
ga: "Edɔ mi, mi jeee gbɛ. Mii fee ni ma tsɔ lɔle agbo ni mii ya blog lɛ he kɛkɛ."

english: "Well, you could have at least used your turn signal!"
ga: "Ojogbaŋŋ, obaanyɛ ni shi kulɛ osũ okadi kane ni tsɔɔ akɛ odɔ lɛ!"

english: "I did use my turn signal!"
ga: "Mi sũ mi kadii kane ni tsɔɔ akɛ miidɔ lɛ!"

english: "No, you didn't! You just pulled right out in front of me!"
ga: "Daabi, osũuu! Otsi kɛ damɔ mi hiɛ oya nɔɔ!"

english: "I'm telling you, I used my turn signal!"
ga: "Mii kɛɛ bo, mi sũ mi dɔɔ okadii kane lɛ!"

english: "Whatever. You're still a terrible driver."
ga: "Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ. Tsɔnekudɔlɔ gbonyo ji bo olo."

english: "And you're a jerk!"
ga: "Ni ofeee jogbaŋŋ kwraa!"

english: "At least I know how to drive!"
ga: "Kɛ hoo lɛ mi le bɔni akudɔɔ tsɔne!"

english: "Oh, yeah? Well, I'm a better writer than you are!"
ga: "Nakai? Ojogbaŋŋ, mi hu ŋmalɔ kpakpa ji mi fe bo!"

english: "That's debatable."
ga: "Abaanyɛ aje he ŋwane."

english: "It's not debatable! I'm Ernest Hemingway!"
ga: "Anyɛɛɛ he ŋwane aje! Ernest Hemingway ji mi!"

english: "Who?"
ga: "Namɔ?"

english: "Ernest Hemingway! The greatest writer of all time!"
ga: "Ernest Hemingway! Niŋmalɔ wulu ni fe fɛɛ!"

english: "Never heard of him."
ga: "Mi nu ko ehe."

english: "Well, you've heard of me now!"
ga: "Ojogbaŋŋ, onu mihe agbɛnɛ!"

english: "Yeah, I heard of you."
ga: "Hɛɛ, mi nu ohe."

english: Grace: Can you tell me a little bit about its history?
ga: Grace: Obaanyɛ okɛɛ mi noko fioo yɛ eblema sane lo?

english: Teacher: Of course. Tea originated in China, where it has been cultivated for over 5,000 years.
ga: Tsɔɔlɔ: Anɔkwale. Tii je shishi kɛjɛ China, he ni adu fe afii 5,000 kɛ sɛɛ.

english: The first written record of tea dates back to the 3rd century BC, when it was mentioned in a Chinese medical text.
ga: Wolo klɛŋklɛŋ ni aŋma yɛ tii he yaa sɛɛ yɛ tee ohai 3rd BC, be ni atsɛ yɛ Chinese tsofahe kaa.

english: Tea was originally used as a medicinal herb, but it quickly became a popular drink among Chinese people of all social classes.
ga: Shishijee lɛ akɛ tii tsuɔ nii akɛ baa tsofa, shi oya ni ebatsɔ nii ni anuɔ ni ale yɛ Chinese bii ateŋ.

english: Grace: What about outside of China? When did tea start to spread to other parts of the world?
ga: Grace: Ni China kponɔ hu? Mɛɛ be tii je shwamɔ kɛtee jeŋ lɛ fãi?

english: Teacher: Tea was first introduced to Europe in the 16th century by Portuguese traders.
ga: Tsɔɔlɔ: Tii shishi kwraa yɛ Europe yɛ ohai 16th be amli kɛtsɔ Portuguese nihɔɔlɔi anɔ.

english: It quickly became popular among European elites, and by the 18th century, tea had become a staple of British culture.
ga: Eba tsɔ nɔ ni ale oha yɛ Europe shikatsɛmɛi ateŋ, ni ohai 18th be lɛ, tii bafee noko ni fata British kusum he.

english: In the 19th century, tea was also introduced to North America, where it became a popular drink among both colonists and Native Americans.
ga: Yɛ ohai 19th be amli lɛ, tii shishi hu kwraa yɛ Northern America, he ni ebatsɔ nii ni anuɔ ni ale waa yɛ Ameeican shihelɔi kɛ maŋbii lɛ ateŋ.

english: Grace: That's really interesting.I never knew that tea had such a long history.
ga: Grace: Eyɛ naakpɛɛ waa. Mi leee da akɛ tii yɛ yinɔsane kakadaŋŋ nɛkɛ.

english: Teacher: It's a fascinating story, and it's one that's still being written today.
ga: Tsɔɔlɔ: Eji naakpɛɛ sane, ni eji nɔ ni aŋma olo ŋmɛnɛ.

english: During World War II, the Allies and Axis powers used a variety of aircraft to achieve air superiority.
ga: Yɛ World War II, Allies kɛ Axis hewalɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ lɛlɛ henɔi tsu nii koni amɛ ye nɔ.

english: One of the most important factors in determining the outcome of a battle was the accuracy of the aircraft's bombing.
ga: Nibii ni hia kome fe fɛɛ ni tsɔɔ nɔ ni baaba yɛ ta ko mli ji bɔ ni kɔɔyɔŋ lɛlɛ fɔɔ okpɛlɛmii ojogbaŋŋ.

english: The height at which an aircraft could fly was also a critical factor, as it determined how far it could travel and how much weight it could carry.
ga: Bɔ ni kɔɔyɔŋ lɛlɛ lɛ yaa ŋwɛi hu fata nibii ni he hia lɛ he, ni etsɔɔ bɔni ebaanyɛ eya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛha kɛ miitsiimɔ enyiɛ ebaanyɛ ni ewo.

english: The United States developed a number of high-altitude bombers during the war, including the B-17 Flying Fortress and the B-29 Superfortress.
ga: United States fee okpɛlɛmii ni yaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ ayibɔ yɛ ta be amli, B-17 Flying Fortress kɛ B-29 Superfortress fata he.

english: These aircraft were able to fly at altitudes of over 30,000 feet, which made them difficult for enemy fighters to intercept.
ga: Nɛkɛ kɔɔyɔŋ lɛlɛ nɛɛ baanyɛ ni eya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ fe naji 30,000, ni haa ewa aha nɔmɔ henyɛlɔi lɛ.

english: They also carried a large payload of bombs, which could be used to attack targets deep behind enemy lines.
ga: Amɛ woɔ okpɛlɛmii agboi babaoo, ni abaanyɛ akɛ tutua amɛ yɛ henyɛlɔi lain lɛ sɛɛ tɔɔ.

english: The German Luftwaffe also developed a number of high-altitude bombers, including the Heinkel He 177 Greif and the Messerschmitt Me 264 Amerika Bomber.
ga: German Luftwaffe lɛ hu ma okpɛlɛmii ni yaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ ayibɔ, Henkel He 177 Greif kɛ Messerschmitt Me 264 Amerika Bomber hu fata he.

english: These aircraft were not as successful as their American counterparts, however, due to a number of technical problems.
ga: Nɛkɛ kɔɔyɔŋ lɛlɛ lɛ yeee omanye tamɔ e America henɔi lɛ, kɛlɛ, naagbai komɛi ahewɔ.

english: I know what you did yesterday.
ga: Mi le nɔni ofee nyɛ.

english: You posted a picture of yourself wearing that green rag on social media.
ga: Okɛ ohe mfoniri ni owo nakai tako eŋɔli ko fɔ intanɛt ɛ nɔ.

english: I know you thought it was funny, but it wasn’t.
ga: Mi le akɛ ojwɛŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔnɔ, shi ebɛɛɛ ŋmɔnɔ.

english: It was disrespectful to your mother, and it hurt her feelings.
ga: Etsɔɔɔ bulɛ kɛha onyɛ, ni eye ehenumɔi awui.

english: I’m not asking you to apologize because I’m mad at you.
ga: Mii bi bo ni okpa fai ejaakɛ mi mli efu bi.

english: I’m asking you to apologize because it’s the right thing to do.
ga: Mii bi bo akɛ okpa fai ejaakɛ no ji nii kpakpa ni afeɔ.

english: Your mother loves you, and she deserves your respect.
ga: Onyɛ sumɔɔ bo, ni esa obulɛ.

english: Please call her today and tell her you’re sorry.
ga: Ofainɛ tswaa lɛ ŋmɛnɛ ni okɛɛ lɛ akɛ edɔ bo.

english: Tell her that you didn’t mean to hurt her feelings, and that you promise to never wear that green rag again.
ga: Kɛɛmɔ lɛ akɛ ojeee gbɛ akɛ obaa ye ehenumɔ awui, ni owo lɛ shi akɛ owooo nakai tako eŋɔli lɛ dɔŋŋ.

english: I know you’re a good person, and I know you love your mother.
ga: Mi le akɛ gbɔmɔ kpakpa ji bo, ni mi le akɛ osumɔɔ onyɛ.

english: So please, do the right thing and apologize.
ga: Hewɔ ofainɛ, feemɔ nɔ ni hi ni okpa fai.

english: After you apologize to your mother, I want you to burn that green rag.
ga: Kɛji okpa onyɛ fai sɛɛ lɛ, mi tao ni oshã nakai tako eŋɔli lɛ.

english: It’s a symbol of your disrespect, and it needs to be gone.
ga: Eji okadii akɛ obuuu mɔ, ni ehe hia akɛ etee.

english: I know it might be hard to let go of that rag, but it’s important.
ga: Mi le akɛ ewa ni obaa ŋmɛɛ nakai tako lɛ he, shi ehe hia.

english: It’s a symbol of your past, and it’s time to move on.
ga: Eji obei ko ni eho okadii, ni be eshɛɛ ni ootsa nɔ.

english: You’re a new person now.
ga: Gbɔmɔ ehei ji bo agbɛnɛ.

english: You’re a better person.
ga: Gbɔmɔ kpakpa ji bo.

english: And you don’t need that rag to define you anymore.
ga: Ni kaaa ha ni nakai tako lɛ tsɔɔ bo mɔni ji bo.

english: So please, burn it.
ga: Hewɔ ofainɛ, shã lɛ.

english: Burn it and let it go.
ga: Shãa ni oŋmɛɛ he.

english: And then go hug your mother and tell her you love her.
ga: Ni oya fua onyɛ ni okɛɛ lɛ akɛ osumɔ lɛ.

english: She loves you too.
ga: Esumɔɔ bo hu.

english: A car was driving too fast and lost control, swerving into the other lane and hitting a car head-on.
ga: Kar ko mii kudɔ oya ni enyɛɛɛ kudɔmɔ dɔŋŋ, ebote gbɛ kokro lɛ mli ni ekɛ eyitso shì kar ko yitso.

english: The driver of the first car was killed instantly, and the driver of the second car was seriously injured.
ga: Tsɔnekudɔlɔ ni yɔɔ kar klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ mli lɛ gbo amrɔ nɔŋŋ, ni tsɔnekudɔlɔ ni yɔɔ kar ni ji enyɔ nɔ pila waa diɛŋtsɛ.

english: My friend Joseph called me to talk about it.
ga: Mi naanyo Joseph tsɛ mi koni ekɛ mi awie.

english: "It's so sad," he said. "I can't imagine how the families of the victims are coping."
ga: "Eji awrɛho sane waa," ekɛɛ. "Mi nyɛɛɛ ma jwɛŋ bɔni mɔni egbo lɛ wekumɛi kɛ sane lɛ kpeeɔ aha."

english: "Me neither," I responded. "It's a reminder that we need to be careful when we're driving.
ga: "Mi hi nakai," Mi jie naa. "Eji kaimɔ akɛ esa ni wɔ kwɛ ojogbaŋŋ kɛji wɔŋ kudɔ kar.

english: Even a small mistake can have devastating consequences."
ga: Tɔmɔ bibioo ko po baanyɛ ni ekɛ sɛɛnamɔ naagbai aba."

english: "I agree," replied Jo. "We all need to follow the rules of the road and drive defensively."
ga: "Mikpɛlɛ nɔ," Jo jie naa. "Esa ni wɔ nyiɛ gbɛ he gbɛjianɔtoi sɛɛ ni wɔ kudɔ ojogbaŋŋ."

english: "Absolutely," I quickly added. "And we need to be aware of the dangers of distracted driving. Things like texting and talking on the phone can take our attention away from the road and lead to accidents."
ga: "Eka shi faŋŋ," Mi kɛ fata he oya. "Ni esa akɛ wɔ le nagbaai ni nyiɛ kudɔmɔ ni ajie hiɛ yɛ nɔ. Nibii tamɔ tɛlɛfon nɔ nyɛmɔmɔ kɛ enɔ wiemɔ baanyɛ ejie ojwɛmɔ kɛjɛ gbɛ nɔ ni ekɛ oshara baa ba."

english: "I know," said Jo sheepishly. "I'm guilty of it myself sometimes."
ga: "Mi le," Jo kɛɛ gbeyeishemɔ mli. "Mi ye he efɔ bei komɛi mi diɛŋtsɛ."

english: In the small town of Malgudi, there was a corrupt police inspector named Ramasamy.
ga: Yɛ Malgudi maŋ bibioo lɛ, ayɛ polisifonyo onukpa ko ni bɛɛɛ jeŋba ni atsɛɔ lɛ Ramasamy.

english: He would often take bribes from the people he arrested, and he would also use his power to harass and intimidate people.
ga: Bei pii lɛ ebaa he shika kɛjɛ mɛi ni emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ adeŋ, ni ekɛ e hewalɛ hu baa hao ni ewoɔ mɛi ahe gbeyee.

english: One day, Ramasamy arrested a young man named Krishnan for a crime he did not commit.
ga: Gbi ko lɛ, Ramasamy mɔ oblanuu ko ji atsɛɔ lɛ Krishnan kɛha awui ko ni efeee.

english: Krishnan was innocent, but Ramasamy refused to listen to him.
ga: Jeee Krishnan ni fe, shi Ramasamy booo lɛ toi.

english: He demanded a bribe from Krishnan, and when Krishnan refused to pay, Ramasamy threw him in jail.
ga: Ebi shika kɛjɛ Krishnan deŋ, kɛ ni Krishnan kɛhaaa lɛ, Ramasamy wo lɛ tsuŋ mli.

english: Krishnan's father, a poor farmer, was desperate to get his son out of jail.
ga: Krishnan tsɛ, okwaafonyo ohiafo ko, he mii sha lɛ koni ejie ebi nuu lɛ kɛjɛ tsuŋ ni awo lɛ.

english: He went to see Ramasamy and begged him to release Krishnan, but Ramasamy refused.
ga: Eya na Ramasamy ni ekpa lɛ fai koji eŋmɛɛ Krishnan he, shi Ramasamy ekpɛnɛɛɛ nɔ.

english: The farmer then went to the local temple and prayed to God for help.
ga: Kɛkɛ lɛ okwaafonyo lɛ tee maŋ lɛ sɔlemɔhe ni esɔle kɛya nyɔŋmɔ koni ewa lɛ.

english: The next day, the farmer was walking home from the temple when he saw a large snake crossing the road.
ga: Enɔ jetsɛremɔ lɛ, okwaafonyo lɛ mii nyiɛ kɛ ya shia kɛjɛ sɔlemɔhe ni ena onufu agbo ko ni mii fo gbɛ mli.

english: The farmer was afraid of snakes, but he knew that he had to do something to help his son.
ga: Okwaafonyo lɛ mii she onufu lɛ gbeyei, shi ele akɛ esa ni efee noko kɛ wa ebi lɛ.

english: He picked up the snake and carried it to the police station.
ga: Ekɔ onufu lɛ ni ewo lɛ kɛ tee polisifoi anitsumɔ he.

english: When Ramasamy saw the snake, he was terrified.
ga: Ni Ramasamy na onufu lɛ, eshe gbeyei.

english: Dentist: Let me take a look. [Examines the patient's teeth.] Hmm, it looks like you have a cavity.
ga: Nyanyɔŋ he tsofatsɛ: Ha ni ma kwɛ. [Kwɛ helatsɛ nyanyɔŋ.] Hmm, etamɔ oyɛ bu yɛ onyanyɔŋ mli.

english: I'm going to need to drill out the decay and fill the hole.
ga: Ma gbulɔ fɔlɔ kɛ jie nɔ ni egbo lɛ ni ma tsiŋ bu lɛ naa.

english: Patient: Will it hurt?
ga: Tsofatsɛ: ebaa waa mi he?

english: Dentist: It might be a little uncomfortable, but I'll do my best to make it as painless as possible.
ga: Nyanyɔŋ he tsofatsɛ: ebaa ni ohe ajɔɔɔ bo fioo, shi ma bɔmɔdɛŋ ni ma fee ni eka wa ohe tsɔ.

english: Dentist: (gives the patient a local anesthetic) Okay, this will numb the area so you won't feel anything.
ga: Nyanyɔŋ he tsofatsɛ: (ha helatsɛ lɛ tsofa) Yoo, enɛ baa ha jɛmɛ ajɔ hewɔ onuuu noko he.

english: Dentist: (drills out the decay and fills the hole) All done!
ga: Nyanyɔŋ he tsofatsɛ: (gbulɔ nɔni egbo lɛ kpo ni etsiŋ bu lɛ naa) Agbe naa!

english: Patient: Thank you, doctor. That wasn't so bad.
ga: Helatsɛ: Oyiwaladɔŋŋ, dɔkita. Ewaaa mi he tsɔ.

english: Dentist: You're welcome. Just be sure to brush and floss regularly to prevent future cavities.
ga: Nyanyɔŋ he tsofatsɛ: Shidaa bɛ. Kwɛmɔ ni osha onyanyɔŋ ni ojie mii daa koni oka na ekoŋŋ.

english: Patient: I will Dentist: (hands the patient a list of instructions) Here are some instructions on how to care for your new filling.
ga: Helatsɛ: Ma fee Nyanyɔŋ he tsofatsɛ: (ha helatsɛ gbejianɔtoi ko) Na nitsumɔi komɛi yɛ bɔ ni obaanyɛ ni okwɛ obu ni atsiŋ naa lɛ.

english: Patient: Thank you.
ga: Helatsɛ: Oyiwaladɔŋŋ.

english: Dear [Name], I hope this letter finds you well.
ga: Naanyo kpakpa [Gbɛi], Mi hiɛkanɔ akɛ niŋmaa wolo nɛɛ baa shɛ onɔ ojogbaŋŋ.

english: I'm writing to you from our family farm, where the harvest has been going well this year.
ga: Mi ŋma bo kɛjɛ wɔ weku ŋmɔ lɛ mli, heni kpamɔ lɛ mli ya nɔ ojogbaŋŋ afi nɛɛ.

english: We're expecting a bumper crop of sugarcane, which is used to make rum.
ga: Wɔ hiɛ kã shɛ̃ ŋmɔshi nii pii, ni akɛ feɔ rum.

english: Rum is a distilled spirit made from sugarcane molasses or sugarcane juice.
ga: Rum ji dãa ni spiriti ni asɔɔ nɔ ni anaa kɛjɛɔ shɛ̃ molasses loo shɛ̃ nu.

english: It's typically aged in wooden barrels, which gives it its characteristic flavor.
ga: Aha etsɛɔ yɛ googa ni akɛ tso fee, ni haa enaa ŋɔɔ waa.

english: Rum can be enjoyed neat, on the rocks, or mixed in cocktails.
ga: Abaanyɛ ni anu rum folo, akɛ ais awo mli, loo akɛ futu daa krokomɛi.

english: There are many different types of rum, each with its own unique flavor profile.
ga: Ayɛ rum henɔi srɔtoi, eko fɛɛ eko kɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ enuŋtɛ naa pɔtɛɛ.

english: Some of the most popular types of rum include light rum, dark rum, and spiced rum.
ga: Rum henɔi komɛi ni ale waa rum ni yɛɔ fioo, rum ni diŋɔ, kɛ rum ni awo mli spais fata he.

english: Light rum is typically made from molasses and has a light, sweet flavor.
ga: Rum ni yɛŋɔ ji nɔni akɛ molasses fee ni emii etsiii, enaa ŋɔɔ.

english: Dark rum is made from sugarcane juice and has a richer, more complex flavor.
ga: Rum ni diŋɔ ji nɔni akɛ shɛ̃ nu fee ni emii ti, ni enaa wa.

english: Spiced rum is made with added spices, such as cinnamon, nutmeg, and cloves.
ga: Awo spais rum mli tsofa ni jieɔ ŋma, tamɔ sinamon, kɛ klovs.

english: Rum is a versatile spirit that can be used in a variety of cocktails.
ga: Rum ji dãa henɔ ni abaanyɛ akɛ hoo niyenii srɔtoi babaoo.

english: Some classic rum cocktails include the daiquiri, the mojito, and the pina colada.
ga: Rum dãa futumɔ komɛi lɛ daiquiri, monitor, kɛ pina colada fata he.

english: Rum can also be used in more creative cocktails, such as the Hemingway Daiquiri or the Painkiller.
ga: Abaanyɛ ni akɛ rum afee dãa futumɔi pii, tamɔ Hemingway Daiquiri loo Painkiller.

english: We must reject the forces of division and hate.
ga: Esa ni wɔ kpoo mligbalamɔ kɛ hetsɛ̃ yiwalɛ.

english: We must break the chains of poverty and ignorance.
ga: Esa ni wɔ ye wɔ he kɛjɛ ohia kɛ nilee ni bɛ.

english: And we must bind ourselves together in a common purpose: to build a better future for Nigeria.
ga: Ni esa ni wɔ tsa kɛ ekomefeemɔ yɛ yiŋtoo kome mli: koni wɔ ma wɔ sɛɛ kpakpa aha Nigeria.

english: The destiny of Nigeria is not to be a land of division and conflict.
ga: Jeee Nigeria shɛɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni mli eja kɛ tawuu.

english: It is to be a land of unity and progress.
ga: Eji shikpɔŋ ni sa ekomefeemɔ kɛ hiɛ yaa.

english: It is to be a land where everyone has a chance to succeed, regardless of their background or circumstances.
ga: Esani efee shikpɔŋ ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ aha hegbɛ ni eye omanye, ekɔɔ he ni amɛ jɛ loo amɛ shihilɛ.

english: But we cannot achieve this future without working together.
ga: Shi wɔ nine nyɛɛɛ ashɛ nɛkɛ wɔsɛɛ kɛji wɔ kɛ ekomefeemɔ tsuuu nii.

english: We must reject the forces that seek to divide us and come together as one people.
ga: Esa ni wɔ kpoo yiwalɛ ni miitao agbala wɔ mii ni wɔ tsa akɛ mɛi kome.

english: We must break the chains of poverty and ignorance that hold us back.
ga: Esa ni wɔ ye ohia kɛ nilee ni bɛ ni mii tao agbala wɔ sɛɛ he nɔ.

english: The future of Nigeria is in our hands.
ga: Nigeria wɔsɛɛ yɛ wɔ deŋ.

english: Let us not squander it.
ga: Nyɛ ka haa wɔ fiteɔ lɛ.

english: Let us reject, break and bind the forces that seek to control and pervert our destiny.
ga: Nyɛ haa wɔ kpoo, kumɔ ni wɔ fimɔ yiwalɛ ni mii tao akudɔ ni eye wɔ shɛɛ nɔ.

english: Let us come together as one people and build a better future for all.
ga: Nyɛ haa wɔ tsaa are mɛi kome ni wɔ ma wɔsɛɛ kpakpa aha wɔ fɛɛ.

english: "Complete your Amazon shopping experience with our new and improved ad service!" the ad read.
ga: "Gbee o Amazon nihemɔi niiashikpamɔ lɛ naa kɛ wɔ sɛɛvis adafitwsaa ehei ni atsake lɛ!" adafitwsaa lɛ kaneɔ.

english: "With our service, you'll never have to worry about missing out on a great deal again.
ga: "Kɛ wɔ sɛɛvis ɛ, esaaa ni ohao akɛ onine shɛɛɛ nibii kpakpa nɔ dɔŋŋ.

english: Just sit back and relax, and we'll take care of the rest.
ga: Ta shi ni ojɔɔ ohe kɛkɛ, ni wɔ baa fee fã ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Our service is completely free to use, and it's easy to get started.
ga: Wɔ sɛɛvis ɛ wɔheee noko kɛji ootao ni okɛ tsu nii, ni eji nɔni eshishije ka shi faŋŋ.

english: Just sign up for an account and start adding products to your cart.
ga: Kɛ ogbɛi afata he koni ona akaunt ni obɔi nibii kɛ onihemɔ lɔle lɛ mii woo.

english: When you're ready to check out, our service will automatically find the best deals for you and apply them to your order.
ga: Kɛji offers klado ni oshì lɛ, wɔ sɛɛvis ɛ baa tao nibii kpakpa eha bo lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni ekɛ baa ha nibii ni ohe lɛ.

english: So what are you waiting for?
ga: Hewɔ lɛ mɛni omɛɛɔ?

english: Sign up for our service today and start saving money on all your Amazon purchases!"
ga: Kɛ ogbɛi afata wɔ sɛɛvis ɛ he ŋmɛmɛ ni oje shika kɛ too shishi yɛ onibii fɛɛ ni obaa he yɛ Amazon nɔ!"

english: As the customer clicked on the ad, they were whisked away to a new website.
ga: Be ni nihelɔ lɛ nyɛ adafitwsaa lɛ nɔ lɛ, akɛ amɛ tee wɛbsait koŋkro nɔ.

english: The website was full of ads for all sorts of products, all of which were supposedly on sale.
ga: Wɛbsait lɛ eyi kɛ adafitwsaai kɛya nibii babaoo, fɛɛ asumaa atse amɛ nɔ.

english: The customer was tempted to buy a few things, but they hesitated.
ga: Ekaa nihelɔ lɛ koni ehe nibii fioo, shi amɛ shashao shi.

english: They had heard stories about people getting scammed by online ads, and they didn't want to be one of them.
ga: Amɛ nu saji akɛ intanɛt adafitwsaa mii tswa mɛi ojo, ni amɛ sumɔɔɔ ni akɛ fee amɛ.

english: The customer decided to do some research on the company that was running the ad.
ga: Nihelɔ lɛ kpɛ eyiŋ akɛ ebaa fee niiamlitaomɔ komɛi yɛ nitsumɔ ni mii tswa adafi lɛ he.

english: They found a few negative reviews, but most of the reviews were positive.
ga: Amɛ na wiemɔi ni ehiii, shi ekomɛi pii hi.

english: The black dog came to me in the night.
ga: Gbee ediŋŋ lɛ ba miŋɔɔ gbɛkɛ mli.

english: It had cold, wet fur and its eyes were like coals.
ga: Eyɛ yitsɔi ni ejɔ, efɔ kɛ ehiŋmɛi efee tamɔ ŋai.

english: It growled at me and I could smell its breath, hot and reeking of death.
ga: Ebo ewo mi ni ma nyɛ afu emumɔ, edɔ ni eje fu tamɔ gbele.

english: I knew that I must run, but my legs were leaden and I could not move.
ga: Mi le akɛ esa ni ma jofoi, shi mi naji mi tsii ni mi nyɛɛɛ ma tsi mi he.

english: The dog came closer and closer, its teeth bared.
ga: Gbee lɛ bɛŋkɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ, enyanyɔŋ eje kpo.

english: I closed my eyes and waited for the end.
ga: Mi ŋa mi hiŋmɛi ni mi mɛ naagbee lɛ.

english: But then I heard a voice.
ga: Shi kɛkɛ lɛ mi nu gbee ko.

english: It was a woman's voice, soft and gentle.
ga: Yoo ko gbee ni, blɛoo ni ehe jɔ.

english: "Do not be afraid," she said. "I will help you."
ga: "Kaaa she gbeyei," ekɛɛ. "Ma ye ma bua bo."

english: I opened my eyes and saw the woman standing in front of me.
ga: Mi gbele me hiŋmɛi ni mi na yoo lɛ damɔ mi hiɛ.

english: She was tall and slender, with long black hair and dark eyes.
ga: Ekwɛ ni eyɛ bloblo, kɛ yitsɔi diŋŋ kakadaŋŋ kɛ hiŋmɛi ediŋŋ.

english: She wore a white dress that flowed around her like a mist.
ga: Ewo ataadei eyɛŋ ni nyiɛ ehe tamɔ afua.

english: "Who are you?" I asked. "I am the Angel of Death," she said.
ga: "Namɔ ji bo?" Mi bi. "Gbele bɔfo ji mi," ekɛɛ.

english: "I have come to take you to the other side." I was not afraid anymore.
ga: "Mi ba ma wo bo kɛ ya afã kroko lɛ. "Mi sheee gbeyei dɔŋŋ.

english: I knew that the woman would take me to a place where there was no pain or suffering.
ga: Mi le akɛ yoo lɛ kɛ mi baa yaa he ko ni piŋmɔ kɛ amanehulu bɛ.

english: I took her hand and she led me away.
ga: Mi mɔ enine ni eyi gbɛ.

english: As we walked, the black dog followed us.
ga: Be mi wɔ mii nyiɛ lɛ, gbee ediŋŋ lɛ nyiɛ wɔ sɛɛ.

english: I'm Dr. Boakye, a pediatrician at the Korle Bu Teaching Hospital.
ga: Atsɛɔ mi Dr. Boakye, datrɛfonyo ni kwɛɔ gbekɛbii yɛ Korle Bu Teaching Hospital.

english: I'm here today to talk to you about the new malaria vaccine that's been approved for use in Ghana.
ga: Mi yɛ biɛ ŋmɛnɛ koni bi kɛ bo awie atiridii gbuu tsofa ni ahe awo mli ni akɛ tsu nii yɛ Ghana.

english: Father: I'm not interested in having my children vaccinated.
ga: Tsɛ: Mi sumɔɔɔ ni agbu mi bii lɛ kwraa.

english: Doctor: I understand that you're concerned, but I'd like to take a few minutes to explain why I think it's a good idea to vaccinate your children against malaria.
ga: Datrɛfonyo: Mi nu shishi akɛ egba onaa, shi ma sumɔ ni ma he obei fioo koni ma gbala mli ma tsɔɔ bo nɔ ni hewɔ ni mi jwɛŋɔ akɛ eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa kɛji ogbu obii lɛ atiridii tsofa lɛ.

english: Father: I don't need to be convinced. Malaria is a serious disease, but it's not that common in our village.
ga: Tsɛ: Mi sumɔɔɔ ni otɔ̃ mi yiŋ. Atiridii ji hela ni naa wa, shi afɔɔɔ naa yɛ wɔ akrowa lɛ mii.

english: Doctor: That's true, but malaria is still a major public health problem in Ghana. In 2020, there were over 24 million cases of malaria in Ghana, and over 4,000 people died from the disease
ga: Datrɛfonyo: Anɔkwale ni, shi atiridii ji maŋ hewalɛ sane otii yɛ Ghana. Yɛ 2020 lɛ, ana 24 akpekpei kɛ sɛɛ yɛ atiridii saji he yɛ Ghana, kɛ gbɔmɛi 4,000 kɛ sɛɛ gbo kɛjɛ hela.

english: Father: But my children are healthy. They've never had malaria
ga: Tsɛ: Shi mi bii lɛ yɛ hewalɛ. Amɛ nako atiridii dã

english: Doctor: That's good, but it doesn't mean they're immune. Anyone can get malaria, even if they've never had it before.
ga: Datrɛfonyo: Ehi, shi etsɔɔɔ akɛ amɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛ na. Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ baanyɛ ni ena atiridii, kɛji amɛ nako eko dã kwraa.

english: "So, I was just on the internet, minding my own business, when I saw this pop-up ad that said I had a virus on my computer.
ga: "Hewɔ lɛ, mi tee intanɛt ɛ nɔ kɛkɛ, mii ye mishĩa sane, ni mi na adafitwsaa ko pue ni kɛɛ akɛ mi yɛ muawai yɛ mi kɔmpiuta lɛ nɔ.

english: I was like, "What? No way!"
ga: Mi fee tamɔ, "Mɛni ɛ? Daabi da!"

english: But then I clicked on it, and it took me to this website that looked really official, and it said that I needed to download this software to fix the virus.
ga: Shi ni mi nyɛ nɔ, ni ekɛ mi tee nɛkɛ wɛbsait ni tamɔ ekpakpa, ni ekɛɛ akɛ esa ni ma gbala sɔfwɛɛ ni mi kɛɛ saa kɔmpuita mli muawai lɛ.

english: So I did, and I installed it, and then it started filling my computer with all this malware.
ga: Hewɔ lɛ mi fee, ni mi wo nɔ, kɛkɛ ni ebɔi mi kɔmpuita nɔ yimɔ kɛ naagbai pii.

english: I was so mad!
ga: Mi miifu waa diɛŋtsɛ!

english: I tried to uninstall it, but it wouldn't let me.
ga: Mi fee ni ma jie kɛjɛ nɔ, shi ehaaa ni ma fee.

english: I finally had to take my computer to a repair shop, and they had to wipe the whole thing and reinstall Windows.
ga: Naagbee lɛ esa ni mi kɛ mi kɔmpuita lɛ aya he ni asaa kɔmpuita yɛ, ni esa ni amɛ tsumɔ emii nibii fɛɛ ni amɛ kɛ wo nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: It was a total nightmare.
ga: Eji lamɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei waa.

english: So, that's why I'm always so careful about clicking on pop-up ads.
ga: Hewɔ lɛ, eji nɔ ni hewɔ ni mi kwɛɔ mi he daa yɛ adafitwsaa puemɔ klikimɔ.

english: You never know what they're going to do.
ga: Oleŋ nɔ ni amɛ baa fee kɔkɔɔkɔ.

english: They could be filled with malware, or they could steal your personal information.
ga: Amɛ baanyɛ ni amɛ yi kɛ naagbai, loo amɛ baanyɛ ni amɛ ju osaji fɛɛ.

english: It's just not worth the risk.
ga: Ehe esaaa oshara ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: If you ever see a pop-up ad that looks suspicious, just close it and don't click on it.
ga: Kɛji ona adafitwsaa ni pueɔ ni yɔ kɔshikɔshi lɛ, ŋa kɛkɛ ni oka nyɛ nɔ.

english: And if you're ever not sure whether or not it's safe, just don't do it.
ga: Ni kɛji oleee akɛ eyɛ shweshweeshwe loo daabi lɛ, bɛ kaaa feee kɛkɛ.

english: Here is a delicious pork dish from the county of Lancashire.
ga: Naa kpootoo niyenii ni ŋɔɔ waa kɛjɛ Lancashire maŋ mli.

english: Ingredients: 1kg pork belly, 1 tbsp English mustard, 1 tbsp black treacle, 1 tbsp cider vinegar, 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce, 1 tbsp vegetable oil, 1 large onion, 4 cloves garlic, 2 bay leaves, 1 sprig of thyme, 100ml cider, 100ml chicken stock, 1 tbsp cornflour, 2 tbsp cold water.
ga: Niyenii nibii: kpootoo musu 1kg, English mustard niyeli awalei 1, treacle diŋŋ niyeli awalei 1, wain ni joo niyeli awalei 1, Worcestershire flɔ niyeli awalei 1, fɔ niyeli awalei 1, sabolai agbo 1, klov galiki 4, baai 2, thyme 1, cider 100ml, wuɔ nu 100ml, abele ashikiŋshã niyeli awalei 1, nu ni mli ejɔ niyenii awalei 2.

english: 1. Preheat the oven to 180 degrees.
ga: 1. Dɔɔ flɔnɔɔ lɛ mli kɛya shi 180 degrees.

english: 2. Trim the pork belly of any excess fat and score the skin in a criss-cross pattern.
ga: 2. Fɔlɔmɔ fɔ pii lɛ kɛjɛ kpootoo musu lɛ he ni ogbala heloo lɛ he.

english: 3. In a bowl, mix together the mustard, treacle, vinegar, Worcestershire sauce and oil.
ga: 3. Yɛ tsinii mli lɛ, futumɔ mustard, treacle, wain ni joo, Worcestershire flɔ kɛ fɔ kɛ tsa.

english: Rub this mixture all over the pork belly.
ga: Kɛ futumɔ nii nɛɛ akpa kpootoo musu lɛ he fɛɛ.

english: 4. Place the pork belly in a roasting tin and roast in the oven for 2 hours, or until the skin is golden brown and the meat is cooked through.
ga: 4. Kɛ kpootoo musu lɛ awo nishãa tsinsii mii ni oshã yɛ flɔnɔɔ lɛ mli ŋmɛlɛtswaa 2, loo kɛyashi be ni hewolo lɛ maa tsɔ asarasu ni loo lɛ mii awoo.

english: 5. While the pork is roasting, finely chop the onion, garlic, bay leaves and thyme.
ga: 5. Be mli ni kpootoo lɛ mii shã lɛ, fɔlɔmɔ sabolai, galiki, baai kɛ thyme lɛ bibii.

english: Nelson Mandela is a South African anti-apartheid revolutionary, political leader, and philanthropist who served as the first black president of South Africa from 1994 to 1999.
ga: Nelson Mandela ji South African nyo ni hetsɛ̃ hewolonɔ su mligbalamɔ hiɛtsakemɔ, ni maŋkwramɔ nɔyelɔ, kɛ moko ni feɔ mɛi ejurɔ ji lɛ ni sɔmɔ akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ mɔ diŋŋ sɛinɔtalɔ yɛ South Africa kɛjɛ 1994 kɛyashi 1999.

english: He is widely regarded as one of the most significant figures in world history.
ga: Anaa lɛ akɛ moko ni he hia waa yɛ jeŋ yinɔsane mli.

english: Mandela was born in 1918 in Mvezo, South Africa.
ga: Afɔ Mandela 1918 yɛ Mvezo, South Africa.

english: He grew up in a rural village and was educated at a Methodist mission school.
ga: Eda yɛ akrowa ko mli ni etee skul lɛ yɛ Methodist mission school ko.

english: After high school, he studied law at the University of Fort Hare.
ga: Sɛkɛndre skul sɛɛ lɛ, ekase mla he nibii yɛ University of Fort Hare.

english: In 1944, he joined the African National Congress (ANC), a political organization that was fighting against apartheid.
ga: Yɛ 1944 lɛ, eya fata African National Congress (ANC), maŋkwramɔ gbejianɔtoo ni damɔ kɛ shĩ hewolonɔ su mligbalamɔ.

english: Mandela was arrested for his political activities in 1962 and sentenced to life in prison.
ga: Amɔ Mandela kɛha emaŋkwramɔ nifeemɔi yɛ 1962 ni awo lɛ tsuŋ wala be fɛɛ.

english: He spent 27 years in prison, during which time he became a symbol of the anti-apartheid movement.
ga: Eye afii 27 yɛ tsuŋwoo mli, nakai be amli ni eba fee kadimɔ aha hewolonɔ su mligbalamɔ nyiɛmɔi hetsɛ̃mɔ.

english: In 1990, Mandela was released from prison and elected president of South Africa in 1994.
ga: Yɛ 1990, Ajie Mandela kɛjɛ tsuŋwoo mli ni awo lɛ sɛinɔtalɔ kɛha South Africa yɛ 1994.

english: As president, Mandela worked to unite South Africa and promote reconciliation between blacks and whites.
ga: Akɛ sɛinɔtalɔ lɛ, Mandela tsu nii koni eha South Africa efee ekome ni tsi kpatamɔ yɛ mɛi diŋji kɛ eyɛŋ sɛɛ.

english: He also oversaw the end of apartheid and the transition to a democratic government.
ga: Ekwɛ hewolonɔ su mligbalamɔ nagbee lɛ nɔ ni tsakemɔ kɛ tee demokrase nɔyeli.

english: Mandela is a Nobel Peace Prize laureate and has been awarded numerous other honors.
ga: Mandela ji moko ni nà Nobel Peace Prize jeremɔ ni aha lɛ jeremɔ nii krokomɛi babaoo.

english: After school, I usually go home and do my homework.
ga: Skul sɛɛ lɛ, mi yaa shĩa ni mi feɔ mi skul nitsumɔ ni afeɔ yɛ shĩa.

english: Then I might watch TV or play video games.
ga: Kɛkɛ lɛ ma kwɛ TV loo ma tswa vidio nɔ shwɛmɔ.

english: Sometimes I go out with my friends.
ga: Bei komɛi lɛ mi kɛ mi nanemɛi jieɔ kpo.

english: We might go to the movies, or to a park, or just hang out at someone's house.
ga: Wɔ baanyɛ wɔ ya kwɛ sini, loo shwɛmɔ he, loo wɔ ya shwɛ yɛ moko shĩa ni.

english: On weekends, I often sleep in late.
ga: Yɛ otsii lɛ anaagbee lɛ, be pii lɛ mi wɔɔ kɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Then I might go shopping, or see a movie, or go to a museum.
ga: Kɛkɛ lɛ ma nyɛ ma ya niihemɔ, loo ma kwɛ sini, loo ma ya blema nibii atoohe.

english: I also like to spend time with my family.
ga: Mi sumɔɔ ma na be ma ha mi wekumɛi.

english: We might go out to dinner, or play games, or just watch TV together.
ga: Wɔ baanyɛ wɔ je kpo wɔ ya ye gbɛkɛ niyenii, loo wɔ tswa gamii, loo wɔ kwɛ TV kɛkɛ.

english: I'm really enjoying my life after school.
ga: Mii nà miishɛɛ yɛ mi shihilɛ mli waa ni mi gbe skul naa sɛɛ lɛ.

english: I have a lot of freedom, and I can do whatever I want.
ga: Mi yɛ heyeli babaoo, ni manyɛ ma fee nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni mii sumɔ.

english: I'm also learning a lot about myself, and about the world around me.
ga: Mi kase mihe nibii babaoo, kɛ jeŋ nibii ni ebɔle mi.

english: I'm excited to see what the future holds.
ga: Mi yɛ miishɛɛ koni ma na nɔ ni baa ba wɔ sɛɛ.

english: Using data to help people with mental health issues is a relatively new field, but it is showing great promise.
ga: Ni akɛ saji ni ahala ni akɛ baa ye abua mɛi ni yɔɔ jwɛŋmɔ hela saji lɛ ji nitsumɔ ehei, shi etsɔɔ shiwoo ni hi waa.

english: One example is the use of data to personalize therapy for patients.
ga: Nɔkwɔmɔnɔ kome ji saji ni ahala ni akɛ tsuɔ nii koni ana tsofafeemɔ gbɛi pɔtɛɛ aha helatsɛmɛi.

english: By looking at a patient's individual data, therapists can better understand their needs and create a treatment plan that is tailored to them.
ga: Kɛji okwɛ helatsɛ ko he saji ni ahala lɛ, tsofafeelɔi baanyɛ ni enu amɛ haomɔi jogbaŋŋ ni afee tsamɔ gbejianɔtoo pɔtɛɛ aha lɛ.

english: This can lead to better outcomes for patients, as they are more likely to receive the help that they need.
ga: Enɛ kɛ sɛɛnamɔ ni hi baaba aha helatsɛ lɛ, akɛ ni amɛ na tsamɔ ni sa amɛ.

english: One study, which was published in the journal "JAMA Psychiatry," found that patients who received personalized therapy based on their data were more likely to improve their symptoms than those who received standard therapy.
ga: Nikasemɔ kome, ni akala awo wolo ni atsɛɔ lɛ "JAMA Psychiatry," na akɛ helatsɛmɛi ni nà tsamɔi pɔtɛɛ ni damɔ amɛ hela saji ni ahala lɛ nɔ na tsakemɔi yɛ amɛ hela okadii lɛ amli fe mɛi ni nà tsamɔi ko kɛkɛ.

english: The study also found that the patients who received personalized therapy were more likely to stay in treatment for longer periods of time.
ga: Nikasemɔ lɛ hu na akɛ helatsɛmɛi ni nà tsamɔi pɔtɛɛ lɛ tsa tsamɔ lɛ nɔ be babaoo.

english: This study is just one example of how data can be used to improve mental health care.
ga: Nikasemɔ nɛɛ ji nɔkwɛmɔnɔ kome kɛha bɔni abaanyɛ akɛ nibii ni ahala tsuɔ ni koni aha jwɛŋmɔ hela tsamɔ aha hiɛ.

english: As more research is done in this area, we can expect to see even more advances in the use of data to help people with mental health issues.
ga: Be ni afee niiamlitaomɔ pii yɛ nakai hei lɛ, wɔ baa na nibii ni ahala ni akɛ yeɔ buaa mɛi ni yɔɔ jwɛŋmɔ hela saji lɛ mii ya hiɛ.

english: My sister is a therapist who uses data to help her patients.
ga: Tsofafeelɔi ji mi nyɛmi yoo ni kɛ saji ni ahala yeɔ ebuaa ehelatsɛmɛi.

english: Freshwater lakes are home to a wide variety of flora and fauna, from microscopic algae to large fish and mammals.
ga: Nu-ŋma kpaakpo ji shĩa aha kwɛnii kɛ kooloi henɔi srɔtoi babaoo, kɛjɛ kwɛ̃ɛ nibii bibii ni hiŋmɛ enaaa kɛyashi loo agboi kɛ koolooi.

english: The unique environment of freshwater lakes provides a variety of habitats for these organisms, and the interactions between them are complex and fascinating.
ga: Akutsoŋ pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ nu-ŋma kpaakpo mli haa shĩai henɔi kɛha nɛkɛ nibii nɛ, kɛ nifeemɔi ni yɔɔ amɛ teŋ mli wa ni eyɛ naakpɛɛ.

english: One of the most striking features of freshwater lakes is the presence of a distinct zonation of plant life, which is determined by the depth of the water and the amount of sunlight that reaches the bottom.
ga: Noko krɛdɛɛ ni afɔɔ naa yɛ nu-ŋma kpaakpo ji tsei shihilɛ ahei srɔtofeemɔ, ni anàa kɛjɛ nu lɛ mli kɔlɛ kɛ hulu abɔ ni shɛɛɔ eshishi.

english: In shallow areas, where there is plenty of light, a dense mat of rooted plants known as a "macrophyte bed" forms.
ga: Yɛ hei ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ, ni hulu pii shɛɔ lɛ, tsei shishifãi efee saa pii ni atsɛɔ lɛ "macrophyte bed" henɔi.

english: This provides a habitat for a variety of invertebrates, fish, and amphibians.
ga: Enɛ haa shĩa kɛha koolooi ni bɛ wui, loo, kɛ nu mli koolooi.

english: In deeper areas, where there is less light, the water column is dominated by phytoplankton, which are microscopic algae that float freely in the water.
ga: Yɛ hei ni mli kwɔ lɛ, he ni hulu babaoo bɛ lɛ, nu lɛ mli eyi kɛ jwɛi bibii babaoo, ni ji kwɛ̃ɛ nibii bibii ni anaaa ni nyiɛ nu lɛ hiɛ.

english: These organisms are the primary producers in the lake ecosystem, and they are the basis of the food chain.
ga: Nibii nɛɛ ni klɛŋklɛŋ nibii ni feɔ niyenii yɛ nu maŋ lɛ mli, ni amɛ jeɔ niyenii yeli lɛ shishi yɛ nu lɛ mli.

english: The fauna of freshwater lakes is also diverse, and includes a wide variety of fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds, and mammals.
ga: Nu-ŋma kpaakpo mli koolooi hu yɛ henɔi, ni loo ahenɔi babaoo, nu mli kooloi, koolooi ni wamɔɔ, okpoi, kɛ koolooi agbo fɛɛ fata he.

english: Fish are the most abundant vertebrates in freshwater lakes, and they play a vital role in the food chain.
ga: Loo ji nɔ ni fa yɛ nu-ŋma kpaakpo lɛ mli waa, ni amɛ tsu nitsumɔ ni he hia waa yɛ niyenii yeli mli.

english: Some of the most common fish species in freshwater lakes include trout, bass, pike, and perch.
ga: Loo henɔi komɛi ni yɔɔ nu-ŋma kpaakpo mli ji trout, bass, pike kɛ perch.

english: The stainless steel plate is a good conductor of heat, so it can help to dissipate heat from the fire, while the fire proof rock wool is a good insulator, so it can help to prevent the fire from spreading.
ga: Dade tsinsii ji nɔni mɔɔ dɔlɛ mli jogbaŋŋ, hewɔ lɛ ebaanyɛ ni egbala dɔlɛ kɛjɛ la mli, be mli ni too yitsɔi tɛ ni nyɛɔ la ni nɔ ni baanyɛ ni edamɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ la hiɛ, hewɔ lɛ ebaanyɛ ni egbe la ni eka shwa.

english: In addition, the storage area is also equipped with a fire alarm system, so that if there is a fire, the alarm will sound and the fire department will be notified.
ga: Kɛfata he lɛ, niitoohe lɛ hu yɛ la ŋmɛlɛ ni gbɛɔ gbɛjianɔtoo, koni kɛji la ba, ŋmɛlɛ lɛ baa gbɛɛ ni la he nitsulɔi lɛ baa le.

english: The storage area is also regularly inspected by the fire department, so that any potential fire hazards can be identified and addressed before they become a problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ la he nitsulɔi ba kwɛɔ niitoohe lɛ bei mli, koni ana nibiii ni baanyɛ ewo la ni asaa amɛ dani ebatsɔ sane.

english: As a result of these measures, the storage area is a safe and secure place to store valuable goods.
ga: Gbɛji nɛɛ ahewɔ lɛ, niitoohe lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe koni anyɛ akɛ nibii kpakpai ato.

english: In addition to the fire safety measures, the storage area is also equipped with a security system to protect against theft.
ga: Kɛfata la shweshweeshwe feemɔ gbɛi lɛ, niitoohe lɛ hu yɛ shweshweeshwe feemɔ gbɛjianɔtoo ni buɔ he kɛjɛ juu.

english: The security system consists of a surveillance camera, a burglar alarm, and a security guard.
ga: Shweshweeshwe feemɔ gbɛjianɔtoo yɛ kamera, ŋmɛlɛ ni gbɛɔ kɛji julɔ bata noko he yɛ shĩa mli, kɛ bulɔ.

english: The surveillance camera monitors the area 24 hours a day, the burglar alarm is activated if anyone tries to break in, and the security guard is on duty to patrol the area and respond to any incidents.
ga: Kamerai lɛ naa akutsoŋ lɛ mli ŋmɛlɛtswai 24 daa gbi, asu ŋmɛlɛ ni gbɛɔ waa kɛji julɔ bata noko he yɛ shĩa mli, kɛ bulɔ ni mitsunii yɛ akutsoŋ lɛ mli ni baa he ebua kɛ sane ba.

english: As a result of these security measures, the storage area is a safe and secure place to store valuable goods.
ga: Shweshweeshwe feemɔ gbɛi lɛ hewɔ lɛ, niitoohe lɛ ji heko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni abaanyɛ akɛ nibii kpakpa ato.

english: Facebook Users Drunkenly Post About Their Lives
ga: Mɛi Ni Kɛ Facebook Tsuɔ Nii Lɛ Kɛ Amɛ Shihilɛ Wo Nɔ Ni Amɛ Tɔ Dãa

english: Facebook users are getting drunk and posting about their lives, and it's causing a stir.
ga: Mɛi ni kɛ Facebook tsuɔ nii mii tɔ dãa ni amɛ kɛ amɛ shihilɛ wo nɔ, ni ekɛ saneŋ ba.

english: The social media platform has been flooded with photos and videos of people who are clearly intoxicated, and many of them are sharing personal details about themselves that they wouldn't normally share.
ga: Intanɛt ɛ nɔ eyi kɛ mɛi ni etɔtɔɔ dãa amfonirii kɛ vidioii, ni amɛ teŋ mɛi pii mi ja amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ he saji ni esaaa ni mɛi leɔ ni amɛ bei pii lɛ amɛ jaaa.

english: Some users are concerned that the trend is dangerous, as it could lead to people making poor decisions or doing things they regret.
ga: Mɛi ni kɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ eko miihao akɛ nɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ yɛ oshara, akɛ ni ebaanyɛ ewo mɛi ashi ni amɛ kɔ yiŋkpɛ gbonyo loo afee nibii ni ehiii.

english: Others are simply amused by the antics of their fellow drunk Facebook users.
ga: Efee mɛi komɛi aŋmɔnɔ yɛ nibii ni amɛ Facebook bii ni amɛ tɔ dãa lɛ feɔ.

english: One user posted a photo of herself passed out on the floor with the caption, "I'm so drunk I can't even stand up."
ga: Ekome kɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ emfoniri ni ekashi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni eŋma, "Mi tɔ dãa aahu akɛ mi nyɛɛɛ shi ma damɔ."

english: Another user shared a video of herself dancing on a table while shouting, "I'm the life of the party!"
ga: Moko krokomɛi hu kɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ evidio ni eejo yɛ okpɔlɔ nɔ ni ebɔlɔ, "Mi kɛ paati lɛ wala!"

english: The trend has even caught the attention of celebrities.
ga: Nii ni yaa nɔ lɛ ehe mɛi ni ale amɛ waa ajwɛŋmɔ.

english: Comedian Amy Schumer posted a photo of herself on Twitter with the caption, "I'm so drunk I can't even spell my own name."
ga: ŋmɔnɔtsɛ Amy Schumer kɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mfoniri fɔ Twitter ni eŋma, "Mi tɔ dãa aahu akɛ mi nyɛɛɛ ma ŋma mi diɛŋtsɛ mi gbɛi."

english: Facebook has not commented on the trend, but it's clear that it's causing a stir.
ga: Facebook ewieko noko yɛ nibii nɛɛ anɔ, shi eka shi faŋŋ akɛ ekɛ saneŋ ba.

english: Only time will tell whether the trend will continue or fade away.
ga: Be pɛ baa tsɔɔ kɛji nii nɛɛ baa ya nɔ loo ebaa laaje.

english: Zambia is a landlocked country in Southern Africa.
ga: Zambia ji shikpɔŋ maŋ ko ni yɔɔ Africa wuoyigbɛ.

english: It is bordered by Angola to the west, the Democratic Republic of the Congo to the north, Tanzania to the northeast, Malawi to the east, Mozambique to the southeast, Zimbabwe to the south, and Botswana to the southwest.
ga: Angola efo ehe yɛ anaigbɛ, Democratic Republic of Congo yɛ kooyigbɛ, Tanzania yɛ kooyi bokagbɛ, Malawi yɛ bokagbɛ, Mozambique yɛ wuoyi bokagbɛ, Zimbabwe yɛ wuoyigbɛ, kɛ Botswana yɛ wuoyi anaigbɛ.

english: Zambia has a population of over 17 million people and a land area of 752,618 square kilometers.
ga: Zambia mɛi ateŋ babaoo fe 17 akpekpei kɛ sɛɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ dalɛ 752,618 sqɛɛ kilomitaii.

english: Zambia's current president is Hakainde Hichilema, who was elected in August 2021.
ga: Zambia sɛinɔtalɔ amrɔ nɛɛ ji Hakainde Hichilema, ni awo lɛ yɛ Manyawale 2021.

english: Hichilema is a member of the United Party for National Development (UPND).
ga: Hichilema fata United Party Kɛha National Development he (UPND).

english: The UPND is the largest opposition party in Zambia.
ga: UPND lɛ ji, shitee awolɔi yɛ Zambia.

english: The economy of Zambia is based on copper mining.
ga: Zambia shika he gbɛjianɔtoo damɔ akɔɔble tsaa.

english: Copper is the country's largest export.
ga: Akɔɔble ji maŋ lɛ majemɔ nii ni da waa.

english: Other important exports include cobalt, zinc, and lead.
ga: Majemɔ nibii krokomɛi ni he hia kobɔlt, sãnyãa, kɛ lɛd.

english: The Zambian economy has been struggling in recent years due to low copper prices.
ga: Zambia shika gbɛjianɔtoo mii na naagbai yɛ afii nɛɛ mli akɔɔble nyɔmɔwoo hewɔ.

english: Zambia is a member of the United Nations, the African Union, and the Southern African Development Community (SADC).
ga: Zambia ji United Health Nations, African Union, kɛ Southern Africa Development Community (SADC) kui lɛ ateŋ kome.

english: The signing of Lionel Messi by Paris Saint-Germain sent shockwaves through the world of soccer.
ga: Paris Saint-Germain he Lionel Messi ni enɛ haa bɔɔlutswaa jeŋ lɛ fɛɛ naakpɛ.

english: The Argentine superstar had been one of the most coveted players in the world for years, and his arrival in Paris marked a major turning point in the club's history.
ga: Argentina mɔ wulu lɛ ji tswalɔi ateŋ kome ni hiɛ kɔ̃ enɔ fe fɛɛ yɛ jeŋ lɛ mli afii babaoo, ni ebaa yɛ Paris kadi kuu lɛ yinɔsane tsakemɔi wulu ko.
