english: Messi had spent his entire professional career with Barcelona, where he had won everything there was to win.
ga: Messi ehi Barcelona bɔɔlutswaa nitsumɔ be amli fɛɛ, ni eye kunim fɛɛ kunim ni yɔɔ ni abaanyɛ aye.

english: But after a tumultuous few months, he decided to leave the club and sign with PSG.
ga: Shi yɛ basabasafeemɔ nyɔŋji fioo sɛɛ lɛ, ekpɛ yiŋ akɛ ebaa shi kuu lɛ ni eya fata PSG he.

english: The move was a major coup for PSG, who were looking to add a superstar to their squad in order to compete for the Champions League title.
ga: Tsakemɔ lɛ ji noko wulu aha PSG, ni miitao mɔ wulu ni amɛ kɛ fata amɛ kuu lɛ he koni amɛ tswa yɛ Champions League lɛ mli.

english: Messi's signing was met with excitement by PSG fans, who were eager to see the world's best player in action.
ga: Mɛi ni sumɔɔ PSG lɛ kɛ miishɛɛ ya kpe Messi hemɔ lɛ, ni amɛ tao ni amɛ na jeŋ lɛ tswalɔi fe fɛɛ ni miitsu nii.

english: But there were also some concerns about how he would fit into the team.
ga: Shi naagbai komɛi hu ba yɛ bɔi ebaa ya kuu lɛ mli aha.

english: PSG already had a number of talented players, and it was unclear how Messi would be able to work with them.
ga: PSG yɛ tswalɔi ayibɔ ni he esa ko omo, ni ekaaa shi faŋŋ bɔni Messi baanyɛ ekɛ amɛ etsu nii.

english: Of Mice and Men is a novel by John Steinbeck that tells the story of two migrant workers, George and Lennie, who travel together in search of work during the Great Depression.
ga: Of Mice and Men ji wolo ni John Steinbeck ŋma ni gbaa adesa yɛ gbɛfalɔi nitsulɔi enyɔ ko, George kɛ Lennie ni fa gbɛ yɛ nitsumɔi taomɔ hewɔ yɛ Great Depression be amli.

english: The novel is set in a time and place where the American Dream is all but dead, and the only way to survive is to stick together and look out for each other.
ga: Wolo lɛ yɛ be kɛ he ko ni American lamɔ ji fɛɛ shi egbo, ni gbɛ nɔ pɛ ni yiŋ baa ye wala ji kɛji afee ekome ni wɔ kwɛ wɔ he nɔ.

english: George and Lennie are both dreamers.
ga: Lalɔi ji George kɛ Lennie.

english: George dreams of one day owning a farm, where he and Lennie can live in peace and harmony.
ga: George lamɔi akɛ gbi ko lɛ ebaa na ŋmɔ, he ni ekɛ Lennie ba hi ji yɛ toiŋjɔlɛ kɛ ekomefeemɔ mli.

english: Lennie dreams of petting soft rabbits and being gentle with them.
ga: Lennie laa ni emɔ kɛŋkpɛlɛ ni yɛ bɔdɔɔ he kɛ amɛ shwɛ blɛoo.

english: But their dreams are constantly thwarted by the harsh realities of the world they live in.
ga: Shi jeŋ ni amɛ yɔɔ mli ni shihilɛ wa waa lɛ haa amɛ lamɔi fiteɔ daa.

english: One day, George and Lennie find work on a ranch in California.
ga: Gbi ko lɛ, Georgia kɛ Lennie na nitsumɔ yɛ koolooi alɛɛhei yɛ California.

english: They are immediately befriended by Candy, an old ranch hand who is missing an arm.
ga: Oya ni Candy kɛ amɛ fee naanyo, nuumo ko ni bɛ nine kome.

english: Candy tells George and Lennie about his dream of one day owning a small farm, and the three men decide to pool their money together to buy a farm.
ga: Candy kɛɛ George kɛ Lennie yɛ elamɔ akɛ gbi ko lɛ esumɔɔ ni enà ŋmɔ bibioo ko, ni hii etɛ kpɛ yiŋ akɛ amɛ kɛ amɛ shika baa tsa ni amɛ he ŋmɔ ko.

english: But their plans are once again thwarted when Lennie accidentally kills a woman.
ga: Shi amɛ gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ fite ekoŋŋ beni Lennie kɛ oshara gbe yoo ko.

english: George is forced to shoot Lennie to prevent him from being lynched.
ga: Anyɛ George nɔ ni etswa Lennie koni akɛ gbe lɛ yakatswaa.

english: George is devastated by Lennie's death, but he knows that it was the only thing he could do.
ga: George hiɛ ekpãtã yɛ Lennie gbele lɛ he, shi ele akɛ no pɛ ji nɔni ebaa nyɛ ni efee.

english: A: I'm so itchy! I think I have lice.
ga: A: Mi he kɔmɔ mi! Mi jwɛŋ akɛ mi yɛ ŋmoo.

english: B: Oh no! That's terrible.
ga: B: Oh daabi! Eyɛ gbeyei.

english: I know how to get rid of them, though.
ga: Mi le bɔni ma shwiee amɛ, moŋ.

english: We can use a traditional remedy.
ga: Wɔ baanyɛ wɔ kɛ blema tsabaa ko afee.

english: A: What is it?
ga: A: Mɛni ni?

english: B: We'll need some olive oil, some lemon juice, and a few cloves of garlic.
ga: B: Wɔ baa hia oliv fɔ, abonua nu, kɛ galiki fioo.

english: A: Okay, I have all of that. What do we do with it?
ga: A: Yoo, Mi yɛ enɛ fɛɛ. Mɛni wɔ kɛ fee?

english: B: First, we'll mix the olive oil, lemon juice, and garlic together.
ga: B: Klɛŋklɛŋ, wɔ baa futu oliv fɔ, abonua nu, kɛ galiki kɛ tsa.

english: Then, we'll apply it to your hair and scalp.
ga: Kɛkɛ lɛ, wɔ kɛ baa kpa oyitsɔi yɛ oyiteŋ.

english: We'll let it sit for about an hour.
ga: Wɔ baa ha emashi aafee ŋmɛlɛtswa kome.

english: A: An hour? That sounds like a long time.
ga: A: ŋmɛlɛtswaa kome? Etamɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: B: It is, but it's worth it.
ga: B: Nakai, shi ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ.

english: The oil will help to suffocate the lice and the lemon juice will help to kill them.
ga: Fɔ lɛ baa ye ebu ni etsi ŋmoo lɛ amumuɔ naa ni abonua nu lɛ baa gbe amɛ.

english: The garlic will help to repel them.
ga: Galiki lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɛ shwieɔ amɛ kɛ yaa sɛɛ.

english: A: Okay, I'll do it.
ga: A: Yoo, Ma fee.

english: "Mommy, what are those?" the toddler asked, pointing at the plants in the living room.
ga: "Ma, mɛni ji enɛɛ mɛ?" gbekɛ fioo lɛ bi, enine tsɔɔ tsei ni yɔɔ asa lɛ mli.

english: "Those are plants," Mommy replied "They're living things, just like you and me."
ga: "Enɛɛ mɛ tsei ni," Ma jie naa "Amɛ yɛ wala yɛ amɛ mli, tamɔ mi kɛ bo pɛpɛɛpɛ."

english: "Can I touch them?" the toddler asked.
ga: "Ma nyɛ ma ta amɛ he?" gbekɛ fioo lɛ kɛɛ.

english: "Yes, you can, but be gentle," Mommy said "The leaves are fragile."
ga: "Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ, shi fee blɛoo," Ma kɛɛ "Baai lɛ waa."

english: The toddler reached out and touched a leaf.
ga: Gbekɛb fioo lɛ kpa enine mli ni eta baa ko he.

english: The leaf felt soft and smooth.
ga: Baai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛ trotro.

english: "I like it," the toddler said.
ga: "Mi sumɔɔ," gbekɛ fioo lɛ kɛɛ.

english: "I'm glad," Mommy said. "Plants are good for us. They help clean the air and make us feel better."
ga: "Eŋɔɔ mi naa," Ma kɛɛ. "Tsei hi aha wɔ. Amɛ bua kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ mli tsumɔmɔ ni ehaa wɔ naa henumɔ kpakpa."

english: The toddler continued to look at the plants. Then, he noticed a cable running along the floor.
ga: Gbekɛ fioo lɛ tsanɔ ekwɛ tsei lɛ. Kɛkɛ ni, ena waya kpã kã shikpɔŋ.

english: "What's that?" he asked.
ga: "Mɛni nɛ?" ebi.

english: "That's a cable," Mommy said.
ga: "Waya kpã ni," Ma kɛɛ.

english: "It's used to connect the TV to the wall."
ga: "Akɛ tsaa TV kɛ pɛtɛɔ gbogbo he."

english: "Can I touch it?" the toddler asked.
ga: "Ma nyɛ ma ta he?" gbekɛ fioo lɛ bi.

english: "No, you can't," Mommy said. "Cables can be dangerous.They can give you a shock."
ga: "Daabi, onyɛɛɛ," Ma kɛɛ. "Waya kpã baanyɛ efee gbeyei. Amɛ baanyɛ ni amɛ shɔkii bo."

english: The toddler looked disappointed, but he didn't touch the cable.
ga: Gbekɛ fioo lɛ nijiaŋjewui, shi etaaa waya kpã lɛ he.

english: Birthdays are a time to celebrate the day you were born.
ga: Fɔmɔ gbii ji bei ni ayeɔ gbi ni afɔ bo.

english: It is a day to reflect on all the good things in your life and to thank those who have made you who you are.
ga: Eji gbi ni akaiɔ ni bii kpakpa yɛ owala mli kɛ shidaa aha mɛi ni ha ofee bɔni oyɔɔ lɛ.

english: It is also a day to set goals for the year ahead and to make plans for the future.
ga: Eji gbi hu ni akɛ otii mamɔɔ hiɛ kɛha afii ni baa lɛ ni ato gbɛjianɔi kɛha wɔ sɛɛ.

english: To make the most of your birthday, start by making a list of all the things you are grateful for.
ga: Koni ofɔmɔ lɛ aya nɔ ojogbaŋŋ lɛ, je shishi ni oŋma nibii fɛɛ ni oyɔɔ shidaa aha.

english: This could include your family, friends, health, home, job, or anything else that is important to you.
ga: Oweku, hewalɛ, shĩa, nitsumɔ, loo nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni he hia baanyɛ efata he.

english: Once you have made your list, take some time to reflect on each item and how it has made your life better.
ga: Kɛji ogbe oniŋmaa ota lɛ, kɔ bei ni okai nibii lɛ fɛɛ ekome komei kɛ bɔni ehaa oshihilɛ feɔ kpakpa.

english: Next, set some goals for the year ahead.
ga: Nɔni tsanɔ, too otii komɛi kɛha afii ni baa lɛ.

english: These goals can be anything you want them to be, but they should be specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound.
ga: Otii nɛɛ baanyɛ efee nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni osumɔ ni amɛ fee, amɛ fee pɔtɛɛ, anyɛ asusu, anyɛ ana, ehe hia, kɛ bei ahi he.

english: For example, you might set a goal to lose weight, get a promotion at work, or travel to a new place.
ga: Nɔkwɛmɔnɔ, okɛ baa fee otii akɛ shwelɛ baa ba shi, oya hiɛ yɛ nitsumɔ mli, loo ofa gbɛ kɛya heko hei.

english: Finally, make plans for the day of your birthday.
ga: Naagbee lɛ, too gbɛjianɔi kɛ ha ofɔmɔ gbi.

english: This could include spending time with your loved ones, eating your favorite foods, or doing something you have always wanted to do.
ga: Enɛ baanyɛ ni efee akɛ obaa na bei aha mɛi ni osumɔɔ, ye niyenii ni osumɔɔ waa, loo ofee noko ni otao ofee kɛtsɛ.

english: Person 1: Romantic Comedies are so unrealistic.
ga: Gbɔmɔ 1: suɔmɔ nibii ahe ŋmɔnɔ ji lakamɔ nifeemɔ.

english: Person 2: I know, right? The love interests always fall in love at first sight, and they never have any problems.
ga: Gbɔmɔ 2: Mi le, waa? Suɔlɔi lɛ sumɔɔ amɛ he fe nine shishijee lɛ, ni amɛ bɛ naagbai ko.

english: Person 1: And the conflicts are always so contrived.
ga: Gbɔmɔ 1: Ni bei lɛ yɛ ŋaa daa.

english: Like, in one movie, the couple broke up because the guy's best friend was in love with the girl.
ga: Tamɔ, yɛ sini kome mli lɛ, hefatalɔi lɛ kpa gbaa ejaakɛ nuu lɛ naanyo kpakpa miisumɔ yoo lɛ.

english: Person 2: That's so ridiculous. It's not like that happens in real life.
ga: Gbɔmɔ 2: Eji nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔnɔ. Jeee akɛ nakai baa mli yɛ anɔkwa wala mli.

english: Person 1: Exactly. And even when they do get together, it's always so perfect.
ga: Gbɔmɔ 1: Nakai. Ni kɛji amɛ fee ekome lɛ, eyɛ emuu daa.

english: They never have any fights or disagreements.
ga: Amɛ bɛ nɔmɔi loo naatamɔi ko.

english: Person 2: It's like the movies are trying to tell us that love is always easy and perfect.
ga: Gbɔmɔ 2: Etamɔ sinii lɛ kɛɛ wɔ akɛ suɔmɔ waaa ni eyɛ emuu daa.

english: But that's not the case.
ga: Shi jeee nakai ni.

english: Love is hard work.
ga: Suɔmɔ lɛ nitsumɔ agbo ni.

english: It takes time and effort to build a lasting relationship.
ga: Akɛ be kɛ nitsumɔ maa gbala ni sɛɛ baa tsɛ.

english: Person 1: I know. That's why I don't watch rom-coms anymore.
ga: Gbɔmɔ 1: Mi le. No hewɔ mi kwɛɛɛ suɔmɔ-ŋmɔnɔ sinii dɔ̃ɔ.

english: They give people unrealistic expectations about love.
ga: Amɛ haa mɛi lakamɔ gbɛkwɛmɔ yɛ suɔmɔ he.

english: My first day of school was a day I will never forget.
ga: Mi gbi klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ skul ji gbi ni mi hiɛ kpaaa nɔ da.

english: I was both excited and nervous, not knowing what to expect.
ga: Mi miishɛɛ mi he nakai beiaŋ lɛ nɔɔ mi tsui fa, ni mi leee nɔ ni baakpa gbɛ.

english: When I woke up that morning, I got dressed quickly and ate a quick breakfast.
ga: Ni mi te shi nakai leebi lɛ, Mi saa mi he oya ni mi ye leebi niyenii oya.

english: Then, my mom drove me to school and walked me to my classroom.
ga: Kɛkɛ lɛ, mi nyɛ kɛ mi tee skul yɛ kar mli ni ekɛ mi tee mi skul tsu lɛ mli.

english: When I walked into the classroom, I was immediately greeted by my teacher, Ms. Smith.
ga: Ni mi bote skul tsu lɛ mli lɛ, Mi tsɔɔlɔ lɛ ŋa mi nɔɔ, Ms Smith.

english: She was a kind-looking woman with a warm smile.
ga: Eje yoo kpakpa ni suɔmɔ yɔɔ ŋmɔnɔ mli.

english: She introduced herself to me and then showed me to my seat.
ga: Ejie ehe shi kɛ tsɔɔ me ni etsɔɔ mi heni ma ta.

english: I sat down next to a girl named Sarah.
ga: Mi sa gbekɛ yoo ni atsɛɔ lɛ Sarah.

english: She smiled at me and said, "Hi, I'm Sarah."
ga: Ekɛ mi ŋmɔ ni ekɛɛ, "Miŋa bo, Atsɛɔ mi Sarah."

english: I smiled back and said, "Hi, I'm Vera."
ga: Mi kɛ lɛ hu ŋmɔ ni mi kɛɛ, "Miŋa bo, Atsɛɔ mi Vera."

english: We talked for a few minutes before the bell rang for class to start.
ga: Wɔ wie minitii fioo dani ŋmɛlɛ ni haa ni nikasemɔ jeɔ shishi lɛ tswa.

english: Ms. Smith began by introducing herself and telling us about the rules of the classroom.
ga: Ms. Smith bɔi kɛ ehe shi jiemɔ ni ekɛɛ wɔ skul tsu lɛ mli mlai.

english: Then, she started teaching us about math.
ga: Kɛkɛ lɛ, ebɔ wɔ akuntaabuu tsɔɔmɔ.

english: I was a little bit confused at first, but Ms. Smith explained everything clearly.
ga: Efutu mi fioo yɛ shishi jee lɛ, shi Ms. Smith gbala nɔ fɛɛ nɔ mli ni eka shi faŋŋ.

english: After math class, we had a break.
ga: Akuntaabuu nikasemɔ sɛɛ lɛ, wɔ fo mli fioo.

english: Sarah and I went outside to play on the playground.
ga: Mi kɛ Sarah tee kpo lɛ nɔ koni wɔ ya shwɛ yɛ shwɛmɔhe lɛ.

english: We played on the swings and the slide for a while, then we went back inside for lunch.
ga: Wɔ shwɛ yɛ shiishɔ kɛ jɔɔhe shiishɔ be fioo, ni wɔ ku sɛɛ kɛ tee mli ni wɔ ye shwane niyenii.

english: When tissue is injured, the body’s immune system sends white blood cells to the area.
ga: Kɛji fãji ye awui lɛ, gbɔmɔtso mli nii ni gbeɔ muawai lɛ kɛ là mli wala yibii yɛŋ yaa nakai he lɛ.

english: These cells release chemicals that cause blood vessels to dilate and become more permeable.
ga: Nɛkɛ là mli yibii nɛɛ jie tsofai ni haa là fãji lɛ mli gbeleɔ koni enyɛ etsɔ mli.

english: This allows fluid and white blood cells to leak out of the blood vessels and into the injured tissue.
ga: Enɛ haa nu lɛ là mli wala yibii yɛŋ oje là fãji lɛ amli kɛya he ni eye awui lɛ.

english: The fluid forms a clear, watery swelling called edema.
ga: Nu lɛ feɔ nu nii ni efuu, ni mii tse ni atsɛɔ lɛ edema.

english: The white blood cells help to fight infection and to remove damaged tissue.
ga: Là mli wala yibii lɛ yeɔ ebua ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ anɔ ni ejie fãji ni efite.

english: They also release chemicals that stimulate the growth of new tissue.
ga: Amɛ jieɔ tsofai ni haa fãji ehei dalɛ baa.

english: The classic signs of acute inflammation are redness, heat, swelling, and pain.
ga: Kadimɔi komɛi ni tsɔɔ fuumɔ ji he lɛ tsuɔ, dɔlɛ, fuumɔ, kɛ piŋmɔ.

english: These signs are caused by the increased blood flow and the release of chemicals in the injured tissue.
ga: Là ni hoɔ oya kɛ tsofa jiemɔ yɛ fã ni ehe awui lɛ kɛ kadimɔi nɛɛ baa.

english: Redness is caused by the dilation of blood vessels.
ga: Là fãji ni mli egbele lɛ kɛ etsuru feemɔ baa.

english: Heat is caused by the increased blood flow and the release of inflammatory chemicals.
ga: Là ni hoɔ oya kɛ fuumɔ tsofai he ŋmɛɛmɔ kɛ dɔlɛ baa.

english: Swelling is caused by the leakage of fluid from blood vessels into the injured tissue.
ga: Nu ni mii ho kɛjɛ là fãji amli kɛ tee fã ni ehe awui lɛ kɛ fuumɔ baa.

english: Pain is caused by the release of inflammatory chemicals and the pressure of the swelling.
ga: Fuumɔ tsofai he ŋmɛɛmɔ kɛ fuumɔ ni naa wa kɛ piŋmɔ baa.

english: Acute inflammation is a normal part of the healing process.
ga: Fuumɔ fata helatsamɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ he.

english: However, if it is severe or prolonged, it can damage healthy tissue.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, kɛji enaa wa loo etsɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ni efite fãji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: In some cases, acute inflammation can lead to chronic inflammation, which is a long-term condition that can cause pain, disability, and even death.
ga: Yɛ shihilɛ komɛi amli lɛ, fuumɔ baanyɛ ekɛ fuumɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ aba, ni ji hela ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni baanyɛ ekɛ piŋmɔ, kumɔmɔ, kɛ gbele po aba.

english: There are a number of things that can cause acute inflammation, including infection, injury, and autoimmune diseases.
ga: Nibii pii yɛ ni baanyɛ eha fuumɔ aba, kɛ fata he lɛ tsɛŋemɔ, awui, kɛ gbɔmɔtso mli nii ni gbeɔ muawai ahelai.

english: Infections are caused by bacteria, viruses, or fungi.
ga: Muawai, virɔs, loo mɛlɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa.

english: When these organisms enter the body, they can trigger an immune response that leads to inflammation.
ga: Kɛ nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ bote gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli lɛ, amɛ baanyɛ ni gbɔmɔtso mli nii ni gbeɔ muawai lɛ aha hetoo ko ni haa fuumɔ baa.

english: Injuries can also cause inflammation.
ga: Pilamɔi hu baanyɛ ni amɛ kɛ fuumɔ aba.

english: When tissue is damaged, it releases chemicals that attract white blood cells and other immune cells to the area.
ga: Kɛji fã lɛ fite lɛ, ejieɔ tsofai ni gbalaa là mli wala yibii yɛŋ kɛ yibii krokomɛi yɛ ya he ni efite lɛ.

english: These cells release chemicals that cause inflammation.
ga: Nɛkɛ yibii nɛɛ jieɔ tsofai ni kɛ fuumɔ baa.

english: Autoimmune diseases are caused by the body’s immune system attacking its own tissues.
ga: Gbɔmɔtso mli nii ni gbeɔ muawai ahelai baa kɛji gbɔmɔtso mli nii ni gbeɔ muawai lɛ tutua lɛ diɛŋtsɛ efãji.

english: This can lead to inflammation in the affected tissues.
ga: Enɛ baanyɛ eha fuumɔ aba yɛ fã ni ena naagbai lɛ.

english: Acute inflammation is usually treated with pain relievers, such as ibuprofen or acetaminophen.
ga: Fuumɔ bei pii akɛ tsofai ni jɔɔ piŋmɔ he, tamɔ ibuprofen loo acetaminophen tsaa.

english: In some cases, corticosteroids may be used to reduce inflammation.
ga: Yɛ shihilɛ komɛi amli lɛ, akɛ corticosteroids haa fuumɔ baa shi.

english: If the inflammation is caused by an infection, antibiotics may be prescribed.
ga: Kɛji tsɛŋemɔ ha fuumɔ ba lɛ, abaa ha tsofai ni gbeɔ muawai.

english: Chronic inflammation is a long-term condition that can cause pain, disability, and even death.
ga: Fuumɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ji hela ni tsɛɔ ni kɛ piŋmɔ, kumɔmɔ, kɛ gbele po baa.

english: It is often caused by autoimmune diseases, such as rheumatoid arthritis and Crohn’s disease.
ga: Be pii lɛ autoimmune helai haa ebaa, tamɔ hela ni haa talɔi amli woɔ nu kɛ Crohn hela.

english: Chronic inflammation can also be caused by obesity, smoking, and air pollution.
ga: Fuumɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ ebaa kɛtsɔ shwilɛ, tawa shɛremɔ, kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ fitemɔ.

english: There is no cure for chronic inflammation, but it can be managed with medication, lifestyle changes, and physical therapy.
ga: Tsamɔ ko bɛ aha fuumɔ ni naa waa, shi abaanyɛ ni akudɔ kɛ tsofa, shihilɛ tsakemɔi, kɛ gbɔmɔtso tsofafeemɔi.

english: The Mozambican Civil War was a conflict that lasted from 1977 to 1992.
ga: Mazambican taa lɛ ji bèi ni tsɛ kɛjɛ 1977 kɛyashi 1992.

english: It was fought between the Mozambique Liberation Front (FRELIMO), which had ruled the country since its independence from Portugal in 1975, and the Mozambique National Resistance (RENAMO), a rebel group backed by the Rhodesian and South African governments.
ga: Nɔmɔ lɛ ba Mozambique Liberation Front (FRELIMO), ni ye maŋ lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ be ni amɛ tse amɛ he kɛjɛ Portugal yɛ 1975, kɛ Mozambique National Resistance (RENAMO), atũatselɔi kuu ko ni Rhodesian kɛ South African nɔyelɔi fiɔ amɛ sɛɛ ateŋ.

english: The war caused widespread devastation and displacement, and led to the deaths of an estimated 1 million people.
ga: Taa lɛ kɛ hiɛkpatamɔ kɛ he kroko jee ba, ni ekɛ mɛi tamɔ akpekpei 1 gbelei ba.

english: The war began after RENAMO launched an insurgency against FRELIMO in 1977.
ga: Taa lɛ je shishi sɛɛ mli ni RENAMO tse atutua ashi FRELIMO yɛ 1977.

english: RENAMO was opposed to FRELIMO's socialist policies and its close ties to the Soviet Union.
ga: RENAMO damɔshi ashi FRELIMO mlai lɛ kɛ ebɛŋkɛmɔ kɛha Soviet Union.

english: The war quickly escalated, and by the early 1980s, RENAMO had control of much of the countryside.
ga: Taa lɛ mli bawo wu, ni yɛ 1980s shishi jee lɛ, RENAMO na hewalɛ yɛ maŋ lɛ hei pii.

english: FRELIMO was forced to rely on Soviet and Cuban military aid to keep RENAMO at bay.
ga: Anyɛ FRELIMO nɔ ni ekɛ ehiɛ afɔ Soviet kɛ Cuban taalɔi ni heɔ ebua koni eha RENAMO akɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛ.

english: In 1984, FRELIMO and RENAMO signed a peace agreement, but the fighting continued.
ga: Yɛ 1984, FRELIMO kɛ RENAMO kadi toiŋjɔlɛ gbeekpamɔ ko, shi nɔmɔ lɛ tsanɔ.

english: In 1992, the two sides signed a new peace agreement, which called for a ceasefire and the holding of multiparty elections.
ga: Yɛ 1992, hei enyɔ lɛ kadi toiŋjɔlɛ gbeekpamɔ, ni atsɛɔ koni akpa tu tswaa ni afɔ shiki.

english: It was a bright and sunny day in the small village of Locksmiths, and the festival of locks was in full swing.
ga: Eji gbi ni hulu lɛ mii tso ni jeŋ ekpɛ yɛ Locksmiths akrowa bibioo ko, kɛ kladoai afiyeli be eba.

english: The streets were crowded with people, all eager to see the latest and greatest in lockmaking technology.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi lɛ eyi kɛ gbɔmɛi, ni mii eshɛɛ amɛ he akɛ amɛ baa na tsɔne ni akɛ feɔ kladoai lɛ ni eba ehei ni fee fɛɛ lɛ.

english: There were vendors selling everything from simple padlocks to complex combination locks, and artisans demonstrating their skills in lockpicking and locksmithing.
ga: Ayɛ nihɔɔlɔi ni mii hɔɔ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ kɛjɛ kladoai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛtee nɔni mli waaa, kɛ ŋaalɔ ni he esa kɛ dɛŋdade mii jie amɛ kladoa feemɔ kɛ kladoa ŋamɔ nitsumɔi lɛ kpo.

english: In the center of the village square, a large stage had been set up for the day's festivities.
ga: Yɛ maŋ lɛ teŋ lɛ, ato kpoku agbo kɛha gbi lɛ afiyeli lɛ.

english: A group of musicians were playing lively tunes, and a crowd of people were gathered around, clapping and dancing.
ga: Lala tswalɔi komɛi mii tswa lalai, ni mɛi babaoo ebua amɛ he, amɛ tswa amɛ deŋ ni amɛ jo.

english: On the stage, a skilled locksmith was demonstrating how to pick a lock, and the crowd was mesmerized by his skill.
ga: Yɛ kpoku lɛ nɔ lɛ, kladoa he nitsulɔ ko ni he esa mii tsɔɔ bɔni agbeleɔ kladoa, ni efee mɛi babaoo ni ebua shi lɛ naakpɛɛ.

english: As the sun began to set, the festival came to a close.
ga: Be ni hulu lɛ bɔ shi yaa lɛ, akɛ afiyeli lɛ ba naagbee.

english: My friend, Abel, and I were walking home from school one day when we saw a blood drive being held at our local community center.
ga: Mi naanyo, Abel, kɛ mi mii nyiɛ kɛ ya shĩa kɛjɛ skul gbi ko ni wɔ na la gbalamɔ nifeemɔ ni mii ya nɔ yɛ akutsoŋ lɛ mli.

english: We were both 17 years old, and we had never donated blood before.
ga: Wɔ fɛɛ wɔ ye 17, ni wɔ ha ko la daŋ.

english: We decided to stop in and see what it was all about.
ga: Wɔ kpɛ yiŋ akɛ wɔ baa kpa ni wɔ kwɛ nɔ ni yaa nɔ.

english: The process of donating blood was actually pretty simple.
ga: Asumaa gbɛnɔ ni ahaa la waa kwraa.

english: We both filled out a questionnaire and answered some questions about our health history.
ga: Wɔ enyɔ fɛɛ ha saji komɛi ahetoo kɛ tsɔ wɔ hewalɛ yinɔsane.

english: Then, we had our blood pressure checked and our veins were checked to make sure they were big enough.
ga: Kɛkɛ lɛ, akwɛ wɔ la falɛ hiɛ haa kɛ la fãji hu koni ana kɛji emɛ daramɔ hi lo.

english: Once we were cleared to donate, we each sat down in a chair and had a needle inserted into our arms.
ga: Ni aŋmɛ wɔ gbɛ ni wɔ ha la lɛ, wɔ ta sɛi ko mli ni akɛ abui wo wɔ niji amli.

english: The blood was collected in a bag, and the whole process took about 15 minutes.
ga: Aloo la awo baagi mli, ni agbe nɔ fɛɛ nɔ na tamɔ minitii 15.

english: It felt good to know that we were helping to save lives.
ga: Eha wɔ miishɛɛ akɛ wɔ ye wɔbua ni abaa wala yi.

english: After we donated, we were given a juice box and a cookie to help us recover.
ga: Ni wɔ ha la sɛɛ mli lɛ, aha wɔ juis kɛ akpaanɔɔ ni ewa ni wɔ he ewa wɔ.

english: We also received a thank-you card from the blood bank.
ga: Wɔ na shidaa wolo kɛjɛ la nitsumɔ he lɛ.

english: I'm glad that Abel and I decided to donate blood.
ga: Eŋɔɔ mi naa akɛ Abel kɛ mi kpe yiŋ akɛ wɔ baa ha la.

english: It was a quick and easy way to make a difference in the world.
ga: Eji gbɛnɔ ni yɔɔ oya kɛ mlɛo ni akɛ tsakemɔi baa jeŋ lɛ mli.

english: I encourage everyone to consider donating blood if they are eligible.
ga: Mi wo mɔ fɛɛ mɔ shi koni ejwɛŋ la hamɔ he kɛji esa akɛ obaanyɛ oha.

english: It's a simple act of kindness that can help save lives.
ga: Eji mlijɔ lɛ nifeemɔ ni baanyɛ eye ebua ni abaa wala yi.

english: A solo traveler was found safe after spending two nights lost in the Swiss Alps.
ga: Ana gbɛfalɔ ko shweshweeshwe sɛɛ mli ni eye gbɛkɛ ni elaaje yɛ Swiss Alps.

english: The 25-year-old woman, who has not been identified, was hiking in the mountains when she became separated from her group.
ga: Yoo lɛ ni eye afii 25 lɛ, ni ayoo lɛ, mii nyiɛ yɛ gɔŋji lɛ amli ni emi gbala kɛjɛ ekuu lɛ mli.

english: She was reported missing on Tuesday, and search teams were dispatched to find her.
ga: Abɔ amaniɛ akɛ elaaje Jufɔ, ni kuu ni tao mɛi lɛ tee lɛ taomɔ.

english: The woman was eventually found on Thursday, about 10 miles from where she had been hiking.
ga: Naagbee lɛ ana yoo lɛ Soo, tamɔ miles 10 kɛjɛ heni enyiɛ lɛ.

english: She was cold and dehydrated, but otherwise in good condition.
ga: Fɛɛ mii ye lɛ ni egbɔmɔtso mli nu eta, shi no sɛɛ lɛ eyɛ hewalɛ.

english: She told rescuers that she had been following a trail when she got turned around.
ga: Ekɛɛ mɛi ni ba here lɛ akɛ enyiɛ gbɛ ko nɔ ni aha eku esɛɛ.

english: She spent the night in a cave, and she survived by eating snow and drinking from a stream.
ga: Ewɔ bu ko mli nakai gbɛkɛ lɛ, ni ehi wala mli yɛ snoo yeli kɛ faa nu ni enu lɛ he.

english: The woman's experience is a reminder of the importance of being prepared when hiking in the mountains.
ga: Yoo lɛ niiashikpamɔ lɛ ji kaimɔ akɛ ehe hia ni abua he naa kɛji aya nyiɛmɔ yɛ gɔŋji lɛ amli.

english: Hikers should always bring a map, compass, and a flashlight, and they should tell someone where they are going and when they expect to return.
ga: Mɛ ni nyiɛɔ yɛ gɔŋji lɛ amli kɛ shikpɔŋ ahe mfoniri, kɔmpas, kɛ kane aya, ni amɛ kɛɛ moko he ni amɛ yaa kɛ be ni amɛ baa ba.

english: When I was a kid, I would spend hours poring over magazines.
ga: Be ni gbekɛ ji mi lɛ, mi ye ŋmɛlɛtswai babaoo yɛ wolo tɛtrɛɛi ahe.

english: I would read every article, look at every picture, and cut out the ones I liked to put in my scrapbook.
ga: Ma kane niŋmaa lɛ fɛɛ, ma kwɛ mfoniri fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli, ni ma fɔlɔ nɔni mii sumɔ ma wo ni shwɛmɔ wolo ko mli.

english: I loved the way magazines could transport me to different worlds and make me think about things in new ways.
ga: Mi sumɔɔ bɔ ni wolo tɛtrɛɛ lɛ kɛ mi yaa jeŋ srɔtoi ni ehaa mi jwɛŋɔ nibii ahe yɛ gbɛ hei nɔ.

english: One day, I was reading an article about brain science in a magazine.
ga: Gbi ko lɛ, Mii kane niŋmaa ko yɛ jwɛŋmɔ nilee yɛ wolo tɛrɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: The article was really interesting, and it made me think about how my brain works.
ga: Niŋmaa lɛ yɛ naakpɛɛ waa, ni eha ni mi jwɛŋ bɔni mi jwɛŋmɔ tsuɔ nii aha.

english: I realized that I could use my brain to learn anything I wanted, and that was an amazing feeling.
ga: Mi yɔse akɛ manyɛ mi kɛ mi jwɛŋmɔ akase nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni mi sumɔɔ, ni eji henumɔ ni miishɛɛ yɔɔ mli.

english: I've been reading magazines ever since, and I still love the way they can open my mind to new ideas.
ga: Mi kane wolo tɛtrɛɛ kɛjɛ nakai gbi lɛ, ni mi sumɔɔ bɔ ni amɛ gbeleɔ mi jwɛŋmɔ yɛ otii ehei he.

english: The debate about whether animals are happier in the wild or in zoos is a complex one with no easy answers.
ga: ŋwane jee yɛ kɛji koolooi miishɛɛ amɛ he yɛ koo lɛ mli loo koolooi akwɛmɔ he ji nɔ ni naa wa ni hetoo mlɛo bɛɛɛ he.

english: There are many factors to consider, including the individual animal's needs, the type of zoo, and the quality of care provided.
ga: Nibii babaoo yɛ ni esa akɛ akwɛ, kɛ fata he lɛ nibii ni he hia kooloo lɛ, kooloo kwɛmɔ he henɔi lɛ, kɛ mɛi ni kwɛɔ amɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Some animals, such as elephants, are highly social and need to interact with other elephants in order to thrive.
ga: Koolooi komɛi, tamɔ shwuɔi, amɛ sumɔɔ amɛ teŋ nyiɛmɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛ kɛ shwuɔi krokomɛi abɔ.

english: In the wild, elephants live in herds of up to 100 individuals.
ga: Yɛ koo lɛ mli lɛ, shwuɔi kɛ shwuɔi krokomɛi babaoo hiɔ shi kɛyashi ekomekomei 100.

english: They spend their days foraging for food, playing, and socializing.
ga: Amɛ yeɔ amɛ gbii lɛ yɛ niyenii taomɔ, shwɛmɔ, kɛ henaabuamɔ.

english: In a zoo, elephants may not have the same opportunities to interact with other elephants, which can lead to boredom and frustration.
ga: Yɛ koolooi akwɛmɔ lɛ, shwuɔi naa gbɛ ni amɛ kɛ shwuɔi krokomɛi asharaa, ni baanyɛ ekɛ shoofeemɔ kɛ nijiaŋwujee baa.

english: Other animals, such as lions, are solitary hunters.
ga: Koolooi krokomɛi, tamɔ jatai, ji gbɔbilɔi ni nyiɛɔ ekomekomei.

english: In the wild, lions live in prides of up to 15 individuals.
ga: Yɛ koo lɛ mli lɛ, jatai hiɔ shi kuu mli ni amɛ he 15 yɔɔ mli.

english: However, each lion within the pride has its own territory and does not interact with other lions very often.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, jata fɛɛ jata ni yɔɔ kuu lɛ mii lɛ yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eshikpɔŋkuku ni ekɛ jatai krokomɛi yee tsɔ.

english: In a zoo, lions may be able to live in larger enclosures with more space to roam, which can provide them with more opportunities to exercise and explore.
ga: Yɛ koo lɛ mli lɛ, jatai baanyɛ ni ahi tsuji ni dara ni gbɛ babaoo yɔɔ mli ni amɛ foshi, ni baanyɛ eha amɛ gbɛi pii ni amɛ gbɔle amɛ kpojiaŋ kɛ shikpàmɔ.

english: The type of zoo also plays a role in the welfare of its animals.
ga: Koolooi akwɛmɔhe henɔ hu tsɔɔ koolooi lɛ awala mli ahilɛ.

english: Some zoos are very large and provide their animals with spacious enclosures, while others are smaller and may not have as much space.
ga: Koolooi akwɛmɔhe komɛi dara ni amɛ haa amɛ koolooi lɛ tsuji ni gbɛ babaoo yɔɔ mli, be mli ni ekomɛi yɛ bibioo, ni amɛ bɛɛɛ gbɛ babaoo yɛ mli.

english: As I'm driving down the road, I see a goat giving birth in the median.
ga: Be ni mikudɔ kar kɛ nyiɛ gbɛɛ nɔ lɛ, mi na too ni miifɔ yɛ gbɛkpɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: She's lying on her side and her two front legs are extended in front of her.
ga: Eka eŋmawu nɔ ni ehiɛ naji enyɔ lɛ mli ekpã yɛ ehiɛ.

english: The baby goat is coming out of her right side and it's head is already visible.
ga: Too abifao lɛ mii jɛ eŋmawu jurɔ gbɛ ni oona eyitso omo.

english: The mother goat looks up at me and I can see the fear in her eyes.
ga: Too nyɛ lɛ wo ehiɛ nɔ ni ekwɛ mi ni manyɛ ma na gbeyeishemɔ yɛ ehiŋmɛi mli.

english: She's probably wondering if I'm going to hurt her or her baby.
ga: Ejwɛŋ akɛ benɛ ma pila lɛ loo eabifao lɛ.

english: I stop the car and get out.
ga: Mi wa kar lɛ ni mi yi shi.

english: I walk over to the goat and kneel down next to her.
ga: Mi nyiɛ kɛ tee too lɛ ŋɔɔ ni mi kotoshi yɛ emasɛi.

english: I gently stroke her head and tell her that everything is going to be okay.
ga: Mi kɛ mi nine nyiɛ eyiteŋ blɛoo ni kɛɛ lɛ akɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ baa hi.

english: The baby goat starts to emerge and I can see that it's a little girl.
ga: Too abifao lɛ bɔi baa ni manyɛ ma na akɛ gbekɛyoo bibioo ji lɛ.

english: She's crying and her mother licks her clean.
ga: Eefo ni enyɛ lɛmɔ ehe falefale.

english: I watch as the mother goat and baby bond and I feel a sense of peace.
ga: Mi kwɛ be ni too nyɛ lɛ kɛ abifao lɛ na tsakpaa ni mi na toiŋjɔlɛ henumɔ.

english: The city was a vast, sprawling metropolis, full of life and energy.
ga: Maŋ da, metropolis wulu, ni eyi kɛ wala kɛ hewalɛ.

english: It was a place where anything was possible, and where dreams could come true.
ga: Eji heko ni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ baanyɛ aba mli, kɛ heni lamɔi baanyɛ aba mli.

english: But for every person who found success in the city, there were many more who struggled to make ends meet.
ga: Shi kɛ ha mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni na omanye yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ayɛ babaoo ni etɔ amɛ kɛ niyenii kɛ shika namɔ.

english: These people lived in the slums, in tiny apartments that were often overcrowded and in disrepair.
ga: Nɛkɛ mɛi ni hiɔ shi yɛ hei ni ewo muji, shĩai bibii ni be pii lɛ emii ehi tsɔ ni efite.

english: They worked long hours for low pay, and they often had to go without basic necessities like food and healthcare.
ga: Amɛ tsu ni ŋmɛlɛtswai babaoo kɛha nyɔmɔwoo fioo, ni be pii lɛ amɛ bɛɛɛ nibii ni he hia tamɔ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ nɔkwɛmɔ.

english: One such person was a young woman named Amelia.
ga: Nakai moko ji oblayoo ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Amelia.

english: She had come to the city with big dreams, but she quickly found that reality was much different than she had imagined.
ga: Eba maŋ lɛ kɛ lamɔi agbo, shi ena anɔkwale shihilɛ ni yɛ srɔto fe nɔ ni ejwɛŋ oya.

english: She worked as a waitress in a small diner, and she could barely make enough money to pay her rent.
ga: Etsu nii akɛ moko ni toɔ niyenii yɛ okpɔlɔ nɔ yɛ niyenii yeli he bibioo ko, ni efeee shika ni fa ni ekɛ ha etsu nyɔmɔwoo.

english: She often went to bed hungry, and she was always worried about her future.
ga: Bei pii lɛ ekɛ hɔmɔ ya wɔɔ, ni ehaoɔ yɛ ewɔ sɛɛ he daa.

english: One day, Amelia was walking home from work when she saw a man sitting on a bench.
ga: Gbi ko lɛ, Amelia mii nyiɛ kɛjɛ nitsumɔ kɛ ya shĩa ni ena nuu ko ta bɛntsi ko nɔ.

english: He was homeless, and he was holding a sign that said, "Will work for food." Amelia felt sorry for the man, and she decided to buy him a sandwich.
ga: Ebɛ shĩa, ni enyiɛ adeka ni kɛɛ, "Ma tsu nii kɛya niyenii." Nuu lɛ he fee Amelia mɔbɔ, ni eto eyiŋ akɛ ebaa he sandwitsi aha lɛ.

english: As she was talking to the man, she learned that his name was Charlie.
ga: Be ni enyiɛ kɛ tee nuu lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ, ekase akɛ agbɛi ji Charlie.

english: Demonetization is the process of removing legal tender from circulation.
ga: Demɔnitaizashin ji gbɛnɔ ni ajieɔ shika ni akpaa egbɛfaŋ.

english: In India, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced on November 8, 2016, that all ₹500 and ₹1000 banknotes would cease to be legal tender from midnight.
ga: Yɛ India, Maŋsɔɔlɔ Onukpa Narendra Modi tswa adafi yɛ Alemle 8, 2016, akɛ abaakpa ₹500 kɛ ₹1000 shika kɛ nii tsumɔ kɛjɛ maŋkɛ.

english: This move was intended to crack down on corruption and counterfeiting, but it also caused significant disruption and hardship for many people.
ga: Afee nɛ koni ju kɛ fɔ̃ kɛ amale shika aba shi, shi ekɛ naagbai ni yeɔ tsui kɛ fimɔ ba aha mɛi babaoo.

english: There are several reasons to be skeptical of demonetization.
ga: Yiŋtoi srɔtoi yɛ ni baa ha yiŋ afee kɔshikɔshi yɛ demɔnitaizashin he.

english: First, it is not clear that it will be effective in reducing corruption.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ, ekaaa shi faŋŋ akɛ ebaa tsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ ju kɛ fɔ̃ shi baa.

english: Corruption is a complex problem that cannot be solved simply by removing cash from circulation.
ga: Ju kɛ efɔ̃ ji sani ni naa wa ni anyɛɛɛ akpa kɛji ajie shika gbɛfaŋ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli.

english: In fact, there is some evidence that demonetization may actually increase corruption, as it makes it more difficult for people to track and trace their money.
ga: Yɛ anɔkwale mii lɛ, odaseyeli komɛi yɛ akɛ demɔnitaizashin baa ha ju kɛ fɔ̃ aya ŋwɛi, akɛ ni ehaa ewaa aha mɛi ni amɛ na he ni amɛ shika lɛ etee.

english: Second, demonetization is likely to have a negative impact on the poor.
ga: Nɔ ni ji enyɔ, etamɔ demɔnitaizashin baa ha ohiafoi lɛ naagbai.

english: Many poor people in India rely on cash for their daily transactions.
ga: Ohiafoi babaoo yɛ India hiɛ kã shika nɔ kɛha amɛ daa gbi nibii feemɔ.

english: The sudden withdrawal of large-denomination banknotes made it difficult for them to buy food, pay their bills, and access other essential services.
ga: Shika wuji amrɔ jiemɔ ha ewa aha amɛ yɛ niyenii hemɔ he, amɛ nyɔmɔwoi, ni amɛ nine ashɛ nitsumɔi ni he hia amɛ.

english: Third, demonetization has caused significant disruption to the economy.
ga: Enɔ etɛ, shika ni abuu kɛ naagbai ni yeɔ tsui eba shika he gbɛjianɔtoo nɔ.

english: Businesses had to close for days or even weeks while they adjusted to the new currency.
ga: Esa ni nitsumɔi aŋamɔ gbii babaoo loo otsii po be mli ni ahe shika hei tsakemɔi lɛ awo mli.

english: The dish is said to have originated in the Philippines, where it is known as lechon.
ga: Niyenii nɛɛ akɛɛ jɛ Philippines, he ni ale lɛ akɛ lechon.

english: It is also popular in other parts of Southeast Asia, such as Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand.
ga: Ale waa yɛ Southeast Asia hei komɛi, tamɔ Indonesia, Malaysia, kɛ Thailand.

english: To make lechon, a whole pig is gutted and cleaned, then stuffed with a mixture of garlic, ginger, lemongrass, and other spices.
ga: Koni afee lechon, agbeɔ kpootoo muu ni ajieɔ emii nibii ni asaa he, ni awo lɛ galiki, kakatsofa, abonua jwɛi, kɛ tsofai ni afutu.

english: The pig is then roasted over a fire of charcoal or wood for several hours.
ga: Kɛkɛ lɛ ashã kpootoo lɛ yɛ ŋai la nɔ loo tso la nɔ ŋmɛlɛtswai babaoo.

english: The result is a juicy, flavorful meat that is perfect for a special occasion.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔ ji loo ni mli efɔ, ni naa ŋɔɔ ni ji emuu kɛ ha bei pɔtɛɛ ko.

english: Lechon is often served with rice and vegetables.
ga: Bei pii lɛ akɛ omɔ kɛ aduawai yeɔ Lechon.

english: It can also be eaten as a main course or as an appetizer.
ga: Abaanyɛ ni aye lɛ akɛ niyenii kpakpa diɛŋtsɛ aloo nɔ ni akɛ jieɔ daa.

english: If you are ever lucky enough to try lechon, you will not be disappointed.
ga: Kɛji ohe ba nii ni oye lechon, onijiaŋ ejeee wui.

english: It is truly a unique and delicious dish.
ga: Eji niyenii ni yɛ pɔtɛɛ ni ŋɔɔ.

english: In addition to the traditional method of cooking lechon, there are also several modern variations.
ga: Kefata blema gbɛnɔi ni akɛ hoɔ lechon lɛ, ayɛ ŋmɛnɛ henɔi srɔtoi babaoo hu.

english: Some chefs cook the pig in a pit oven, while others use a rotisserie.
ga: Nihoolɔi komɛi hoɔ kpootoo lɛ yɛ flɔnɔɔ bu ko mli, be mli ni ekrokomɛi kɛ rotisserie hoɔ.

english: There are also recipes for making lechon in a slow cooker or in the oven.
ga: Ayɛ bɔni ahoɔ lechon yɛ kuka mli loo yɛ flɔnɔɔ mli.

english: No matter how it is cooked, lechon is always a crowd-pleaser.
ga: Bɔ fɛɛ bɔni ahoɔ lɛ aha, lechon baa saa mɛi ahiɛ daa.

english: It is a hearty and flavorful dish that is perfect for any occasion.
ga: Eji niyenii ni ŋɔɔ ni haa miishɛɛ ni ji emuu aha be fɛɛ be.

english: So if you are looking for a new and exciting dish to try, lechon is definitely worth a look.
ga: Kɛji ootao niyenii hei ni yɔɔ miishɛɛ ni oye lɛ, lechon sa waa diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Me: What's up with your car? It's been making a weird noise lately.
ga: Mi: Mɛni efe okar lɛ? Efee dede ko ni yɔɔ srɔto gbeetɛnɛ.

english: Uncle: Yeah, I know. I'm taking it to the mechanic tomorrow.
ga: Tsɛkwɛ: Hɛɛ, mi le. Mi kɛ yaa tsɔne saalɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ wɔ.

english: Me: Is it going to be expensive.
ga: Mi: Ejara baa wa.

english: Uncle: It might be. The car is old, and parts are hard to come by. But I'm hoping it's just a minor issue.
ga: Tsɛkwɛ: Ebaanyɛ ni efee. Kar lɛ egbɔ, ni ehe nibii namɔ wa. Shi mi hiɛ ka nɔ akɛ sani bibioo kɛkɛ ni.

english: Me: Well, good luck. Let me know what the mechanic says.
ga: Mi: Ojogbaŋŋ, shade kpakpa. Ha ni ma le nɔ ni tsɔne saalɔ lɛ kɛɛ.

english: Uncle: I will. Thanks.
ga: Tsɛkwɛ: Ma fee. Oyiwaladɔŋŋ.

english: Me: Hey, by the way, did you know that nuclear cars are a thing?
ga: Mi: Kwɛmɔ, shi, ani ole akɛ nuklea kars ni yɔɔ nɔ?

english: Uncle: No, I didn't. That's interesting.
ga: Tsɛkwɛ: Daabi, mi leee. Eyɛ naakpɛɛ.

english: Me: Yeah, they're pretty cool. They use nuclear power to generate electricity, which powers the car's motor.
ga: Mi: Hɛɛ, amɛ yɛ fɛo waa. Akɛ nuklea hewalɛ feɔ srawa hewalɛ, ni haa kar moto lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Uncle: That sounds like it would be really expensive.
ga: Tsɛkwɛ: Etamɔ ejara baa wa waa.

english: Me: It can be, but it's also a lot more efficient than traditional cars. Nuclear cars can go for hundreds of miles on a single tank of fuel.
ga: Mi: Ebaanyɛ ni efee, shi etsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe blema kars lɛ. Nuklea kars baanyɛ eya miles ohai yɛ fuɛl tanki kome nɔ.

english: Uncle: Hmm, I'll have to look into that.
ga: Tsɛkwɛ: Hmm, Esa ni ma kwɛ no mli.

english: A man walks into a comedy club and orders a filet mignon.
ga: Nuu ko bote ŋmɔlɔ shwɛmɔhe ni ebi ni aha lɛ tsina loo ni eye.

english: The waiter brings him the steak and he starts to eat it.
ga: Mɔ ni ŋmɛɔ okpɔlɔ lɛ kɛ tsina loo lɛ ba ha lɛ ni ebɔi yeli.

english: After a few bites, he stops and says, "This steak is terrible! It's tough and tasteless."
ga: Ni eye fioo sɛɛ lɛ, ekpa ni ekɛɛ, "Tsina loo nɛɛ ehiii kwraa! Ewa ni ŋɔɔmɔ bɛ mli."

english: The waiter replies, "Well, sir, you did order a filet mignon."
ga: Mɔ toɔ niyenii yɛ okpɔlɔ nɔ lɛ ha hetoo, "Ojogbaŋŋ onukpa, obi ni aha bo tsina loo."

english: "Yes, but I didn't order a raw filet mignon!"
ga: "Hɛɛ, shi mi biii ni aha mi tsina loo ni ahoko!"

english: "Sir, all of our steaks are served raw. We require our customers to cook them themselves."
ga: "Onukpa, tsina loo lɛ fɛɛ ni wɔ toɔ lɛ ahoko. Wɔ haa wɔ nihelɔi lɛ hoɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ."

english: "But I don't know how to cook!"
ga: "Shi mi leee ni hoomɔ!"

english: "That's not our problem. We're a comedy club, not a restaurant."
ga: "Jeee wɔ sane ji no. ŋmɔnɔ shwɛmɔhe ji wɔ, jeee he ni ayeɔ nii yɛ."

english: The man angrily gets up and storms out of the club.
ga: Nuu lɛ kɛ mlifu te shi ni eshi daa shwɛmɔhe.

english: He had been in a car accident, and he was unconscious.
ga: Ebote kar oshara ko mli, ni nɔ̃ nyɔ enɔ.

english: His parents, who had been driving by when the accident happened, rushed to his side.
ga: Efɔlɔi, ni miikudɔ tsɔne kɛho ni oshara lɛ ba lɛ, tee emasɛi oya.

english: They were frantic with worry.
ga: Amɛ ye he hiamɔ haomɔ.

english: The paramedics arrived and loaded the boy into an ambulance.
ga: Tsofa feemɔ he nitsulɔi lɛ ba shɛ ni amɛ kɛ gbekɛ nuu lɛ wo ambolans lɛ mli.

english: His parents followed in their car, their hearts pounding with fear.
ga: Efɔlɔi kɛ amɛ kar nyiɛ sɛɛ, amɛ tsui mii tswa kɛ gbeyeishemɔ.

english: At the hospital, the doctors examined the boy and determined that he had a concussion and a broken leg.
ga: Yɛ helatsamɔhe lɛ, datrɛfoi lɛ kwɛ gbekɛ nuu lɛ ni amɛ na akɛ nɔ̃ enyɔ enɔ ni enane eku.

english: They admitted him to the hospital and began treatment.
ga: Ahe lɛ aŋmɛ helatsamɔhe ni abɔi tsamɔ.

english: The boy's parents stayed by his side, never leaving him alone.
ga: Gbekɛ nuu lɛ fɔlɔ hi emasɛi, amɛ shiii ekome da.

english: They watched over him as he slept, their hearts filled with love and hope.
ga: Amɛ kwɛ enɔ ni ewɔ, amɛ tsui eyi kɛ suɔmɔ kɛ hiɛnɔkamɔ.

english: "Royalty," said the Blacksmith, "is a curious thing. It's a kind of magic, really.
ga: "Maŋtsɛyeli," sɔ̃lɔ lɛ kɛɛ, "eji noko ni aatao ni ale. Eji majik henɔ, lɛɛlɛŋ.

english: People get all worked up about it, and they don't even know why.
ga: Mɛi nyaa he waa, ni amɛ leee nɔ ni hewɔ.

english: It's not as if kings and queens have any real power, these days. They're just figureheads.
ga: Jeee akɛ maŋtsɛmɛi kɛ manyɛmɛi yɛ hewalɛ ko, yɛ nɛkɛ gbii nɛɛ amli. Yitsogbɛ pɛ ji amɛ.

english: But people still seem to need them.
ga: Shi etamɔ ehe hia mɛi olo.

english: They need someone to look up to, someone to represent the idea of the nation." The Blacksmith paused.
ga: Amɛ hia moko ni amɛ kɛ amɛ hiɛ baa fɔ enɔ, moko ni baa damɔ shi aha susumɔ ni ji maŋ lɛ." Sɔ̃lɔ lɛ mɛ.

english: "I suppose it's a kind of comfort," he continued.
ga: "Efeɔ mi akɛ miishɛjemɔ henɔ ni," etsanɔ.

english: "To know that there's someone out there who's better than you.
ga: "Ni ole akɛ moko yɛ jɛmɛ ni hi fe bo.

english: Someone who's got it all sorted out.
ga: Moko ni ena nɔfɛɛnɔ naa.

english: Someone who can make the world a better place.
ga: Moko ni baanyɛ ni efee jeŋ lɛ he ko kpakpa ni ahiɔ.

english: Of course, it's all an illusion. But that doesn't make it any less important.
ga: Eji anɔkwale akɛ, lakamɔ nifeemɔ ni. Shi etsɔɔɔ akɛ ehe ehiaaa.

english: People need their illusions. They need to believe in something.
ga: Lakamɔ feemɔ he hia mɛi. Esa ni amɛ he noko amɛ ye.

english: And if that something is a king or a queen, then so be it."
ga: Ni kɛ nakai noko lɛ ji maŋtsɛ ko loo maŋnyɛ ko lɛ, bɛ aba mli nakai."

english: The Blacksmith paused for a moment, then smiled.
ga: Sɔ̃lɔ lɛ mɛ fioo, ni eŋmɔ.

english: The Old Man and the Sea
ga: Nuumo lɛ kɛ ŋshɔ lɛ

english: Santiago, an old Cuban fisherman, has gone eighty-four days without catching a fish.
ga: Santiago, Cuban nuumo wolɛɛnyo ko, etee gbii nyɔŋmai kpaanyɔ kɛ ejwɛ ni emɔko loo.

english: He is the oldest man in the village, and the youngest, Manolin, no longer wants to fish with him because the old man is unlucky.
ga: Lɛ ji nuu onukpa fe fɛɛ yɛ akrowa lɛ mli, ni gbekɛ fe fɛɛ, Manolin, sumɔɔɔ ni ekɛ lɛ aya wuo ejaakɛ nuumo lɛ he baa nii.

english: One day, Santiago sets out in his skiff and hooks a giant marlin.
ga: Gbi ko lɛ, Santiago kɛ elɛlɛ bibioo tee wuo ni emɔ marlin oblaŋ ko.

english: The marlin is so big that it pulls the skiff far out to sea.
ga: Marlin lɛ daa waa akɛ egbala lɛlɛ bibioo lɛ kɛtee ŋshɔ lɛ mii tɔɔ.

english: Santiago fights the marlin for two days and nights, but he cannot bring it in.
ga: Santiago kɛ marlin ɛ nɔ gbii enyɔ kɛ gbɛkɛi, shi enyɛɛɛ ni ekɛ ba ŋshɔ lɛ naa.

english: The marlin is too heavy, and the old man is too tired.
ga: Marlin ɛ miitsii tsɔ, ni etɔ nuumo lɛ tsɔ.

english: Finally, the marlin begins to tire.
ga: Naagbee lɛ, marlin ɛ nijiaŋ bɔi wui je.

english: Santiago is able to get a harpoon into the marlin, and he kills it.
ga: Santiago nyɛ ena akpɔlɔi ewo marlin ɛ mli, ni egbe lɛ.

english: But the marlin is so big that Santiago cannot bring it into the boat.
ga: Shi marlin ɛ daa kwraa tsɔ akɛ Santiago nyɛɛɛ ekɛ lɛ awo lɛlɛ lɛ mli.

english: He ties the marlin to the side of the boat and begins to row back to shore.
ga: Efĩ marlin lɛ epɛtɛ lɛlɛ lɛ ŋmawu ni ewiri kɛ ba ŋshɔ lɛ naa.

english: A school of sharks follows the boat, and they begin to eat the marlin.
ga: Ogboolei pii nyiɛ lɛlɛ lɛ sɛɛ, ni amɛ bɔi marlin ɛ yeli.

english: Santiago fights the sharks off, but he cannot stop them all.
ga: Santiago wu eshi ogboolei lɛ, shi enyɛɛɛ ni ekpa amɛ fɛɛ.

english: By the time he reaches shore, only the head and the tail of the marlin are left.
ga: Be ni eshɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ, marlin ɛ yitso kɛ elee pɛ ni eshwɛ.

english: The police will likely take the person to the station and question him.
ga: Polisifonyo lɛ ekolɛ kɛ gbɔmɔ baaya polisifoi anitsumɔhe ni ebi lɛ sane.

english: They will want to know where he got the wallet and why he was carrying it.
ga: Amɛ baasumɔ ni amɛ le he ni ena shika kotoku lɛ kɛjɛ kɛ nɔni hewɔ ni ehiɔ ehe.

english: If the person cannot provide a satisfactory explanation, he may be arrested and charged with theft.
ga: Kɛji enyɛɛɛ eha saji amlitsɔɔmɔi ni ha mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ, abaa mɔ lɛ ni afolɔ enaa akɛ julɔ.

english: If the person is arrested, he will be taken to jail and held until his trial.
ga: Kɛji amɔ lɛ, abaa wo lɛ tsu kɛyashi bei ni abaa ye esane.

english: At his trial, the prosecution will have to prove beyond a reasonable doubt that he is guilty of theft.
ga: Yɛ esaneyeli lɛ, esani naafolɔlɔ lɛ atsɔɔ akɛ eye juu he fɔ ni nwanejee ko nɛɛ he.

english: The defense will have the opportunity to present evidence and witnesses that may help to exonerate the person.
ga: Hefalɔ lɛ baa na hegbɛ ni eha odaseyeli kɛ odasefoi ni baa ye ebua gbɔmɔ akɛ eyeko juu fɔ.

english: If the person is found guilty, he may be sentenced to jail time, probation, or community service.
ga: Kɛji ana akɛ gbɔmɔ lɛ eye fɔ lɛ, abaa wo lɛ tsu, aaka lɛ akwɛ, aloo ma sɔɔmɔ nitsumɔ.

english: He may also be ordered to pay restitution to the victim of the theft.
ga: Agbɛnɛ hu abaa nyɛ ni afa lɛ ni eto mɔ ni eju lɛ lɛ najia.

english: In some cases, the person may be able to avoid criminal charges by entering into a diversion program.
ga: Yɛ shihilɛ komɛi amli lɛ, gbɔmɔ lɛ baanyɛ ni etsi ehe kɛjɛ sane ni akɛ fɔ enɔ lɛ kɛji ebote divɛshin gbɛjianɔto.

english: Diversion programs are designed to help people who have committed minor crimes avoid the criminal justice system.
ga: Afee divɛshin gbɛjianɔtoi ni eye ebua gbɛmɛi ni amɛ ye awui bibii amɛ kaya jalɛsaneyeli he gbɛjianɔtoi.

english: In a diversion program, the person may be required to complete community service, pay restitution, or attend counseling.
ga: Yɛ divɛshin gbɛjianɔto lɛ, ebaa hia akɛ gbɔmɔ baa gbe ma nitsumɔ anaa, ebaa to mɔ ni aye lɛ esha najia, aloo ebaa ya ŋaawoo.

english: If the person is found not guilty, he will be released from jail and the charges against him will be dropped.
ga: Kɛji gbɔmɔ lɛ ye bem, abaa jie lɛ ni abaa ŋmɛɛ efɔ ni akɛ ŋmɛ enɔ lɛ he.

english: He will be able to go on with his life without a criminal record.
ga: Ebaanyɛ ni eye wala ni abuuu lɛ awuiyelɔ.

english: It is important to note that the above is just a general overview of what may happen to a presumed thief who is held by police.
ga: Ehe hia ni akadi akɛ sane ni awie he yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ ji nɔni abaafee moko ni polisifoi emɔ lɛ julɔ.

english: The specific circumstances of each case will vary, and the outcome may depend on a number of factors, such as the evidence available, the person's criminal history, and the judge or jury's decision.
ga: Shihilɛ pɔtɛɛ ni yɔ sane fɛɛ sane efeee ekome, ni nɔ ni baajɛ sane lɛ mli baa damɔ nibii srɔtoi komɛi, tamɔ odaseyeli ni yɔɔ, gbɔmɔ awuyeli ni eye tsutsu bei amli, kɛ kojolɔ loo mɛni ni bua kojolɔi yeɔ sane lɛ ayikpɛ.

english: The couple, a renowned linguist and a world-renowned pastry chef, had been trying for a baby for years.
ga: Hefatalɔi lɛ, mɔni wieɔ wiemɔi babaoo ni ale lɛ jogbaŋŋ, dokɔdokɔ nihoolɔ ni maŋ fɛɛ le lɛ jogbaŋŋ, miitao bi a afii babaoo nɛɛ.

english: They had been to every doctor and specialist they could find, but nothing seemed to work.
ga: Amɛ tee datrɛfoi babaoo kɛ mɛi ni he esa waa, shi fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ noko tsuuu ni.

english: The linguist was starting to lose hope, and the pastry chef was worried that their reputation would be ruined if they couldn't have a child.
ga: Mɔ ni wie wiemɔ babaoo lɛ nijiaŋ je wui, ni dokɔdokɔ nihoolɔ lɛ hao ak egbɛi kpakpa lɛ baa fite kɛji efɔɔɔ bi.

english: One day, the linguist was working on a new translation of a difficult poem when he had a breakthrough.
ga: Gbi ko lɛ, mɔ ni wieɔ wiemɔ babaoo lɛ mii ha lalafoo wiemɔ shishinumɔ ni ena hiɛyaa kpele ko.

english: He realized that the key to having a child was to find a way to combine their two passions.
ga: Eyɔse akɛ otii titiri ni baa hani efɔ bi lɛ ji etao gbɛko nɔ ni ekɛ amɛ henumɔi enyɔ lɛ etsa.

english: He called the pastry chef and told her his idea.
ga: Etswa dokɔdokɔ nihoolɔ lɛ ni ekɛɛ lɛ esusumɔi.

english: The pastry chef was skeptical at first, but she agreed to give it a try.
ga: Dɔkɔdɔkɔ nihoolɔ lɛ yiŋ fee lɛ kɔshikɔshi shishijee lɛ, shi ekɛlɛ nɔ ni eka feemɔ ekwɛ.

english: They spent the next few months working on a new recipe for a cake that would be infused with the linguist's love of language and the pastry chef's love of baking.
ga: Amɛ ye nyɔji fioo kɛ tsu keeki shaa he nii ni akɛ mɔ ni wieɔ wiemɔ babaoo lɛ suɔmɔ kɛ ha wiemɔ lɛ nihoolɔ lɛ suɔmɔ lɛ ha nishaa wo mli.

english: When the cake was finally finished, they took it to the premier of a new play that the linguist was translating.
ga: Ni asha keeki lɛ ata, amɛ kɛ tee sini ehee ni mɔ ni wieɔ wiemɔ babaoo lɛ mii tsɔɔ shishi.

english: They waited until the after-party, and then they cut the cake and served it to everyone.
ga: Amɛ mɛ kɛyashi kuu bibioo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ni amɛ folɔ keeki lɛ ni amɛ ja aha mɔ fɛɛ mɔ.

english: The cake was a huge hit.
ga: Asumɔ keeki lɛ waa diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Everyone loved the taste, and they were all impressed by the story behind it.
ga: Mɔ fɛɛ mɔ sumɔ eŋɔɔmɔ ni amɛ naakpɛ amɛ he yɛ adesa ni yɔɔ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Hockey is a fast-paced, physical sport that is played on ice.
ga: Hockey ji gbɔmɔtso kpɔjiaŋgbɔlemɔ ni atswaa yɛ ais nɔ.

english: It is played with two teams of six players each, with one goaltender.
ga: Akɛ kpojiaŋgbɔlemɔ kui enyɔ kɛ emlibii ekpaa kɛha kuu kome kɛ goalkwɛlɔ.

english: The object of the game is to score goals by shooting the puck into the opponent's net.
ga: Shwɛmɔ lɛ otii titri ji atswa puck awo mɛni ni teɔ shi awoɔ kuu lɛ ayaa mli.

english: Hockey is a popular sport in Canada, the United States, and Europe.
ga: Hockey ji kpojiaŋgbɔlemɔ ni ale waa yɛ Canada, United States, and Europe.

english: It is also an Olympic sport.
ga: Eji Olympic kpojiaŋgbɔlemɔ hu.

english: The first indoor hockey game was played in Montreal, Canada, in 1875.
ga: Atswa klɛŋklɛŋ tsu mii Hockey shwɛmɔ yɛ Montreal, Canada, yɛ 1875.

english: The National Hockey League (NHL) was established in 1917.
ga: Aje National Hockey League (NHL) shishi 1917.

english: Hockey is a demanding sport that requires a high level of skill and athleticism.
ga: Hockey ji kpojiaŋgbɔlemɔ ni wa waa ni hia hesaa kɛ kpojiaŋ wa.

english: Players must be able to skate, shoot, pass, and stickhandle at a high level.
ga: Esa ni kuubii lɛ ale shwɛmɔ yɛ ais nɔ, passi mɔ, kɛ tso nyiɛmɔ yɛ ojogbaŋŋ gbɛ nɔ.

english: They must also be able to think quickly and make split-second decisions.
ga: Esa ni amɛ nyɛ amɛ jwɛŋ oya ni eha yiŋkpɛɛ oyaiyai.

english: Hockey is a great sport for people of all ages.
ga: Hockey ji shwɛmɔ wulu kɛ ha gbɛmɛi ni eye afii srɔtoi fɛɛ.

english: It is a fun and challenging way to stay active.
ga: Eji miishɛɛ gbɛnɔ ni kaa shi kɛha ekaafeemɔ.

english: Were it within my power to impart to you the incredibly detailed information concerning my deepest fear, I would do so without hesitation.
ga: Heni eyɛ mi hewalɛ mli akɛ mi kɛ naakpɛɛ sane fitsofitso ni tsɔɔ mi gbeyeshemɔ baa ha bo lɛ, ma fee nakai ni eshashaooo sho.

english: However, such knowledge is not mine to give.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, nɛkɛ nilee nɛɛ jeee mi enɔ ni ekɛ baa ha.

english: Suffice it to say that my greatest dread is something so insidious and far-reaching that it defies description.
ga: Abaanyɛ ni akɛɛ akɛ nɔni mi sheɔgbeye waa ji noko nigii ni naa wa akɛ anyɛŋ ana wiemɔi ni akɛaatsɔɔ mli.

english: It is a terror that lurks in the shadows, waiting to pounce at the most unexpected moment.
ga: Eji gbeyeenii ni etee ehe yɛ susumai amli, emɛ ni etu emɔ ni ale he bei.

english: It is a predator that feeds on my very essence, leaving me feeling weak and vulnerable.
ga: Eji kooloi awuyelilɔi shɔɔ mi hewalɛ, ni eha egbɔjɔ ni enyɛɔ ena ehe nɔ hewalɛ.

english: This insidious fear has been with me for as long as I can remember.
ga: Gbeyeshemɔ nigii kɛ mi yɛ gbi abɔ ni ekaiɔ.

english: It has shaped my life in ways that I am only beginning to understand.
ga: Etsake ewala yɛ gbɛ anɔi babaoo ni kpaako mii nu shishi.

english: I have become a recluse, afraid to venture out into the world lest I come face to face with my worst nightmare.
ga: Etsɔ mɔ kome mɔ, mi shegbeyee akɛ ma ya je lɛ mli ekolɛ ma ni naa lamɔi ni yɔɔ gbeyei waa.

english: I have lost friends and family, and my relationships have suffered.
ga: Eweku kɛ enaanemɛi egbo egbogboi, ni ewekukpaa epiŋ.

english: I am constantly on edge, waiting for the other shoe to drop.
ga: Mifee yeyeeye be fɛɛ be, mii mɛ nɔni baa ba.

english: I know that I am not alone in my suffering.
ga: Ele akɛ jeee me pɛ ni mii piŋ.

english: There are others who share my burden.
ga: Mei krokomɛi yɛ nuɔ ejatsu lɛ shishi.

english: We are a community of the damned, united by our fear.
ga: Wɔ ji akutso ni abu wɔ fɔ, gbeyeshemɔ haa wɔ feɔ ekome.

english: We are the ones who walk in the shadows, afraid of the light.
ga: Wɔ ji mɛi ni nyiɛɔ susuma mli, ni sheɔ kane gbeyee.

english: We are the ones who are haunted by the past, and who live in fear of the future.
ga: Wɔ ji mɛi ni tsutsu nibii miigba wɔ naa, ni wɔ kɛ wɔsɛɛ gbeyeshemɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Grandmother is sitting in her rocking chair, knitting a sweater.
ga: Naa ta esɛi niihoso, eloo ataade ni mii ti.

english: Her granddaughter, a teenager, is sitting on the couch, watching TV.
ga: Enabii, oblanyo, eta sɛi saatso mli, eekwɛ TV.

english: Grandmother: I remember when I was your age, we didn't have any of these fancy gadgets.
ga: Naa: Ekaiɔ akɛ bei ni etamɔ bo lɛ, wɔ bɛɛɛ nɛkɛ tsɔji fɛɛfɛo nɛɛ.

english: We had to go outside and play.
ga: Esane wɔ je kpo ni wɔ shwɛ.

english: Granddaughter: I know, Grandma. You've told me that story a million times.
ga: Nabii: Ele, Naa. Ogba mi sane lɛ akpekpei abɔ.

english: Grandmother: Well, it's true!
ga: Naa: Ojogbaŋŋ, anɔkwale ni!

english: We had to use our imaginations to have fun.
ga: Esane wɔ kɛ wɔ jwɛŋmɔ mfoniri ana miishɛɛ.

english: We didn't have all these video games and computers to entertain us.
ga: Wɔ bɛɛɛ vidio shwɛmɔi kɛ kɔmpuitai nɛɛ ni ha wɔ hiɛtserɛjiemɔ.

english: Granddaughter: But I like video games and computers. They're fun.
ga: Nabii: Shi esumɔɔ vidio shwɛmɔi kɛ kɔpuitai. Amɛ he yɛ miishɛɛ.

english: Grandmother: I'm not saying they're not fun, but they're not the same as playing outside.
ga: Naa: Ekɛɛɛ akɛ amɛ he bɛ miishɛɛ, shi amɛ tamɔɔɔ ni ashwɛ yɛ kpo nɔ.

english: When you play outside, you get exercise and you meet new people.
ga: Kɛji oshwɛ yɛ kpo nɔ lɛ, eha ogbɔleɔ okpojiaŋ ni ekɛ mɛi ehe kpeɔ.

english: Granddaughter: I know, Grandma. But I still like video games.
ga: Nabii: Ele, Naa. Shi esumɔɔ vidio shwɛmɔi olo.

english: Grandmother: Well, I guess you're just a product of your generation.
ga: Naa: Ojogbaŋŋ, efeɔ mi akɛ bo ji yɛ yinɔ ni naa nibii.

english: Granddaughter: I guess so.
ga: Nabii: Efeɔ mi nakai.

english: [Grandmother smiles and goes back to knitting.
ga: [Naa fee ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsa niloo lɛ nɔ.

english: Granddaughter goes back to watching TV.]
ga: Nabii lɛ tsa TV kwɛmɔ nɔ.]

english: The influences of religion on music are vast and varied.
ga: Hewalɛ ni jamɔ yɔɔ yɛ lala nɔ fa kɛ srɔtoo.

english: From the chanting of hymns in ancient temples to the soaring melodies of gospel songs, music has long been used to express religious beliefs and emotions.
ga: Kɛjɛ lala lamɔi yɛ blema jamɔhei kɛtee sanekpakpa lalai, akɛ lalai tsɔɔ jamɔ hemɔkɛyeli kɛ henumɔi bei pii ni eho.

english: In many religions, music is seen as a way to connect with the divine.
ga: Yɛ jami babaoo lɛ, anaa lala akɛ gbɛ ni akɛ Nyɔŋmɔ naa tsakpaa.

english: The sounds and rhythms of music can create a sense of awe and reverence, and can help to transport the listener to a higher plane of consciousness.
ga: Lala gbɛɛmɛ baaha naakpɛɛ kɛ gbeyeshemɔ henumɔ ko, ni ebaa wo toibolɔ lɛ kɛya hiɛtsɛrɛmɔ.

english: For example, in Hinduism, music is considered to be a form of yoga.
ga: Nɔkwɛmɔnɔ, yɛ Hindu jamɔ lɛ, anaa lala akɛ yoga henɔ.

english: The practice of kirtan, or devotional chanting, is said to help to purify the mind and open the heart to the divine.
ga: Kirtan gbɛtsɔɔmɔi, loo yaafo Kala hetuu-kɛhamɔ, akɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsuuɔ jwɛŋmɔ ni egbele tsui lɛ kɛha nyɔŋmɔ.

english: In Buddhism, music is often used as a form of meditation, helping to focus the mind and bring about a state of calm and tranquility.
ga: Yɛ Buddha jamɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ akɛ lala feɔ nii anɔ jwɛŋmɔ, ye ebuaa jwɛŋmɔ ni ekɛ naajɔlɛ kɛ toiŋjɔlɛ baa ba.

english: In addition to its spiritual role, music can also be used to address social and political issues.
ga: Kɛfata mumɔŋ nistumɔ lɛ, akɛ lala wiɔ shihilɛ kɛ maŋkwramɔ saji.

english: In the civil rights movement, for example, music played a powerful role in mobilizing people and inspiring them to fight for justice.
ga: Yɛ maŋ ahegbɛ kui lɛ, nɔkwɛmɔnɔ, lala tsu hewalɛ nifeemɔ yɛ gbɛmɛi buamɔ ni ewo amɛ hewalɛ ni anɔ aha jalɛsaneyeli.

english: The songs of Martin Luther King Jr, Mahalia Jackson, and others helped to give voice to the hopes and dreams of African Americans, and helped to bring about a more just and equitable society.
ga: Martin Luther King Jr, Mahalia Jackson, kɛ mɛi krokomɛi a lalai ye ebua Amerika mɛi diji hiɛnɔkamɔ kɛ lamɔi gbee, ni ekɛ kpaŋmɔ kɛ shihilɛ kpakpa baa ba.

english: The peacock is a large and colorful bird that is native to Asia.
ga: Piikɔk ji loofɔlɔ agbo ni ehe yɛ fɛo ni yɔɔ Asia maŋ lɛ.

english: It is known for its beautiful plumage, which is made up of iridescent blue, green, and purple feathers.
ga: Etsɛji fɛfɛo ni tamɔ bluu, baaŋmɔŋ, kɛ kɔɔjaŋ ni tsakeɔ, hewɔ ale lɛ.

english: Peacocks are also known for their elaborate courtship displays, which they perform to attract mates.
ga: Ale Piikɔk hu yɛ amɛ nyiɛmɔ ni tsɔɔ gbalashihilɛ ani feemɔi, ni ha yoo lɛ sumɔɔ amɛ.

english: During these displays, the male peacock will spread his tail feathers and fan them out to create a large, colorful fan.
ga: Yɛ nifeemɔi nɛɛ amli lɛ, piikɔk nuu baa gbɛ elee tsɛji mli ni etsɔ papa agbo kɛ he sui.

english: The female peacock will then choose a mate based on the size and beauty of his tail feathers.
ga: Piikɔk yoo baa damɔ dalɛ kɛ lee tsɛji he fɛo ni ekɛ baa hala hefatalɔ.

english: Peacocks are also known for their intelligence and ability to learn.
ga: Ale Piikɔk hu yɛ amɛ nilee ni amɛ le bɔ ni akaseɔ nii.

english: They can be trained to perform tricks and can even be taught to talk.
ga: Abaanyɛ ni atsɔse amɛ yɛ lakamɔ mli ni abaanyɛ atsɔɔ amɛ wiemɔ po.

english: In addition to their beauty and intelligence, peacocks are also important members of the ecosystem.
ga: Kefata amɛ hefɛo kɛ nilee, piikɔk he hia waa yɛ nibii kɛ amɛ shihilɛhe mli.

english: They help to control the population of insects and other pests, and their droppings can help to fertilize the soil.
ga: Amɛ yeɔ buaa kooloi filikilɔ bibii afa lɛ kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nibii akudɔmɔ, ni amɛ wamɔ yeɔ buaa sui lɛ.

english: I sit on the edge of the bed, my feet dangling over the side.
ga: Eta saatso lɛ naabu, enane tsotsoro emasɛi.

english: The air is thick with the smell of sweat and sex.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ lɛ tsii kɛ latsa kɛ bɔlɛnamɔ.

english: The sheets are tangled around my legs, and I can feel the warm imprint of his body on the mattress next to me.
ga: Mama eha enane he, ni mii nu egbɔmɔtso kadimɔ ni edɔ yɛ emasɛi yɛ saatso lɛ nɔ.

english: I reach for the postcard on the nightstand and write my name and address on the front.
ga: Ekɔ wolo ni ka okpɔlɔ lɛ nɔ ni eŋma egbɛi kɛ he ni pɔtɛɛ ni eyɔ yɛ ehiɛ.

english: Then I turn it over and begin to write "Dearest Ted," I write. "I'm having the time of my life here in Italy.
ga: Ni etsɔ esɛɛ ni ebɔi ŋmaa “Suɔmɔ Ted,” eŋma. “Miiye wala yɛ Italy.

english: The weather is perfect, the food is delicious, and the people are so friendly.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ lɛ hi waa, niyenii lɛ ŋɔɔ, ni gbɛmɛi lɛ he yɛ miishɛɛ.

english: I've been swimming in the ocean, exploring the ruins of ancient cities, and eating the best things the country has to offer."
ga: Mii sele yɛ ŋshɔɔ mli, miikpɛ blema maŋji ni efite, ni miiye nibii kpakpai ni maŋ lɛ baaha.”

english: I think of Ted's disintrest in outdoor activities and his bland cooking. I glance at Alfonso.
ga: Ejwɛŋ bɔni Ted sumɔɔ kponɔ nifeemɔi kɛ enihoomɔ ni eŋɔɔ. Ekwɛ Alfonso.

english: "I'm enclosing this postcard with a picture of the beach where I'm staying.
ga: “Ekɛ ŋshɔnaa he ni ehiɔ lɛ mfoniri miiwo wolo lɛ mli.

english: It's a beautiful spot, with white sand and crystal-clear water."
ga: Eji heko ni yɔɔ fɛo waa, kɛ shia eyɛŋ kɛ nu ni hiɛ tse waa.

english: The history of Cameroon is long and complex, dating back to the earliest human settlements in the region.
ga: Cameroon yinɔsane yɛ kakadaŋŋ Kɛ hwanyaŋŋ, eyaa sɛɛ kɛyaa be mli ni ato adesa ashihilɛhei ashishi yɛ kpokpaa nɔ.

english: The area was first settled by Bantu peoples around 3000 BCE, and it was later conquered by the Kanem-Bornu Empire in the 11th century.
ga: Bantu bii ni ba to jɛmɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ 3000 BCE ni Kanem-Bornu Empire he amɛ nɔ yɛ afii ohai 11.

english: In the 15th century, the Portuguese arrived in Cameroon and established trade relations with the local people.
ga: Yɛ afii ohai 15 lɛ, Portuguese bii ba shɛ Cameroon ni amɛ kɛ maŋbii lɛ je nihɔɔmɔ tsakpaa shishi.

english: The region was later colonized by Germany in the 1880s, and it became a German colony known as Kamerun.
ga: Sɛɛ mli lɛ Germany ba ye kpokpaa lɛ nɔ yɛ 1880 afii bei amli, ni eba tsɔ German shihemɔ maŋ ni atsɔɔ lɛ akɛ Kamerun.

english: During World War I, Cameroon was occupied by British and French forces, and it was divided between the two countries after the war.
ga: Be ni awuɔ Jeŋ Ta I lɛ he, Cameroon ba yi kɛ British kɛ French asrafoi, ni emli gbala ewo maŋ enyɔ mli ni ta lɛ ba naagbee.

english: The British-controlled region became known as Southern Cameroons, while the French-controlled region became known as French Cameroon.
ga: Kpopkaa ni yɔɔ British kudɔmɔ shishi lɛ ale amɛ akɛ Cameroon Wuoyigbɛ, be mli ni kpokpaa ni yɔɔ French kudɔmɔ shishi lɛ ale amɛ akɛ French Cameroon.

english: In 1960, Southern Cameroons became independent from Britain, and it merged with French Cameroon to form the Federal Republic of Cameroon.
ga: Yɛ 1960 afi lɛ, Cameroon Wuoyigbɛ ba tse amɛ he kɛjɛ British bii lɛ, ni amɛ French Cameroon bii bafee ekome kɛ fee Federal Republic of Cameroon.

english: In 1972, the federal system was abolished and Cameroon became a unitary state.
ga: Yɛ 1972 afii lɛ, afo maŋ muu lɛ gbejianɔtoo mli ni Cameroon bafee maŋ kome maŋ.

english: Cameroon has experienced a number of political and economic challenges in recent years.
ga: Cameroon ena maŋkwramɔ kɛ shika shidamɔ naagbai yɛ afi ni eho mli.

english: Mystery surrounds disappearance of Eva Green.
ga: Teemɔŋ saji yɛ Eva Green laajemɔ he.

english: Eva Green, a 25-year-old woman from London, has been missing for over a week.
ga: Eva Green, yoo no eye afii 25 ni ejɛ London maŋ nɔ, elaaje otsii kome kɛ sɛɛ nɛ.

english: She was last seen on February 25th, leaving her apartment in the city's Notting Hill neighborhood.
ga: Ana lɛ Oflɔ 25, ni eeshi etsu ni yɔɔ Notting Hill akutsoŋ lɛ mli.

english: Green is described as being 5'6" tall, with long brown hair and green eyes.
ga: Atsɔɔ Green akɛ moko ni kɛlɛ ji 5’6’’, kɛ eyitsɔi kakadaŋŋ braun kɛ hiŋmɛi baaŋmɔŋ.

english: She was last seen wearing a black coat, jeans, and a white t-shirt.
ga: Ana lɛ ni ewo kootu ediŋ, jeans, kɛ T-shirt eyɛŋ.

english: Police have said that they are concerned for Green's safety and are asking anyone with information about her whereabouts to come forward.
ga: Polisifoi ekɛɛ akɛ amɛ naa gba amɛ naa yɛ Green shweshweeshwe feemɔ nɔ ni amɛ bi kɛ ji moko le ehe sane lo.

english: Green's family and friends are desperate for news of her.
ga: Green wekumɛi kɛ enanemɛi hiɛnɔka esane he waa.

english: They have been posting flyers and distributing missing person's posters around the city.
ga: Amɛ kɛ adafitswaa woji pɛtɛshi ni amɛ ja moko ni elaaje adafitswaa woji yɛ maŋ lɛ mli.

english: They have also set up a Facebook page to help spread the word about her disappearance.
ga: Amɛ gbele gbɛ yɛ Facebook ni eye ebua amɛ ni agbɛ elaajemɔ sane lɛ kɛya jeŋ fɛɛ.

english: The police have not yet released any information about possible suspects or motives in Green's disappearance.
ga: Polisifoi lɛ hako sane ko yɛ mɔ fee loo nɔ ni hewɔ ni Green laaje lɛ.

english: They are asking anyone with information to come forward, no matter how small.
ga: Amɛ bi mɔfɛɛmɔ ni yɔɔ ehe sane ni ekɛ ba, yɛ bɔ ni bibioo ni eha po.

english: Green's disappearance is a mystery, but her family and friends are hopeful that she will be found safe and sound.
ga: Green laajemɔ yɛ naakpɛɛ, shi ewekumɛi kɛ enanemɛi hiɛkanɔ akɛ abaa na lɛ shweshweeshe.

english: Trimming your dog's nails is a necessary part of grooming, but it can be a daunting task for some pet owners.
ga: Ogbee waobii anaa kuu he hia yɛ hesaamɔ nifeemɔ mli, shi eji nifeemɔ ni wa aha kooloi anɔtsɛ komɛi.

english: If you're not sure how to trim your dog's nails, don't worry - it's easier than you think.
ga: Kɛji obɛ nɔminaa yɛ bɔ ni akuɔ ogbee waobii anaa lɛ, kaa ye otsui eyɛ mlɛo kraa fe bɔ osusuɔ.

english: The first step is to gather your supplies.
ga: Nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ji buamɔ onibii.

english: You'll need a pair of sharp scissors or a nail clipper, a styptic powder or pencil, and a towel.
ga: Obaa hia sakisi loo nɔ ni akɛ kuɔ waobii anaa, styptic mulu loo pɛnsil, kɛ papaŋ.

english: Next, you'll need to clip your dog's nails in a comfortable place.
ga: No sɛɛ lɛ, ehiaŋ akɛ obaa ku ogbee lɛ waobii anaa yɛ he ni hi jogbaŋŋ

english: If your dog is nervous, try clipping their nails in a quiet room where they can't see out the window.
ga: Kɛji ogbee lɛ tsui fa, bɔmɔdɛŋ ni oku ewaobii anaa yɛ tsu diŋŋ ko mli he ni enaa samflɛ ko mli.

english: You may also want to have someone help you hold your dog still.
ga: Obaa sumɔ ni moko hu eye ebua bo ni omɔ ogbee lɛ mli diŋŋ.

english: To trim your dog's nails, start by gently grasping their paw.
ga: Kɛ obaa ku ogbee waobii anaa lɛ, je shishi ni omɔ enane blɛoo.

english: Then, use your scissors or clippers to clip the tip of the nail.
ga: Kɛkɛ, kɛ osakisi loo klippa aku waobii lɛ anaa.

english: Be careful not to cut too short, as this can cause pain and bleeding.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni okaaa ku lɛ kuku, akɛ ebaa ni amɛ pila loo la eho.

english: If you do cut your dog's nail too short, apply a styptic powder or pencil to stop the bleeding.
ga: Kɛji oku ogbee waobii anaa kuku fe nine, kɛ styptic mulu loo pɛnsil akpa nɔ ni ekpa la hoo lɛ.

english: Styptic powders and pencils are available at most pet stores.
ga: Ahɔɔ Styptic mulu loo pɛnsil yɛ koolo ni akɛ amɛ shwɛɔ shwapo mli.

english: Once you've trimmed all of your dog's nails, be sure to reward them with a treat.
ga: Kɛji oku ogbee waobii anaa fɛɛ ogbenaa lɛ, kwɛmɔ ni oha ŋɔɔmɔ nii akɛ nyɔmɔwoo.

english: Trimming nails can be a stressful experience for some dogs, so it's important to make it a positive experience.
ga: Waobii anaa kuu baanyɛ efee haomɔ nifeemɔ kɛha gbee komɛi, hewɔlɛ ehe hia ni afee lɛ niiashikpamɔ ni ja.

english: With a little practice, you'll be able to trim your dog's nails like a pro.
ga: Kɛ kasemɔ fioo lɛ, obaanyɛ oku ogbee waobii anaa tamɔ mɔ ni he esa.

english: And your dog will be happy to have their nails trimmed, too!
ga: Ni ogbee lɛ mii baa shɛ ehe aɛ aku ewaobii anaa, hu!

english: Here are a few additional tips for trimming your dog's nails:
ga: Naa ŋaawoo krokomɛi ɛha gbee waobii anaa kuu:

english: * Start by trimming the nails on your dog's front paws.
ga: *Je shishi kɛ ogbee lɛ nane ni yɔɔ hiɛ kuu.

english: This is usually the easiest place to start.
ga: Bei pii lɛ enɛ ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ.

english: * If your dog is nervous, try trimming their nails one at a time.
ga: * Kɛji ogbee lɛ tsui fa, bɔmɔdɛŋ ni oku ewaobii anaa ekomei ekomei.

english: * Be sure to trim the nails evenly.
ga: * Kwɛmɔ ni oku waobii lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: You don't want one nail to be shorter than the others.
ga: Osumɔɔɔ ni waobi efee kuku fe fa bii lɛ.

english: * If you're not sure how to trim your dog's nails, ask your veterinarian or a groomer for help.
ga: * Kɛji obɛ nɔminaa yɛ bɔ ni akuɔ ogbee lɛ waobii lɛ, bi kooloi ahelatsalɔ loo mɔ ni saa kooloi ahe ni amɛ ye abua bo.

english: With a little care and attention, you can keep your dog's nails trimmed and healthy.
ga: Kɛji okwɛ lɛ ni ohiɛ hi enɔ fioo, obaanyɛ oku ogbee waobii anaa yɛ hewalɛ gbɛ nɔ.

english: Ivory Coast is a country in West Africa that has been in the midst of a civil war since 2010.
ga: Ivory Coast ji maŋ ko ni yɔɔ Afrika Anaigbɛ ni yɛ maŋ ta mli kɛjɛ 2010.

english: The conflict began after incumbent president Laurent Gbagbo refused to accept defeat in the 2010 presidential election.
ga: Nɔmɔ lɛ he shishi ni nɔyelɔ Laurent Gbagbo ekpɛnɛɛɛ ni aye enɔ kunim yɛ 2010 nɔyelɔ oshiki fɔɔ.

english: Gbagbo was eventually ousted by forces loyal to Alassane Ouattara, who was declared the winner of the election.
ga: Yɛ naagbee lɛ asrafoi ni yeɔ anɔkwa kɛha Alassane Ouattara shwie Gbagbo, ni awo lɛ akɛ eye kunim yɛ oshikifɔɔ lɛ mli.

english: However, the conflict has continued, with sporadic violence breaking out in the country.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, nɔmɔ lɛ tsara nɔɔ, kɛ basabasafeemɔ ni ba maŋ lɛ mli.

english: In 2017, there were hopes that the country would finally be able to move on from the civil war.
ga: Yɛ 2017 afii lɛ, hiɛnɔkamɔ lɛ akɛ maŋ lɛ baa ya ehiɛ ni eje maŋ ta lɛ mli.

english: However, these hopes were dashed when Gbagbo was acquitted of charges of crimes against humanity by the International Criminal Court.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, hiɛnɔkamɔi nɛɛ laaje ni Maŋ sɛɛ Awuyeli Saneyeliheŋmɛɛ Gbagbo he akɛ eyeko adesai awui.

english: Gbagbo's acquittal was seen as a blow to the peace process, and it led to renewed violence in the country.
ga: Ana Gbagbo he ŋmɛɛmɔ akɛ efite toiŋjɔlɛ nifeemɔ, ni eba tsɔ basabasafeemɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli.

english: In 2018, the United Nations Security Council imposed sanctions on Gbagbo and his supporters.
ga: Yɛ 2018, United Nations Security Council gbala Gbagbo kɛ egbɛmɛi ni yieɔ esɛɛ atoi.

english: The sanctions were aimed at pressuring Gbagbo to end his support for violence in the country.
ga: Toiŋgbalamɔ nɛɛ afee koni Gbagbo kɛ esumɔmɔ kɛha basabasafeemɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛɛ aba naagbee.

english: The sanctions have had some success, and there has been a decrease in violence in Ivory Coast since they were imposed.
ga: Toiŋgbalamɔ lɛ na omanye komɛi, ni basabasafeemɔ yɛ Ivory Coast ebashi kɛ nakai bei lɛ.

english: However, the country is still far from stable.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, maŋ lɛ efeko shiŋŋ kwraa.

english: There are many different ways to do laundry, from using a traditional washing machine and dryer to more eco-friendly methods like hand washing and line drying.
ga: Ayɛ gbɛi srɔtoi ni akɛ fɔɔ nii ahe, kɛjɛ blema nii ahe fɔmɔ tsɔne kɛ nii ahe gbimɔ tsɔne kɛtee gbɛjianɔ ni waa jeŋ tamɔ nine Nii ahe fɔmɔ kɛ kpaa nɔ nii anɔ kamɔ.

english: One way to do laundry without using a machine is to hand wash your clothes in a basin or sink.
ga: Gbɛ kome ni afɔɔ nii ahe ni kɛ nii ahe tsɔne efeee ji nine nii ahe fɔmɔ yɛ gagba loo sinki mli.

english: To do this, fill the basin with warm water and add a small amount of laundry detergent.
ga: Bɔ ni abaa fee lɛ nɛ, kɛ nu ni mii edɔ awo gagba mli ni okɛ samla fioo afata he.

english: Soak your clothes for a few minutes, then scrub them with a washcloth or brush.
ga: Fɔɔ otadei lɛ minitii fioo, kɛkɛ kposamɔ amɛ kɛ papam loo brɔshi.

english: Rinse your clothes thoroughly in clean water, then wring them out.
ga: Jalemɔ otadei lɛ ojogbaŋŋ yɛ nu kpakpa mli, kɛkɛ ŋaa mli.

english: Hang your clothes to dry on a clothesline or drying rack.
ga: Ka otadei lɛ yɛ nikamɔ kpaa loo niigbimɔ taoi anɔ.

english: Another option is to use a washing machine without a dryer.
ga: Gbɛ kroko hu ji akɛ niiahefɔmɔ tsɔne ni nigbimɔ tsɔne fataaa he baafee.

english: This can save energy and money, but it does require more time and effort.
ga: Enaa fiteee hewalɛ lɛ shika, shi ehiaa bei kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ babaoo.

english: To wash clothes in a machine without a dryer, fill the machine with water and add laundry detergent.
ga: Kɛji obaafɔ atadei yɛ niiahefɔmɔ tsɔne ni niiahegbimɔ tsɔne bɛ mli lɛ, kɛ nu awo niiahefɔmɔ tsɔne lɛ mli ni okɛ samla afata he.

english: Set the machine to the appropriate cycle, then start it.
ga: Kɛ tsɔne lɛ afɔ he ni ja, kɛkɛ jee shishi.

english: When the cycle is complete, remove your clothes from the machine and hang them to dry.
ga: Kɛ egbenaa lɛ, jiemɔ ataadei lɛ kɛjɛ tsɔne lɛ mli ni oka amɛ ni amɛ gbi.

english: If you live in an area with a lot of rain, you may be able to use the rain to help you dry your clothes.
ga: Kɛji ohiɔ akutsoŋ ko ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa, obaanyɛ ni nugbɔ aye ebuaa bo kɛ atadei lɛ gbimɔ.

english: Hang your clothes on a clothesline outside in the rain.
ga: Ka otadei lɛ yɛ nii nigbimɔ kpaa nɔ yɛ kpo nɔ yɛ nugbɔ mli.

english: In the beginning, there was only darkness.
ga: Shishijee lɛ, duŋ pɛ ni yɔɔ.

english: The universe was a vast, empty void.
ga: Jeŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ, ka shi ni noko noko bɛ mli.

english: Then, out of the darkness, came a spark.
ga: Kɛkɛ ni, kɛjɛ duŋ lɛ mli lɛ, gaimlibii ba.

english: This spark was the first sign of life in the universe.
ga: Gaimlibii nɛɛ ji okadii kɛŋklɛŋ ni tsɔɔ wala yɛ jeŋ lɛ mli.

english: It grew and expanded, becoming a small ball of fire.
ga: Efee agbo ni emiiɛɛ, ebaatsɔ la bibioo ko.

english: This ball of fire was the sun.
ga: Nɛkɛ la nɛɛ ji hulu lɛ.

english: Around the sun, the planets began to form.
ga: Yɛ hulu lɛ he, shibɔlemɔ ŋulami bɔi baa.

english: The Earth was the third planet from the sun.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ji shibɔlemɔ ŋulami ni ji etɛ kɛjɛ hulu lɛ he.

english: It was a small, rocky planet with a thin atmosphere.
ga: Eji shibɔlemɔŋulami ni yɛ bibioo kɛ tɛsaa, kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hatahata ko.

english: On the Earth, the first living things began to appear.
ga: Yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ, nibii ni yɔɔ wala ji klɛŋklɛŋ ni bɔi kpojee.

english: These were simple organisms, such as bacteria and algae.
ga: Enɛmɛi ji nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛ mli, tamɔ muawai kwɛɛnii bibii.

english: Over time, these organisms evolved into more complex forms of life, such as plants and animals.
ga: Sɛɛ mli lɛ, nɛkɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛ mii lɛ batsɔɔ wala wuji nibii, tamɔ kwɛɛnii loo kooloi.

english: The first humans appeared on Earth about 200,000 years ago.
ga: Adesai klɛŋklɛŋ ba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ 200,000 afii ni eho.

english: Humans have evolved and developed to become the dominant species on Earth.
ga: Adesai su etsake ni amɛ bafee jeŋ nibii amli srɔtoi fe fɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: The universe is still expanding and evolving.
ga: Jeŋ lɛ mii lɛɛ kɛ su miitsake.

english: Scientists believe that it will continue to expand for billions of years.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔI heɔ amɛ akɛ ebaayanɔ ni elɛɛ afiakpekpei.

english: Eventually, the universe will reach a point where it can no longer expand.
ga: Naagbee mli lɛ, jeŋ lɛ baanyɛ eshɛ heni enyɛɛɛ elɛɛɛ dɔŋŋ.

english: At this point, the universe will begin to contract.
ga: He eshɛ nɛɛ, jeŋ lɛ baa bɔi miimɔ.

english: Eventually, the universe will collapse in on itself and disappear.
ga: Naagbee mli lɛ, jeŋ lɛ baa kumɔ ewo emi ni ebaa laaje.

english: But even though the universe may end, the story of life will continue.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ jeŋ lɛ baaba naagbee, wala adesa lɛ baaya nɔ.

english: I'm concerned about the environment and the impact that climate change is having on our planet.
ga: Mi hao yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛ hewalɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔŋ tsakemɔ ena yɛ wɔ shibɔlemɔ ŋulami nɔ.

english: I'm also a big fan of technology and gadgets, so I'm always looking for ways to reduce my carbon footprint without sacrificing my lifestyle.
ga: Mi sumɔɔ tɔnei kɛ elɛtrɔnik nibii hu, no hewɔ lɛ mii tao gbɛjianɔi ni matse mi lashinyanyera najiaŋnaa nɔ ni ma sha eshihilɛ afɔle.

english: That's why I'm so excited about renewable and alternative energy sources.
ga: Enɛ hewɔ emiishɛɛ ehe yɛ hewalɛ srɔtoi ni etaaa.

english: Renewable energy is energy that comes from sources that are naturally replenished, such as solar, wind, and water power.
ga: Hewalɛ ni tsakeɔ ji hewalɛ ni jɛ henɔi ni shikpɔŋ diɛtsɛŋ toɔ ewoɔ enajiaŋ, tamɔ hulu, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ nu hewalɛ.

english: Alternative energy is energy that comes from sources that are not traditionally used for power generation, such as biomass and geothermal energy.
ga: Hewalɛ ji hewalɛ ni jɛ henɔi ni ejɛɛɛ blema hewalɛ, tamɔ biomass kɛ geothermal hewalɛ.

english: Both renewable and alternative energy sources are clean and sustainable, meaning they don't produce greenhouse gases or other pollutants.
ga: Hewalɛ henɔi lɛ fɛɛ mii tse ni etsɛɔ, etsɔɔ akɛ ewooo mulu aloo kɔɔyɔɔ fɔŋ.

english: One of the best ways to make a difference is to switch to renewable energy sources for your home.
ga: Gbɛ nɔ kpakpa kome ni kɛ tsakemɔ baa ji okɛ hewalɛ henɔi ni hi aha jeŋ lɛ baatsu nii yɛ oshia.

english: You can do this by installing solar panels on your roof, buying a wind turbine, or signing up for a green power plan from your utility company.
ga: Obaanyɛ ni ofee enɛ kɛji owo otsu yiteŋ solar tsɔne, hemɔ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔne, loo hemɔ hewalɛ nu hi aha jeŋ lɛ.

english: You can also reduce your energy consumption by unplugging appliances when you're not using them, turning off the lights when you leave a room, and using energy-efficient appliances.
ga: Obaanyɛ ni otse bɔni wɔ ohewalɛ feɔ nii kɛji wɔ gbe tsɔnei nibii kɛji wɔ kɛ amɛ nitsunii ata, gbee kane kɛji oshi tsu mli, ni kɛ nibii ni gbalaaa hewalɛ atsu nii.

english: The old wooden boat sat on the shore, its sails furled and its hull weathered by the sun and the rain.
ga: Tso lɛlɛ momo lɛ ma ŋshɔnaa, ebalaai lɛ bashi ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu lɛ wo lɛ kɛtee
