english: It had seen many years of service, carrying its owners on voyages to far-off lands.
ga: Ena afii babaoo yɛ suɔɔmɔ mli, ekɛ enɔtsɛmɛi etee gbɛfaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shɔɔŋ

english: But now, it was retired, its days of sailing over.
ga: Shi bianɛ, eba enitsumɔ mli, egbɛfaa kɛ lɛlɛ bei eho.

english: One day, a young boy named Thomas came to the beach.
ga: Gbi ko lɛ gbekɛ nuu fioo no atsɔɔ lɛ Thomas ba ŋshɔɔ naa.

english: He had heard stories about the old boat, and he was eager to see it for himself.
ga: Enu lɛlɛ emomo lɛ he adesai, ni emiishwe ni ena lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: When he saw the boat, he was amazed by its size and its beauty.
ga: Be ni ena lɛlɛ lɛ, enaa kpɛ ehe yɛ edalɛ kɛ ehe fɛo.

english: He could imagine himself sailing off on adventures in the vast ocean.
ga: Ena yɛ ejwɛŋmɔ mfoniri akɛ eeya miishɛɛ gbɛfaa yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Thomas asked the owner of the boat if he could take a closer look.
ga: Thomas bi lɛlɛ nɔtsɛ kɛji ebaanyɛ ni ebɛnkɛ lɛlɛ lo.

english: The owner smiled and said, "Of course you can. Come aboard!"
ga: Nɔtsɛ fee ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛɛ: “Hɛɛ obaanyɛ. Ba nɔ!”

english: Thomas climbed into the boat and sat down in the captain's chair.
ga: Thomas kɔ ebote lɛlɛ lɛ mli ni etashi yɛ lɛlɛ kudɔlɔ lɛ sɛi mli.

english: He looked out over the water and imagined himself sailing away to a faraway land.
ga: Ekwɛ nu lɛ nɔ ni ejwɛ ehe ni fa gbɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ tsɔŋŋ ko.

english: The owner of the boat watched Thomas for a moment, then said, "Do you want to learn how to sail?"
ga: Lɛlɛ nɔtsɛ kwɛ Thomas bei fioo, ni ekɛɛ, “Ani otao ni okase bɔ akudɔɔ lɛlɛ loŋ”

english: Thomas' eyes widened "Yes" he said.
ga: Thomas hiŋmɛi gbele waa “Hɛɛ” ekɛɛ.

english: The owner of the boat smiled again.
ga: Lɛlɛ nɔtɛ fee ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: "Then I'll teach you," he said.
ga: “Bɛ ma tsɔɔ bo,” ekɛɛ.

english: Scene: Two friends, Jasmine and Joseph, are sitting at a coffee shop.
ga: Nɔ ni ba: nanemɛi enyɔ, Jasmine kɛ Joseph, ta kɔfe shwapo ko mli.

english: Jasmine: I'm so glad you could meet me today, Joseph.
ga: Jasmine: Eŋɔɔ enaa waa akɛ okɛ mi kpe ŋmɛnɛ, Joseph.

english: I really need your help.
ga: Ye obua me.

english: Joseph: Anything for you, Jasmine.
ga: Joseph: Nɔfɛɛnɔ aha bo, Jasmine.

english: What's going on?
ga: Meni yaa nɔ?

english: Jasmine: I'm having a really tough time at work.
ga: Jasmine: Ewa ha mi waa yɛ nitsumɔ.

english: I'm not sure if I'm going to be able to keep my job.
ga: Mileee kɛji manyɛ ma mɔ nitsumɔ mii.

english: Joseph: Oh no, Jasmine.
ga: Joseph: Oh daabi, Jasmine

english: I'm so sorry to hear that.
ga: Edɔ mi waa akɛ minu enɛ.

english: Jasmine: It's a long story.
ga: Jasmine: Sane kakadaŋŋ ni.

english: But basically, my boss is really unfair to me.
ga: Shi kɛ ma kɛɛ lɛ, enitsumɔ onukpa lɛ yeee mi sane ni eja.

english: She's always picking on me and making me do all the worst jobs.
ga: Eyeɔ esane tsɔ daa gbi ni ehaa efeɔ nitsumɔi ni ehiii fe fɛɛ.

english: And she's not even giving me a fair chance.
ga: Ni ehaaa mi anɔkwale gbɛ po.

english: Joseph: That's terrible, Jasmine.
ga: Joseph: Ehiii kwraa, Jasmine.

english: I can't believe she's treating you like that.
ga: Eheee eyeee akɛ efeɔ bo nakai.

english: Jasmine: I know.
ga: Jasmine: Ele.

english: I'm so stressed out about it.
ga: Mii ye haomɔ yɛ he.

english: I don't know what to do.
ga: Eleee nɔni ma fee.

english: Joseph: Well, first of all, you need to take a deep breath and calm down.
ga: Joseph: Kɛlɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, esane omu waa kɛya omli ni ona tsui.

english: The smell of fresh-baked bread wafted through the air as the baker pulled a tray of golden brown loaves from the oven.
ga: Blodoo ni asha etsɛko ŋma eyi kɔɔyɔɔ mli beni egbala apaawa ni blodoo jwele nɔ kɛjɛ flɔnɔɔ lɛ mli.

english: He carefully set them on a cooling rack and smiled, pleased with his work.
ga: Ekɛ amɛ fɔ shi ni amɛ he ajɔ ni efee ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, emii eshɛɛ ehe yɛ enitsumɔ lɛ he.

english: The loaves were perfectly browned and had a delicious aroma that made his mouth water.
ga: Blodoo lɛ efee braun ojogbaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋma ni ŋɔɔ ni ha ni eba etsine.

english: He couldn't wait to try one!
ga: Enyɛɛɛ ni emɛ ni eye ekome.

english: The baker cut a slice of bread and took a bite.
ga: Nishalɔ lɛ fo blodoo lɛ fioo ni eye.

english: It was even better than he had imagined, with a soft, chewy texture and a rich, flavorful taste.
ga: Eŋɔɔ kwraa fe bɔ ni esusu, eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, ehiɛsu kɛ eŋɔɔmɔ kpakpa ko.

english: He closed his eyes and savored the moment, enjoying the feeling of contentment that came from eating something so delicious.
ga: Eŋa ehiŋmɛi ni enuŋɔɔmɔ he, kɛ miishɛɛ henumɔ ni onaa kɛji oye noko ni ŋɔɔ.

english: The baker knew that he was lucky to have the ability to bake such delicious bread.
ga: Nishalɔ lɛ na miishɛɛ akɛ ebaanyɛ ni esha blodoo ni ŋɔɔ nɛkɛ.

english: He took pride in his work and was always happy to share his creations with others.
ga: Ena henɔwomɔ yɛ enitsuɔ mli ni ekɛ miishɛɛ ja eha mɛi nii ni ebɔ.

english: The type of fish you choose will depend on your personal preferences and the intended use for the fish.
ga: Loo ni obaa hala baa ka osumɔɔ nii kɛ nɔ ni okɛ yaa fee.

english: If you are looking for a fish that is high in omega-3 fatty acids, then you may want to choose a wild river fish.
ga: Kɛji osumɔ loo ni ehi kɛ omega-3 lɛ, bɛ obaa sumɔ ni ohala faa ni hoo mii loo.

english: These fish are typically lower in contaminants than farm-raised fish.
ga: Looi nɛɛ bɛ muji tsɔ yɛ amɛ mli tamɔ loo ni alɛ amɛ yɛ loo ŋmɔ mii.

english: However, wild river fish can be more expensive and difficult to find.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, faa ni yɛ hoo mii loo jara baanyɛ ni wa ni ebaa wa akɛ abaa na.

english: If you are looking for a fish that is mild in flavor and easy to cook, then you may want to choose a calm lake fish.
ga: Kɛji osumɔ loo ni naa ŋɔɔmɔ he jɔ ni ehoomɔ waa, bɛ obaa sumɔ ni ohala faa ni jɔ mii loo.

english: These fish are typically not as high in omega-3 fatty acids as wild river fish, but they are still a good source of protein and other nutrients.
ga: Nɛkɛ looi nɛɛ bei pii lɛ amɛ omega-3 faaa tamɔ faa ni yɛ hoo mii loo, shi eji niyenii amli nu ni hi waa.

english: Calm lake fish are also typically more affordable and easier to find than wild river fish.
ga: Faa ni jɔ mli loo bei pii lɛ jara waaa ni amɛ namɔ waaa tamɔ faa ni yɛ hoo mii nu.

english: If you are looking for a fish that is low in cost and easy to care for, then you may want to choose a stock pond farm raised variety.
ga: Kɛji ootao loo ni jara waaa ni ekɛmɔ waa lɛ, bɛ obaa sumɔ ni ohala loo henɔi ni alɛ amɛ yɛ loo ŋmɔ mli.

english: These fish are typically raised in controlled environments and are fed a diet that is designed to promote growth.
ga: Nɛkɛ loo nɛɛ bei pii lɛ akudɔɔ nibii ni bɔle amɛ ni ahaa amɛ niyenii ni haa amɛ daa oya.

english: Stock pond farm raised fish are typically not as high in omega-3 fatty acids as wild river or calm lake fish, but they are still a good source of protein and other nutrients.
ga: Loo ni alɛ amɛ yɛ looŋmɔ mli bei pii lɛ amɛ omega-3 faaa tamɔ faa ni yɛ hoo loo faa ni jɔ mli loo, shi eji niyenii mli nu ni hi waa.

english: Ultimately, the best type of fish for you will depend on your individual needs and preferences.
ga: Yɛ naagbee lɛ, loo ni hi fe fɛɛ aha bo baa ka bo diŋtsɛ nɔni osumɔɔ ni otaoɔ.

english: Do some research to learn more about the different types of fish available and choose the one that is right for you.
ga: Feemɔ niiamlitaomɔ ni okase loo henɔi srɔtoi ni yɔɔ kɛ nɔni hi eha bo.

english: Unsolved mysteries have captured the public's imagination for centuries.
ga: Teemɔŋ saji ni anako emɔ maŋ lɛ jwɛŋmɔ mfoniri afii oha abɔ.

english: From the disappearance of Amelia Earhart to the identity of Jack the Ripper, these cases have left us wondering what really happened.
ga: Kɛjɛ Amelia Earhart kɛtee namɔ tuuntu ji Jack the Ripper, saji nɛɛ eha wɔ jwɛŋ akɛ meni tee nɔ.

english: While some of these mysteries may never be solved, they continue to fascinate us because they offer a glimpse into the unknown.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ teemɔŋ saji komɛi nɛɛ anaaa he tsabaa, efeɔ wɔ naakpɛɛ olo ejaakɛ ehaa wɔ naa noko fioo yɛ nɔni aleee he eko mli.

english: One of the most famous unsolved mysteries is the disappearance of Amelia Earhart.
ga: Teemɔ saji ko ni ale waa ni anaaa he tsabaa ji Amelia Earhart laajemɔ.

english: Earhart was an American aviator who became the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic Ocean.
ga: Earhart ji Amerika kɔɔyɔɔŋ lɛlɛ kudɔlɔ ni batsɔɔ yoo klɛŋklɛŋ ni fliki kɛfo Atlantik ŋshɔ lɛ.

english: In 1937, she set out on an around-the-world flight with navigator Fred Noonan.
ga: Yɛ 1937, ekɛ kudɔlɔ ko Fred Noonan tee ni amɛ fa kɛ bɔle jeŋ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: The pair disappeared over the Pacific Ocean on July 2, 1937, and their fate remains unknown.
ga: Mɛi enyɔ lɛ laaje yɛ Pasifik ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ Maawɛɛ 2, 1937, ni ale nɔni fee amɛ.

english: There are many theories about what happened to Earhart and Noonan.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔi babaoo yɛ nɔni fee Earhart kɛ Noonan.

english: Some believe that they crashed into the ocean, while others believe that they were captured by the Japanese.
ga: Mɛi komɛi heɔ amɛ yeɔ akɛ amɛ gbee ŋshɔ lɛ mli, ni mɛi krokomɛi hu heɔ amɛ yeɔ akɛ Japanese bii emɔmɔ amɛ.

english: Still others believe that they deliberately disappeared in order to escape the public eye.
ga: Mɛi komɛi hi heɔ amɛ yeɔ akɛ amɛ jegbɛ amɛ laaje koni maŋ lɛ aka na amɛ.

english: The mystery of Earhart's disappearance has been the subject of books, articles, and documentaries.
ga: Teemɔŋ ni yɔɔ Earhart laajemɔ he lɛ akɛ fee woji, niŋmaa kɛ nilee sini saneyitsei.

english: In 2017, a team of researchers announced that they had found evidence that Earhart's plane crashed on a remote island in the Pacific Ocean.
ga: Yɛ 2017, niiamlitaolɔi tswa adafi akɛ amɛ na odase akɛ Earhart kɔɔyɔɔŋ lɛlɛ lɛ gbeeshi yɛ Pasifik ŋshɔ lɛ mli.

english: Giant wolf spiders are the largest species of arachnid in the world, with some individuals reaching lengths of over 12 inches.
ga: Oblaŋ klaŋ anaanu ji henɔ ni da fe fɛɛ yɛ jeŋ lɛ mli, ni ekomɛi kɛlɛ aafe sɛntimitai 30.4.

english: They are found in tropical rainforests around the world, and are known for their aggressive behavior and venomous bite.
ga: Anaa amɛ yɛ koo ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ mli, ni ale amɛ yɛ amɛ jeŋbaa ni yɔɔ basabasa kɛ amɛ naa pɔizin.

english: Despite their fearsome reputation, giant wolf spiders are actually quite docile creatures.
ga: Yɛ amɛ gbɛi ni asheɔ gbee fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, oblaŋ klaŋ anaanui ji kooloi ni he jɔ.

english: They are not aggressive towards humans unless they are provoked, and their venom is not typically fatal to humans.
ga: Amɛ fee basabasa yɛ gbɔmɔ nɔ bɛja emii ewo la, ni amɛ pɔizin egbee gbɔmɔ.

english: However, their bite can be quite painful, and can cause swelling, redness, and itching.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, kɔɔmɔ shaamɔ waa, ni ebaanyɛ eha ohe efuu, etsu, ni ekɔmɔ.

english: Giant wolf spiders are excellent climbers, and can use their silk to create webs that can reach up to 30 feet in length.
ga: Oblaŋ klaŋ anaanu kɔɔ nii jogbaŋŋ, ni amɛ kɛ amɛ yaa feɔ anaanu ntaŋ ni kakadaŋ shɛɔ mitai 9.

english: They are also very fast runners, and can move at speeds of up to 10 miles per hour.
ga: Amɛ joɔfoi waa hu, ni amɛ baanyɛ jofoi oya kɛyashi kilomitai 16 daa ŋmɛlɛtwsaa.

english: Due to their size, speed, and climbing ability, giant wolf spiders are a popular choice for people who want to experience the thrill of riding a giant arachnid.
ga: Yɛ amɛ dalɛ, oyayai, kɛ bɔni amɛ kɔɔ nii lɛ, Oblaŋ klaŋ anaanui ji halamɔ kɛ ha gbɛmɛi ni yɛ Oblaŋ anaanui tamɔ he miishɛɛ.

english: However, it is important to remember that these creatures are wild animals, and should be treated with respect.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, ehe hia waa akɛ obaa kai akɛ adebɔi lɛ jwɛiaŋ kooloo ji amɛ, ni esa ni abu amɛ.

english: If you are thinking about riding a giant wolf spider, it is important to do your research and make sure that you are properly prepared.
ga: Kɛji osumɔ ni ota oblaŋ blaŋ anaanu, ehe hia ni obaa fee niamlitaomɔ ni okwɛ akɛ oto ohe jogbaŋŋ.

english: You should also make sure that you have the proper equipment, such as a harness and a leash.
ga: Esa ni okwɛ akɛ oyɛ nibii kpakpa, tamɔ harnɛs kɛ kpaa.

english: Once you are properly prepared, you can begin your journey by finding a suitable giant wolf spider.
ga: Kɛji oto ko ohe ojogbaŋŋ lɛ, obaanyɛ ni oje ogbɛfaa lɛ ni otao Oblaŋ klaŋ anaanu ni sa.

english: Once you have found a spider, you can approach it slowly and gently.
ga: Kɛji ona anaanuu lɛ, obaanyɛ ni obɛŋɛ lɛ blɛoo kɛ mlijɔɔ.

english: Once the spider is comfortable with you, you can slowly climb onto its back.
ga: Be ni anaanuu lɛ kɛ bo na miishɛjemɔ lɛ, obaanyɛ ni okɔ ota esɛɛ.

english: Once you are on the spider's back, you can hold on tightly and enjoy the ride.
ga: Be mli oyɛ anaanuu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, obaanyɛ ni omɔ mli waa ni ota kɛ miishɛɛ.

english: The spider will use its silk to create a web that will support you as you ride.
ga: Anaanu lɛ kɛ esiliki feɔ anaanu taŋ ni mɔɔ omli kɛji oota.

english: Riding a giant wolf spider is an unforgettable experience.
ga: Oblaŋ klaŋ anaanu tamɔ ji niiashikpamɔ ni hiɛ kpaaa nɔ.

english: It is a great way to experience the thrill of the wild, and to get up close and personal with one of the world's most fascinating creatures.
ga: Eji gbɛ kpakpa nɔ ni abaakpa nii ashi, ni obɛŋkɛ jeŋ adebɔi ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ waa.

english: Fatima Messaoudi: I'm an actor and a furniture designer. I'm also passionate about flowers, especially those that bloom in the winter.
ga: Fatima Messaoudi: Sini jielɔ kɛ mɔni tsuɔ tsu sɛi ahe nitsumɔ ji mi. Esumɔɔ fɔfɔi waa, titiri no ni gbaa yɛ fɛi mli.

english: Interviewer: What drew you to acting and furniture design?
ga: Sanebilɔ: Meni hani osumɔ sini feemɔ kɛ tsu sɛi ahe nitsumɔ.

english: Fatima Messaoudi: I've always loved performing and creating things.
ga: Fatima Messaoudi: Misumɔɔ sini jiemɔ kɛ nibii bɔɔ.

english: Acting allows me to express myself creatively, and furniture design allows me to use my creativity to make something beautiful and functional.
ga: Sini jiemɔ haa eleɔ bɔni ma wieɔ kɛ hiɛ shi kamɔ, ni tsu mii sɛi ahe nitsumɔ ha ekɛ ehiɛshikamɔ feɔ noko fɛɛfɛo ni tsuɔ nii.

english: Interviewer: What are some of the challenges you've faced as an actor and a furniture designer?
ga: Sanebilɔ: Meni ji naagbai ni ona akɛ moko ni sini jieɔ kɛ sɛi ahe nitsulɔ ni.

english: Fatima Messaoudi: One of the challenges I've faced as an actor is the lack of diversity in the industry.
ga: Fatima Messaoudi: Naagba kome ni ena akɛ sini jielɔ ji gbɛmɛi srɔtoi ni bɛɛɛ sini nitsumɔ lɛ mli.

english: I've often been told that I'm not the right type for a role because of my race or ethnicity.
ga: Bei pii lɛ akɛ mi akɛ amɛ tao moko tamɔ me yɛ sini jiemɔ mii yɛ egbɔmɔtso su loo emaŋ weku mli ni ejɛ hewɔ.

english: As a furniture designer, I've faced the challenge of breaking into a male-dominated industry.
ga: Akɛ tsu mii sɛi anitsulɔ, ena naagba akɛ ebote hii sɔɔ nitsumɔ mli.

english: Interviewer: How have you overcome these challenges?
ga: Sanebilɔ: Te efee tɛŋŋ ni oye naagbai nɛɛ anɔ kunim.

english: Fatima Messaoudi: I've overcome these challenges by working hard and never giving up.
ga: Fatima Messaoudi: Mi ye enɔ kunim kɛ nitsumɔ waa feemɔ ni enijiaŋ ejeee wui.

english: Translation has many benefits, including increasing the relative value of content, improving accessibility, and opening up new markets.
ga: Wiemɔ ashishi tsɔɔmɔ yɛ sɛɛnamɔi babaoo, tamɔ saji ni jara wa ni ya hiɛ, gbɛ ŋmɛɛ hiɛ yaa, kɛ jara ehee gbelemɔ.

english: When content is translated, it becomes accessible to a wider audience, which can lead to increased sales and profits.
ga: Kɛji atsɔɔ same mli lɛ, mɛi babaoo naa he hegbɛ, ni haa jara kɛ sɛɛnamɔ yaa ŋwɛi.

english: In addition, translation can help to build relationships with customers in other countries and cultures.
ga: Kɛ fata he, wiemɔ ashishi tsɔɔmɔ baanyɛ ni eyeɔ ebua naanyo feemɔ kaa nihelɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmaji krokomɛi anɔ kɛ kusumii.

english: By displaying content in multiple languages, businesses can show that they are committed to reaching a global audience.
ga: Kɛ otsɔɔ sane yɛ wiemɔi babaoo mli lɛ, nistumɔi baa tsɔɔ akɛ amɛ yɛ shiwoo akɛ amɛ baa shɛ jeŋbii fɛɛ.

english: This can help to build trust and credibility with potential customers.
ga: Enɛ baa ye ebua ni ana hekɛnɔfɔɔ yɛ nihelɔi ateŋ.

english: Here are some specific examples of how translation has benefited businesses: * A small business that sells handmade jewelry translated its website into Spanish, French, and German.
ga: Naa nɔkwɛmɔnii pɔtɛɛ yɛ bɔni wiemɔ tsɔɔmɔ haa nitsumɔi sɛɛnamɔ: * Nitsumɔ bibioo ko ni hɔɔ jwetri ni akɛ nine fee tsɔɔ ewebsaitii kɛtee Spanish, French, kɛ German wiemɔ mii.

english: As a result, it saw a significant increase in sales from international customers * A large corporation that manufactures medical devices translated its product manuals into multiple languages.
ga: Nɔ ni ejɛ mli eba ji akɛ, ena nihɔɔmɔ ni tee hiɛ waa kɛjɛ nihelɔi mi yɔɔ maŋji anɔ *Nitsumɔ ni feɔ tsofa he tsɔji ni tsɔɔ nibii he woji ewo wiemɔi babaoo mli.

english: This helped to ensure that doctors and nurses in other countries could use the devices safely and effectively * A nonprofit organization that provides humanitarian aid translated its brochures and websites into dozens of languages.
ga: Enɛ yeɔ ebua datrɛfoi kɛ helatsɛmɛi akwɛlɔi ni yɔɔ maŋji krokomɛi anɔ akɛ amɛ baanyɛ ni amɛ kɛ tsɔji lɛ atsu nii shweshweeshwe kɛ ojogbaŋŋ.

english: This helped to reach people in need who would not have otherwise been able to access the organization's resources.
ga: Enɛ ye ebua ni ashɛ mɛi babaoo ni ehia amɛ ni shi kulɛ amɛ nine shɛɛ nitsumɔ lɛ nibii ni jara wa.

english: Translation is a powerful tool that can help businesses to grow and succeed.
ga: Wiemɔ tsɔɔmɔ ji dɛŋdade ni yeɔ ebua nitsumɔi ni eya hiɛ ni eye omanye.

english: This is because we are all created in God's image, and God is the essence of rationality and order.
ga: Ejaakɛ abɔ wɔ fɛɛ yɛ Nyɔŋmɔ subaŋ nɔ, ni Nyɔŋmɔ ji nɔ ni he hia ni jwɛŋmɔ yɔɔ mli kɛ famɔ.

english: When we live in accordance with our true nature, we are able to experience peace and harmony.
ga: Wɔ hiɔ shi yɛ wɔ subaŋ kpakpa diɛtsɛŋ, wɔ nyɛɔ wɔ kpaa ni ashi yɛ hejɔlɛ kɛ ekomefeemɔ.

english: However, when we allow our thoughts and actions to become chaotic and inconsistent, we experience inner conflict and turmoil.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, kɛji wɔ ŋmɛ wɔ jwɛŋmɔ kɛ wɔ nifeemɔ gbɛ ni efee basabasa kɛ ni akpaaa gbee, wɔ na niiashikpamɔ yɛ nɔmɔ kɛ basabasafeemɔ.

english: There are many ways to achieve internal consistency.
ga: Gbɛi babaoo yɛ ni akɛ naa mli gbɛ ni atsaa nɔ daa.

english: One way is to live according to our values.
ga: Gbɛ kome ji ohi shi yɛ nibii ni okpɛlɛɔ gbɛ nɔ.

english: When we know what is important to us and we make choices that are consistent with those values, we feel a sense of purpose and direction.
ga: Kɛji wɔ le nɔ ni hia wɔ ni wɔ fee yiŋkpɛɛ akɛ wɔ baa tsa nɛkɛ nibii ni wɔ kpɛlɛɔ nɔ daa, wɔ naa yiŋtoi kɛ gɛtsɔɔmɔ.

english: Another way to achieve internal consistency is to be honest with ourselves about our strengths and weaknesses.
ga: Gbɛ kroko ni ana mli gbɛ ni atsaa nɔ daa ji wɔ kɛ wɔ he eye anɔwale yɛ wɔ hewalɛ kɛ wɔ gbɔjɔmɔi.

english: When we are aware of our true selves, we can make choices that are in alignment with our authentic nature.
ga: Kɛ wɔ lɛ wɔ be dɛŋtsɛ, wɔ baanyɛ wɔ fee yiŋkpɛɛi ni kɛ wɔ anɔkwale subaŋ feɔ ekome.

english: Of course, achieving internal consistency is not always easy.
ga: Eji anɔkwale akɛ, mli gbɛ ni tsaa nɔ daa ni anaa lɛ ekaashi daa.

english: There will be times when we make mistakes or when we are faced with difficult choices.
ga: Bei baa ba ni wɔ baa tɔ loo ni wɔkɛ yiŋ kpɛɛi ni wa baa kpe.

english: However, if we are willing to strive for consistency, we will eventually find our way back to peace and harmony.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, kɛ wɔ sumɔ ni wɔ na nii ni tsaa nɔ daa lɛ, naagbee lɛ wɔ ku wɔ sɛɛ ni wɔ na toiŋjɔlɛ kɛ ekomefeemɔ.

english: Vimes was having a headache.
ga: Vimes yitsoŋ mii gba lɛ.

english: It was the kind of headache that made you want to tear your hair out, or at least write a strongly worded letter to the makers of whatever it was that had given you the headache in the first place.
ga: Eji yitsoŋgbamɔ ni haa oshɛlɛɔ oyitsɔi, loo ŋmaa wolo ni wiemɔ naa wa kɛha mɛi ni feɔ nibii ni ha oyitsoŋ gba bo kɛjɛ shishi lɛ.

english: In this case, the headache was the result of a particularly trying day at work.
ga: Yɛ sane nɛɛ mli lɛ, yitsoŋgbamɔ lɛ ba kɛjɛ gbi ko nitsumɔ ni kaa shi.

english: Vimes had been investigating a series of robberies, and he was starting to feel like he was getting nowhere.
ga: Vimes miitao juu komɛi amli, ni eboɔ henumɔ namɔ akɛ eshɛɛɛ heko.

english: He was tired, he was frustrated, and he just wanted to go home and sleep for a week.
ga: Etɔ lɛ, eye haomɔ, ni etao ni eya shia ni eya wɔ otsi kome.

english: As he was walking back to his office, Vimes passed a small stationery shop.
ga: Ni eku esɛɛ kɛya enitsumɔhe lɛ, Vimes ho woji hɔɔmɔɔ shwapo ko he.

english: In the window, he saw a sign that said "Best Letters in the City".
ga: Yɛ samflɛ lɛ mii lɛ, ena okadii ko ni kɛɛ “ Woji ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli”.

english: Vimes stopped and stared at the sign for a moment.
ga: Vimes wa ni ekwɛ okadii lɛ bei fioo.

english: He thought about his headache, and he thought about all the letters he had to write.
ga: Ejwɛŋ eyitsoŋgbamɔ lɛ he, ni ejwɛŋ woji fɛɛ ni esane eŋma lɛ he.

english: He sighed and went into the shop.
ga: Eye ŋtsɔidɔɔmɔ ni etee shwapo lɛ mli.

english: The shop was full of all sorts of stationery supplies.
ga: Shwapo lɛ eyi kɛ woji nibii ni ahɔɔ srɔtoi.

english: There were pens, pencils, paper, envelopes, stamps, and even a few typewriters.
ga: Niŋmaa tso, pɛnsil, wolo, wolo kotoku ni asɔ naa, stamp, kɛ taipraita fioo yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: It is true that there exist in this world situations that defy all explanation, events so strange and wondrous that they seem to be the stuff of dreams or nightmares.
ga: Eji anɔkwale akɛ shihilɛi yɛ jeŋ nɛɛ mli ni kɛ saji mlitsɔɔmɔi yeee, nifeemɔi ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ akɛ efeɔ tamɔ lamɔ kɛ lamɔi ni yɔɔ gbeyei.

english: Such is the case with the story I am about to tell you, a tale of supernatural forces and the strange events that unfolded when they were unleashed upon the world.
ga: Nakai ni adesa ni mikɛɛ bo lɛ yɔɔ, adebɔɔ hewalɛ adesa kɛ naakpɛɛ nifeemɔ ni baa kɛji aŋmɛɛ amɛ he awo jeŋ lɛ mli.

english: It all began one night, when a group of friends were gathered together for a party.
ga: Fɛɛ je shishi gbɛkɛ ko, be ni nanemɛi kui komɛi bua amɛ naa kɛha yelikɛnumɔ ko.

english: They were drinking and laughing, enjoying each other's company, when suddenly the lights went out.
ga: Amɛ nuu daa kɛ ŋmɔlɔ, amɛ na am kɛ naanyobɔɔ he miishɛɛ, nɔɔ ni kane lɛ gbo.

english: The room was plunged into darkness, and the only sound was the sound of their own breathing.
ga: Tsu lɛ mii ewo duŋ, ni gbɛɛmɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ ji amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ mumɔ gbɛɛmɔ.

english: Then, in the darkness, they saw it: a strange, glowing light.
ga: Kɛkɛ, yɛ duŋ lɛ mli, amɛ na lɛ: naakpɛɛ kane ni kpɛlɛɔ.

english: It seemed to be coming from nowhere, and it was growing brighter and brighter.
ga: Efee akɛ ejɛɛɛ heko kɛ baaa, ni ekpɛlɛ waa kɛ waa.

english: The friends were terrified, but they were also curious.
ga: Nanemɛi lɛ miishe gbeyee, shi amɛ tao ni amɛ le hu.

english: They wanted to know what this light was, and where it was coming from.
ga: Amɛ tao ni amɛ le meni kane ji enɛ, kɛ he ni ejɛ.

english: Slowly, they approached the light.
ga: Fiofio, amɛ bɛŋkɛ kane lɛ.

english: As they got closer, they could see that it was coming from a small, glowing sphere.
ga: Ni amɛ bɛŋkɛ, amɛ na akɛ ejɛ kokroo bibioo ni kpɛlɛɔ.

english: The sphere was hovering in the air, and it was surrounded by a faint aura.
ga: Kokroo lɛ mii bɔle yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli, ni sui ni naa waa ebɔle he.

english: "Dude, I'm so heartbroken right now. My girlfriend of 2 years just broke up with me."
ga: “Chale, eye awrɛho waa bianɛ nɔɔ. Ejɔle ni ekɛ lɛ yɔɔ afii enyɔ nɛ kɛ mi ekpaa bɔɔ.

english: "What happened?"
ga: “Meni ba?”

english: "I don't know. She just said she wasn't feeling it anymore.
ga: “Eleee. Ekɛɛ ebɛ he henumɔ dɔɔ.

english: I'm so confused.
ga: Eye haomɔ po.

english: I thought we were happy."
ga: Ejwɛ akɛ wɔ yɛ miishɛɛ.”

english: "I'm sorry, man.I know how you feel. Heartbreak sucks."
ga: “Edɔ mi, nuu. Ele bɔ ni onuɔ he ohaa. Tsui kumɔɔ eheee.”

english: "It does. I don't know what to do."
ga: “Eji nakai. Eleee nɔ ni ma fee.”

english: "Just give yourself some time.
ga: “Ha ohe bei fioo.

english: Cry it out if you need to.
ga: Fo kɛji osumɔ.

english: And then, when you're ready, start to move on.
ga: Kɛkɛ, kɛ ofee klalo, jee shishi ni oya nɔ.

english: There are plenty of other fish in the sea."
ga: Yei babaoo yɛ jeŋ lɛ mli.”

english: "I know. But I don't know if I'm ready to date again yet."
ga: “ Ele. Shi eleee kɛji efee klalo ni ma bote gbalashihilɛ mli bianɛ.”

english: "That's okay. You don't have to be ready right away. Just take your time and heal."
ga: “Ehi. Esaaa ni ofeɔ klalo bianɛ. Too otsui shi ni otsa ohe.

english: "Thanks, man. I appreciate it."
ga: “Miida bo shi, nuu. Mihiɛ esɔ he.”

english: "No problem."
ga: “Sane ko bɛɛɛ.”

english: A: Do you think the dowry system is a good thing?
ga: A: Ani ojwɛŋɔ akɛ yookpee nikeenii nifeemɔ lɛ hi lo?

english: B: I don't think so.
ga: B: Ejwɛɛɛ nakai.

english: I think it's a form of discrimination against women.
ga: Ejwɛŋɔ akɛ eji abuɔ yei akɛ mɛi ni esaaa hegbɛ henɔ nii.

english: It puts an unfair financial burden on the bride's family, and it can lead to women being treated as commodities.
ga: Ekɛ shika naagbai ni esaaa fɔɔ yemforo yoo lɛ weku nɔ, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ yei ni afeɔ amɛ nibii aba.

english: A: But some people say that the dowry system is a way to protect women.
ga: A: Shi mɛi komɛi kɛɔ akɛ yookpeemɔ nifeemɔ ji gbɛ nɔ ni abuɔ yei ahe.

english: B: I don't think that's true.
ga: B: Ejwɛɛɛ akɛ anɔkwale ni.

english: In fact, I think it can put women in danger.
ga: Yɛ anɔkwale mli, ejwɛɔ akɛ ebaanyɛ ekɛ yei awo oshara mli.

english: If a woman's family can't afford to pay a dowry, she may be less likely to be able to find a husband.
ga: Kɛji yoo lɛ wekumɛi nyɛɛɛ ni amɛ wo yookpee nifeemɔ nyɔmɔ lɛ, ebaa wa akɛ ebaanyɛ ena wu.

english: And if she does get married, she may be more likely to be abused or mistreated by her husband.
ga: Ni kɛji ebote gbala mli lɛ, eyɛ mii akɛ ewu lɛ baa fee lɛ niseniianifeemɔ.

english: A: So what do you think we should do about the dowry system?
ga: A: Hewɔ meni ojwɛŋɔ ni wɔ fee yɛ yookpee nifeemɔ lɛ he.

english: B: I think we should work to abolish it.
ga: B: Ejwɛŋɔ akɛ wɔ tsunii ni agu lɛ.

english: We should educate people about the harmful effects of the dowry system, and we should support laws that make it illegal to demand or accept a dowry.
ga: Esane wɔ tsɔɔ mɛi anii yɛ naagbaai ni yɔɔ yookpeemɔ nifeemɔ mli, ni wɔ damɔ mlai ni eŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ loo heee yookpee nifeemɔ asɛɛ.

english: A: I agree. I think the dowry system is a relic of a bygone era.
ga: A: Mi kpɛlɛɔ nɔ. Mi jwɛŋɔ akɛ yookpee nifeemɔ ji tsutsu nifeemɔ ne eho.

english: I have been living with type 1 diabetes for over 20 years.
ga: Eyɛ sikili hela henɔ 1 afii nyɔŋmai enyɔ kɛ sɛɛ nɛ.

english: I was diagnosed when I was just 10 years old, and it has been a lifelong journey.
ga: Ana akɛ eyɛ be mli ni eye afii nyɔŋmai, ni efee wala bei amli gbɛfaa.

english: There have been many challenges along the way, but I have also learned a lot about myself and what it means to be a strong, resilient person.
ga: Naagbai babaoo eba yɛ gbɛ nɔ, shi mi hu ekase nibii babaoo yɛ ehe hu, kɛ nɔ ni ji kɛji akɛɛ hewalɛ, shifimɔ gbɔmɔ.

english: One of the biggest challenges I have faced is managing my blood sugar levels.
ga: Naagbai wulu kome ni ena ji sikli ni fa yɛ la mli kwɛmɔ.

english: Diabetes is a condition that affects the way your body turns food into energy.
ga: Sikli hela ji hela ni gbaa bɔni ogbɔmɔtso tsɔɔ niyenii ewoɔ hewalɛ mli.

english: When you eat, your body breaks down the carbohydrates in your food into glucose, which is then absorbed into your bloodstream.
ga: Kɛ oye nii lɛ, ogbɔmɔtso kumɔɔ kabohaidrat ni yɔɔ oniyenii mli ewoɔ glucose, ni ola baa gbala awo emii.

english: Your pancreas releases insulin, a hormone that helps glucose get from your blood into your cells.
ga: Omusuŋ kotoku jieɔ insulin, wala yibii ni yeɔ ebua glucose jɛɔ ola mii kɛ boteɔ wala yibii mli.

english: In people with type 1 diabetes, the pancreas doesn't make enough insulin, or it doesn't make any at all.
ga: Yɛ mɛi ni yɔɔ sikli hela henɔ 1, musuŋ kotoku lɛ efeee insulin babaoo, loo efeee kraa.

english: This means that people with type 1 diabetes have to take insulin injections to help their bodies use glucose for energy.
ga: Enɛ tsɔɔ amɛ miɛ ni yɔɔ sikli hela 1 lɛ esane agbu amɛ insulin ni eye ebua amɛ gbɔmɔtsei ni ekɛ glucose afee hewalɛ.

english: Managing my blood sugar levels can be a tricky business.
ga: Sikli ni fa yɛ ela mii kwɛmɔ baanyɛ efee nii ni tsumɔ baa wa.

english: There are a lot of factors that can affect my blood sugar, including what I eat, how much I exercise, and how much stress I am under.
ga: Nibii babaoo yɛ ni baanyɛ egba sikli ni yɔɔ ela mii naa, fata he ji nɔ ni eyeɔ, kpojiaŋ gbɔlemɔ enyɛ efeɔ, kɛ haomɔ ni etsɔɔ mii.

english: I have to constantly monitor my blood sugar levels and make adjustments to my insulin doses as needed.
ga: Esame ehiŋmɛi ahi esikli ni yɔɔ ela mii nɔ ni ma jaje insulin abɔ ni hia mi.

english: The flavors dance on your tongue, creating a symphony of delight.
ga: ŋma lɛ joɔ yɛ olilɛi nɔ, ni efeɔ ŋɔɔmɔ miishɛɛ.

english: The pineapple is sweet and tart, the apple is crisp and juicy, the stone fruit is juicy and flavorful, and the pear is sweet and refreshing.
ga: Blɔfo ŋme lɛ ŋɔɔ, blɔfo gowa lɛ efee kpeŋkpeŋ kɛ akɔnɔ, tɛ adwuwa lɛ he yɛ akɔnɔ kɛ ŋɔɔmɔ, ni pɛya ŋɔɔ ni hejɔɔmɔ yɛ mli.

english: The flavors are perfectly balanced, and each one complements the others.
ga: ŋɔɔmɔ lɛ yɛ gbɛ kpakpa nɔ, ni eko fɛɛ yeɔ ebua ekrokomɛi.

english: The combination is simply irresistible.
ga: Ekome feemɔ ji nii ni anyɛŋ naa atsi.

english: You can enjoy this delicious fruit salad on its own, or as a topping for yogurt or ice cream.
ga: Obaanyɛ ni oye aduawai saladi ni ŋɔɔ nɛɛ efolo, loo okɛ shwee yogɔt loo ais krim nɔ.

english: It is also a great addition to a summer picnic or potluck.
ga: Eji nɔni hi kɛji akɛ fata latsa bei amli hiɛtserɛjiemɔ loo potluck.

english: No matter how you enjoy it, you are sure to love this fruit salad.
ga: Bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni obaa ye lɛ oya, eyɛ mli akɛ obaa sumɔ nɛkɛ aduawai saladi nɛɛ.

english: A: Did you know that deforestation is one of the leading causes of climate change?
ga: A: Ani ole akɛ koo ahiɛ kpatamɔ ji nɔ titiri ni haa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi eba.

english: B: No, I didn't.
ga: B: Daabi, eleee.

english: How does that work?
ga: Te etsuɔ nii ahaa tɛ?

english: A: Well, when we cut down trees, we're not just destroying the trees themselves.
ga: A: Shi kɛlɛ, kɛji wɔ folɔ tsei, jeee tsei lɛ pɛ wɔ fiteɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: We're also destroying the habitats of countless animals and plants.
ga: Wɔ fite kooloi kɛ tsei babaoo ahii he.

english: And when we lose these habitats, we also lose the benefits that they provide us.
ga: Ni kɛji wɔ laaje nɛkɛ hii hei lɛ, wɔ laajeɔ nyɔmɔwoo ni amɛ kɛ haa wɔ.

english: B: Like what?
ga: B: Tamɔ meni?

english: A: Well, for example, trees help to regulate the climate.
ga: A: Shi kɛlɛ, nɔkwɛmɔnɔ, tsei ni yeɔ ebua kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi.

english: They absorb carbon dioxide from the air and release oxygen.
ga: Amɛ heɔ carbon dioxide kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ejieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni wɔ muɔ.

english: They also help to prevent soil erosion and flooding.
ga: Amɛ yeɔ abua ni haaa nugbɔ ni fɔɔ su lɛ aba kɛ nu afua.

english: And they provide food and shelter for animals.
ga: Ni ehaa kooloi lɛ niyenii kɛ wɔɔhei.

english: B: So deforestation has a lot of negative effects.
ga: B: Hewɔ, koo ahiɛ kpatamɔ yɛ naagbai gbohii babaoo.

english: A: It does.
ga: A: Efeɔ nakai.

english: And it's a problem that's only getting worse.
ga: Ni eji naagba ni ehiii fe fɛɛ.

english: Every year, we lose millions of acres of forest to deforestation.
ga: Daa afi, wɔ shweɔ koo shikpɔŋ akpekpei kɛha koo ahiɛ kpatamɔ.

english: And if we don't do something to stop it, the consequences will be devastating.
ga: Ni kɛji wɔ fee noko ni wɔ kpa lɛ, nɔ ni baa jɛ mli lɛ baa fee gbeyee.

english: B: What can we do to stop it?
ga: B: Meni wɔ baanyɛ ni wɔ fee ni wɔ kpa?

english: A: There are a number of things we can do.
ga: A: Nibii komɛi yɛ ni wɔ baanyɛ ni wɔ fee.

english: We can reduce our demand for wood products.
ga: Wɔ baanyɛ ni wɔ tse nibii ni akɛ tso feo bimɔ nɔ.

english: We can plant trees.
ga: Wɔ baanyɛ ni wɔ du tsei.

english: I was fortunate to attend a school that offered a wide range of AP courses and extracurricular activities, which gave me the opportunity to explore my interests and learn about different career paths.
ga: Duromɔ naa lɛ mi tee skuul ni ha AP nikasemɔi henɔi babaoo kɛ skuul sɛɛ nifemɔi, ni ha mi hegbɛ ni ma kpa emiishɛɛ nii amli ni ma kase nitsumɔ gbɛi srɔtoi.

english: One of the most important things I learned in high school was how to think critically and solve problems.
ga: Noko kome ni he hia fe fɛɛ ni ekase yɛ nɔtsamɔ skuul ji bɔ ni ajwɛŋɔ waa kɛ saji saamɔ.

english: My AP English and math classes taught me how to analyze text and data, and my science classes taught me how to design and conduct experiments.
ga: Mi AP Blɔfo kɛ akɔntabuu klas tsɔɔ mi bɔ ni akpɛɔ niŋmaa kɛ saji, ni mi jeŋ nilee klas tsɔɔ me bɔ ni abɔ ni afeɔ nibii ni aka akwɛɔ.

english: These skills have been essential in my college courses and my career as a software engineer.
ga: Nɛkɛ hesaai nɛɛ he ehia yɛ kɔleji nikasemɔ mii kɛ esoftware tsɔne ahe nitsumɔ.

english: Another important thing I learned in high school was how to work effectively with others.
ga: Noko koŋkro ni he hia ni ekase yɛ nɔtsamɔ skuul ji bɔ ni akɛ tsuɔ nii ojogbaŋŋ.

english: My participation in extracurricular activities such as student government and the debate team taught me how to communicate my ideas clearly and persuasively, and how to work as part of a team to achieve a common goal.
ga: Nikasemɔ sɛɛ nifeemɔi ni efee tamɔ nikaselɔ nɔyeli kɛ ŋwanenjee kui tsɔɔ mi bɔ ni my wie tsɔɔmɔi faŋŋ kɛ mɛi kanemɔ, kɛ bɔ ni atsuɔ nii yɛ kuu mli ni ana otii kome.

english: These skills have been invaluable in my career, where I often have to collaborate with others to solve complex problems.
ga: Nɛkɛ hesaai nɛɛ efee noko ni he hia yɛ enitsumɔ mli, heni ekɛ mɛi krokomɛi feɔ ekome ni wɔ saa saji ni wawai.

english: Finally, my high school experience helped me to develop a strong work ethic and a commitment to excellence.
ga: Naagbee, enɔtsamɔ skuul niiashikpamɔ ye ebua mi ni ena jeŋbaa yɛ nitsumɔ kɛ jogbaŋŋ feemɔ shiwoo.

english: The challenging academic courses I took taught me the importance of hard work and perseverance, and the extracurricular activities I participated in taught me the value of teamwork and dedication.
ga: Nikasemɔ ni wa waa ni ekase tsɔɔ mi bɔ ni nitsumɔ ni wa kɛ hiɛmiamɔ he hia, kɛ nikasemɔ sɛɛ nifeemɔ ni ekɛ ehe wo mli tsɔɔ mi akɛ ekomefeemɔ kɛ henɔjɔɔmɔ he hia.

english: These qualities have helped me to succeed in college and in my career.
ga: Nɛkɛ sui kpakpai lɛ ye ebua mi ni eye omanye yɛ kɔleji kɛɛ enitsumɔ mli.

english: I am grateful for the opportunity to have attended a high school that provided me with such a strong educational foundation.
ga: Mi daashi waa akɛ ena hegbɛ ni ma ya nɔtsamɔ skuul ni ha mi nikasemɔ shishijee ni mii wa.

english: I believe that the skills and knowledge I gained in high school have helped me to become a successful college student and a professional.
ga: Eheɔ eyeɔ akɛ hesaai kɛ nilee ni ena yɛ nɔtsamɔ skuul ye ebuaa me ni efee kɔleji nikaselɔ kɛ nitsulɔ ni ye omanye.

english: Pottery is a craft that involves making objects out of clay.
ga: Shɔɔnii ji ŋaa nifeemɔ ni akɛ su feɔ nibii.

english: Pottery is often used for utilitarian purposes, such as storing food or water, but it can also be used for decorative purposes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛ su tsuɔ nii kɛha nibii ni he hia waa, tamɔ niyenii loo nu ni akɛtoɔ, shi nibii ni akɛwulaa shi hu.

english: The process of making pottery begins with gathering clay.
ga: Shɔɔnii nifeemɔ jieɔ shishi lɛ su naabuamɔ.

english: Clay is a natural material that is found in the ground.
ga: Su ji adebɔɔ nii ko ni anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ.

english: Once the clay has been gathered, it is mixed with water and kneaded until it is soft and pliable.
ga: Kɛ́ abua sũ lɛ naa agbe naa lɛ, akɛ nu futuɔ mli ni ashiɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni efeɔ bɔdɔɔ ni enyɛɔ egbɔjɔɔ.

english: The potter then uses a variety of tools to shape the clay into the desired form.
ga: Nishɔlɔ lɛ kɛ dɛŋdade henɔi shɔɔ su lɛ bɔ ni etaoɔ.

english: Once the clay is shaped, it is dried and fired in a kiln.
ga: Kɛ ashɔ su lɛ ataŋ, eha egbiɔ ni akɛ woɔ la mli yɛ flɔnɔɔ mii.

english: Rainstorms are a common occurrence in many parts of the world, and they can have a significant impact on our lives.
ga: Nugbɔŋtɛi ji nifeemɔ ni fɔɔ baa yɛ jeŋ lɛ hei babaoo, ni amɛ yɛ kadimɔ waa yɛ wɔ wala mli.

english: They can bring much-needed water to parched land, but they can also cause flooding, mudslides, and other damage.
ga: Amɛ baanɛ amɛ kɛ nu abɔ ni he hia ashwe shikpɔŋ ni egbiŋ nɔ, shi amɛ baanyɛ ni amɛ ha nu afua hu aba, gɔŋji ni yiridii, kɛ naagbai krokomɛi.

english: Rainstorms are caused by the rising of warm air, which causes water vapor to condense and form clouds.
ga: Nugbɔŋtɛi baa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mii edɔ tee ŋwɛi, ni haa lamɔ seleɔ ni etsɔɔ atatu.

english: When the water droplets in the clouds become too heavy, they fall as rain.
ga: Kɛji nu kulibii ni yɔɔ atatu lɛ mii shiɔ, ni amɛ nɛɛ akɛ nugbɔ.

english: The amount of rain that falls in a rainstorm is measured in inches.
ga: Asusuɔ nugbɔ abɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nugbɔŋtɛi akɛ inchi.

english: A light rainstorm might produce only a few inches of rain, while a heavy rainstorm can produce over a foot of rain.
ga: Nugbɔŋtɛi ni naa waa baanyɛ ni eha nugbɔi fioo aba, be mli ni nugbɔŋtɛi ni naa wa baanyɛ ni eha nugbɔ babaoo.

english: Rainstorms can have a variety of effects on our lives.
ga: Nugbɔŋtɛi baanyɛ ena naagbai henɔi yɛ wɔ wala mli.

english: They can wash away dirt and debris, making roads and sidewalks impassable.
ga: Amɛ baanyɛ ni amɛ loo muji kɛ jwɛi kɛ ya, ehaaa ni anyɛ atsɔ gbɛjegbɛi kɛ gbɛ ni mɛi fɔɔ nɔ tsɔmɔ nɔ.

english: They can also cause power outages and flooding.
ga: Amɛ baanyɛ ni ekɛ kane gbee kɛ nu afua aba.

english: Flooding can be especially dangerous, as it can quickly sweep away people and property.
ga: Nu afua baanyɛ efee beyeei waa, akɛ ni ebaanɛ ni eloo mɛi kɛ amɛ nibii kɛ ya.

english: Despite the potential dangers, rainstorms can also be beneficial.
ga: Naagbai ni baa fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, nugbɔŋtɛi he baanyɛ ehia.

english: They can help to improve soil quality and water the plants.
ga: Amɛ yeɔ abua koni su kpakpa lɛ etee hiɛ ni wɔ shweɔ nu awo tsei anɔ.

english: Rainstorms can also be a source of entertainment, as people enjoy watching the rain and listening to the thunder.
ga: Nugbɔŋtɛi baanyɛ ni efee miishɛɛ nii, ni mɛi miishɛɛ amɛ he kɛji amɛ kwɛ nugbɔ ni amɛ boɔ nugbɔshimɔ toi.

english: Eyes are complex organs that allow us to see.
ga: Hiŋmɛii ji hwanyaŋ faji ni haa wɔ naa nii.

english: They are located in the front of the head and are protected by the eyelids.
ga: Amɛ yɛ yitso lɛ hiɛ ni hiŋmɛii sɛɛ lɛ buɔ he.

english: Each eye is made up of three layers: the sclera, the choroid, and the retina.
ga: Nihaanɔ etɛ ni ha hiŋmɛi enyɔ fɛɛ nɔ: sclera, choroid, kɛ hiŋmɛi faaji.

english: The sclera is the white part of the eye, the choroid is the dark layer behind the sclera, and the retina is the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye.
ga: Sclera ji hiŋmɛi mli eyɛŋ lɛ, choroid ji haanɔ ediŋ ni yɔɔ sclera sɛɛ gbɛ, ni retina ji haanɔ ni yɔɔ hiŋmɛi sɛɛ gbɛ ni nuɔ kane he.

english: The retina contains millions of light-sensitive cells called rods and cones.
ga: Retina yɛ wala yibii akpekpei ni nuɔ kane he ni atsɛɔ amɛ rods and cones.

english: Rods are responsible for night vision, while cones are responsible for color vision.
ga: Rods agbɛnaa nii ji gbɛkɛ nii naa, be mli ni cones gbɛnaa nii ji kɔla nii naa.

english: When light hits the retina, it is converted into electrical signals that are sent to the brain via the optic nerve.
ga: Kɛji kane gbee retina nɔ lɛ, etsakeɔ lɛ ewoɔ elɛtrik aflaŋaa ni akɛ yaa jwɛŋmɔ lɛ kɛ tsɔɔ ɔptik nɛɛv mli.

english: My family has always kept animals.
ga: Mi weku elɛ koolooi daa.

english: When I was a child, we had a dog, a cat, and a few fish.
ga: Beni gbekɛ ji mi lɛ, wɔ yɛ gbee, alɔnte, lɛ loo fioo.

english: As I got older, we added a few more animals to the mix, including a rabbit, a guinea pig, and a hamster.
ga: Ni ebɔi daa lɛ, wɔ kɛ koolooi fioo ba fata he, kpɛŋkpɛlɛ, kwakwei, kɛ hamsta

english: I loved taking care of all of our animals and learning about their different needs.
ga: Mi sumɔɔ wɔ koolooi lɛ fɛɛ ni ekaseɔ amɛ hiamɔ nii srɔtoi.

english: One of my favorite animals that we ever kept was a rabbit named Cocoa.
ga: Kooloo kome ni esumɔɔ fe fɛɛ ni wɔ lɛɛɛ ji kpɛŋkpɛlɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Cocoa.

english: Cocoa was a brown and white Holland Lop rabbit.
ga: Cocoa ji braun kɛ eyɛŋ Holland Lop kpɛŋkpɛlɛ ko.

english: She was the sweetest animal I've ever met and she loved to be cuddled.
ga: Lɛ ji kooloo ni yɔɔ miishɛɛ ni ena ni esumɔɔ ni akɛ lɛ eshɛ.

english: She was also very smart and could learn tricks like sit, stay, and come.
ga: Ehe esa waa hu ni enyɛɔ ekaseɔ ŋaa gbɛi tamɔ shitaramɔ, shihilɛ, kɛ ba.

english: One day, I was playing with Cocoa in the backyard when I noticed that she was chewing on something.
ga: Gbi ko lɛ, mi kɛ Cocoa shwɛ yɛ tsu lɛ sɛɛ ni ena akɛ eekpe noko.

english: I went over to investigate and saw that she was chewing on a piece of fiber from one of our clothes.
ga: Etee ni eya kwɛ nibii amli ni ena akɛ eekpe faiba ko ni jɛ wɔ taadei lɛ amli.

english: I took the fiber away from her and showed it to my mom.
ga: Ehe faiba lɛ kɛjɛ edɛŋ ni ekɛ tsɔɔ enyɛ.

english: My mom explained that rabbits need to eat fiber in order to digest their food properly.
ga: Enɛ gbala mii etsɔɔ mi akɛ ehia akɛ kpɛŋkpɛlɛ baa ye faiba koni amɛ nyɛ amɛ gbɛlɛ amɛ niyenii ojogbaŋŋ.

english: She said that we should give Cocoa some hay to eat, which is a good source of fiber.
ga: Ekɛɛ wɔ ha Cocoa jwɛi gbiŋ koni eye, ni ji faiba ni hii waa.

english: I gave Cocoa some hay and she loved it!
ga: Eha Cocoa jwɛi gbiŋ eko ni esumɔɔ!

english: An earthquake is a sudden and violent shaking of the Earth's crust that can cause great damage.
ga: Shikpɔŋwosomɔ ji noko fɔŋŋ ni baa trukaa ni naa wa ni baanyɛ afite nibii babaoo.

english: The most common cause of earthquakes is the movement of tectonic plates, which are large pieces of the Earth's crust that ride on top of the molten rock beneath the surface.
ga: Nɔ ni haa shikpɔŋhosomɔ baa fe fɛɛ ji tectonic plates he tsimɔ, ni ji shikpɔŋ mli he nii agboi ni nyiɛ tɛi ni ashwie ni yɔɔ shishi gbɛ.

english: When these plates move past or collide with each other, they can cause the Earth's crust to break and produce seismic waves.
ga: Be ni plɛtei nɛɛ tsi amɛ he loo amɛ kɛ amɛ he shi, ebaa ha ni Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akuu ni ekɛ yiwaa ko baa.

english: These waves travel through the Earth and can cause the ground to shake.
ga: Nɛkɛ yiwaa nɛɛ faa gbɛ kɛtsɔɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa ehosoɔ.

english: The magnitude of an earthquake is measured on the Richter scale, which ranges from 0 to 9.
ga: Asusuɔ shikpɔŋhosomɔ miitsiimɔ yɛ Richter scale nɔ, ni kɛjɛ 0 kɛyashi 9.

english: The higher the magnitude, the more powerful the earthquake.
ga: Be ni emii tsii waa, etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋhosomɔ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ waa.

english: Earthquakes can cause damage in a variety of ways, including ground shaking, landslides, tsunamis, building collapses, fires, and loss of life.
ga: Shikpɔŋhosomɔ kɛ naagbai baa yɛ gbɛ henɔi babaoo, tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni hoso, gɔŋji ni kumɔ eshwieɔ shi, tsunamis, tsui ni kumɔ, la, kɛ wala ni ashwee.

english: Earthquakes can also trigger other hazards, such as avalanches.
ga: Shikpɔŋhosomɔi nyɛɔ ekɛ gbeyei nii krokomɛi, tamɔ snoo ni kumɔ.

english: The damage caused by an earthquake depends on a number of factors, including the magnitude of the earthquake, the distance from the epicenter, the type of soil, and the construction of buildings.
ga: Naagbai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋhosomɔi amli damɔ nibii komɛi anɔ, tamŋ emiitsiimɔ, bɔ ni ekɛ epicenter jɛkɛ, su henɔ, kɛ tsu maa.

english: You have no idea how the real world works, and you think that everything should be handed to you on a silver platter.
ga: Oleee bɔ ni jeŋ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ tsuɔ nii, ni ojwɛŋɔ akɛ afee nɔ fɛɛ nɔ aha bo.

english: You're always complaining about something, and you never seem to be happy with anything.
ga: Owieɔ huhuuhu yɛ nɔ ko he be fɛɛ be, ni etamɔ nɔ ni omii shɛɛɛ ohe yɛ nɔ ko he kɔkɔɔkɔ.

english: You're a bunch of entitled brats, and I'm sick of it.
ga: Nyɛ ji gbekɛbii ni efite, ni etɔ mi yɛ he.

english: Grow up.
ga: Feemɔ onukpa.

english: The world doesn't owe you anything.
ga: Jeŋ lɛ ehiɛɛɛ bo nyɔmɔwoo ko.

english: You have to work hard to get what you want.
ga: Esane otsu nii waa koni ona nɔni osumɔɔ.

english: There's no such thing as a free lunch.
ga: Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ ehe nyɔmɔwoo.

english: If you want something, you have to go out and earn it.
ga: Kɛji osumɔ noko, esane oje kpo ni otsu ni ona.

english: Stop whining and complaining.
ga: Kpa tɔkemɔ kɛ huuhuufeemɔ.

english: It's not going to get you anywhere.
ga: Ekɛ bo eyaaa he ko.

english: If you have a problem, then solve it.
ga: Kɛji oyɛ sane lɛ, bɛ saamɔ lɛ.

english: Don't just sit around and cry about it.
ga: Kaa tashi ni ofo yɛ hɛ.

english: Be more mature.
ga: Feemɔ dalɛ nii.

english: Act your age.
ga: Fee onii tamɔ afii abɔ ni oye.

english: You're not children anymore.
ga: Jeee gbekɛbii ji nyɛ dɔɔŋ.

english: It's time to start acting like adults.
ga: Bei eshɛ ni abaa fee nii tamɔ onukpai.

english: I'm tired of dealing with your childish behavior.
ga: Etɔ mi kɛ ogbekɛbii asubaŋ feemɔi.

english: If you don't start acting like adults, then I'm going to have to cut you out of my life.
ga: Kɛji ojeee shishi ni ofee onii tamɔ Onukpa lɛ, bɛ mii ba ma fo bo kɛjɛ ewala mli.

english: I don't have time for your nonsense.
ga: Ebɛɛɛ bei kɛha obuulu anifeemɔ.

english: Grow up and start acting like adults, or I'm out of here.
ga: Daa ni ofee onii tamɔ onukpa, loo mii shi biɛnɛ.

english: I was recently cleaning out my attic when I came across a box of old recipes that had been passed down from my grandmother.
ga: Etsɛ ko tsɔ ni mii tsumɔ attik mli ni ena adeka ni niyenii hoomɔi gbɛtsɔɔmɔi emomo yɔɔ mli ni jɛ enaa nɔ.

english: Some of them were quite old, dating back to the early 1900s.
ga: Ekomɛi etsɛ waa, kɛya 1900s mra sɛɛ gbɛ.

english: I was curious to see what they were, so I started reading through them.
ga: Mi tao ni ma na nɔni ji, hewɔ bɔŋ amɛ kanemɔ.

english: One recipe in particular caught my eye.
ga: Ekome ni yɔɔ mii mɔ ehiŋmɛii.

english: It was for an anti-aging facial mask made with honey, yogurt, and oatmeal.
ga: Eji hiɛ haanɔ ŋku ni kpaa dalɛ ni akɛ wuo, yogɔt, kɛ oats fee.

english: I decided to give it a try, and I was amazed at the results!
ga: Efee akɛ bɔmɔdɛŋ ma fee, ni sɛɛnamɔ fee mi naakpɛɛ.

english: My skin looked so much smoother and younger after using it.
ga: Eheloo efee fɛo ni efee tamɔ gbekɛ ni ekɛ kpa ehiɛ sɛɛmii.

english: I'm so glad I found this old recipe.
ga: Ena miishɛɛ akɛ ena resipi nɛɛ.

english: It's a real treasure, and I'm sure it will remain in my family for many years to come.
ga: Eji nii kpakpa diɛŋtsɛ, ni ele akɛ ebaa hi weku lɛ mii afii babaoo ni baaba.

english: The veteran sat alone in the hospital room, staring at the blank television.
ga: Asrafonyo lɛ ta helatsamɔhe tsu lɛ mli, eekwɛ tɛlɛvisin ni asuuu ko.

english: He had been in the hospital for weeks, and he was starting to go stir-crazy.
ga: Ehi helatsamɔhe lɛ otsii babaoo, ni eebɔi sɛkɛ yeli.

english: He had been in a lot of wars, and he had seen a lot of death and destruction.
ga: Etee tawuu babaoo mii, ni ena gbelei kɛ nifitemɔ babaoo.

english: But nothing had ever prepared him for this.
ga: Shi noko etooo lɛ aha enɛ.

english: The door to his room opened, and a young woman walked in.
ga: Etsu shinaa gbele, ni oblayoo ko bote mii.

english: She was carrying a bouquet of flowers. "Hello," she said. "My name is Sarah.
ga: Ehiɛ fɔfɔi kuu. “Miiŋa bo,” ekɛɛ. “Egbɛi ji Sarah.

english: I'm a volunteer here at the hospital."
ga: Mii ji mɔni kɛ ehe eha yɛ helatsamɔhe nɛɛ.”

english: The veteran smiled. "It's nice to meet you, Sarah," he said.
ga: Asrafonyo onukpa lɛ fee ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. “Eŋɔɔ enaa akɛ ena bo, Sarah,” ekɛɛ.

english: "What are you doing here?"
ga: “Meni ofeeɔ yɛ biɛnɛ?”

english: "I'm here to make you laugh," she said. "Laughter is the best medicine, you know."
ga: “Eyɛ biɛ ni maha ni oŋmɔ,” ekɛɛ. “ŋmɔlɔ ji tsofa ni hi fe fɛɛ, ole.”

english: The veteran laughed. "I'm not sure I can laugh," he said.
ga: Asrafonyo onukpa lɛ ŋmɔ. “Ebɛɛɛ nɔmina akɛ manyɛ ma ŋmɔ,” ekɛɛ.

english: "I've been through a lot."
ga: “Etsɔ nibii babaoo mii.”

english: "I know," Sarah said. "But I'm going to make you laugh."
ga: “Ele,” Sarah kɛɛ. “Shi ma ha ni oŋmɔ.”

english: And she did.
ga: Ni efee.

english: She told jokes and stories, and she even did some magic tricks.
ga: Ekɛɛ shwɛmɔi kɛ adesai, ni efee majik ŋaa komɛi hu.

english: The veteran laughed until his sides hurt.
ga: Asrafonyo onukpa lɛ ŋmɔ kɛyashi emasɛi mii waa ehe.

english: New Study Finds That Breast Cancer Screenings Can Lead to False Positives
ga: Ni Kasemɔ Ehe Na Akɛ Fufɔ Mli Kansa he niiamlikpɛmɔ Nyɛɔ Efeɔ Amale Kpakpa.

english: A new study published in the journal JAMA Internal Medicine has found that breast cancer screenings can lead to false positives.
ga: Nikasemɔ hee ko ni akala awo wolo tɛtrɛɛ ni ji JAMA Internal Medicine lɛ mli lɛ ena akɛ, kɛ́ mɔ ko kwɛ nu mli kansa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ana akɛ eyɛ kansa yɛ amale mli.

english: The study, which was conducted by researchers at the University of California, San Francisco, found that one in five women who underwent a mammogram had a false positive result.
ga: Nikasemɔ lɛ, niiamlitaolɔi ni yɔɔ Califonia, San Francisco, na akɛ yɛ yei enumɔ mii lɛ ekome ni fee fɔfɔ kotoku mii mfoniri na amale kpakpa sɛɛnamɔ.

english: A false positive result is when a mammogram shows that a woman has breast cancer, when she actually does not.
ga: Amale kpakpa sɛɛnamɔ ji kɛji fɔfɔ kotoku mii mfoniri tsɔɔ akɛ yoo yɛ fɔfɔ kansa lɛ, be mli ni ebɛɛɛ eko.

english: This can lead to unnecessary anxiety and stress, as well as unnecessary medical procedures, such as biopsies.
ga: Enɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ basabasafeemɔ kɛ tɔlɛ ni he hiaa baa, kɛ tsofa tsamɔ gbejianɔi hu ni he ehiaa, tamɔ wala yibii amli kwɛmɔ.

english: The study found that the rate of false positives was higher among women who were younger, had dense breasts, and had a family history of breast cancer.
ga: Nikasemɔ lɛ na amale kpakpa abɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi yɛ oblayei, ni amɛ fɔfɔ miitsii, ni amɛ yɛ fɔfɔ kansa yɛ weku yinɔsane mii.

english: The researchers say that these findings are important because they highlight the need for women to understand the risks and benefits of breast cancer screening before they decide whether or not to undergo a mammogram.
ga: Niiamlitaolɔi lɛ kɛɛ akɛ nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ he hia ejaakɛ emaa hiamɔ ni yɔɔ mii kɛɛha yei ni nuɔ naagbai yɛ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ fɔfɔ kotoku mii akwɛmɔ dani amɛ fee amɛ jwɛŋmɔ kɛji amɛ baa fee loo daabi.

english: The study also found that the use of sound waves, known as ultrasound, to screen for breast cancer can help to reduce the number of false positives.
ga: Nikasemɔ lɛ hu na akɛ anyɛɔ akɛ gbɛmɔkei, ni atsɛɔɔ lɛ ultrasound, ekwɛ fɔfɔ kansa mii ni eye ebua ni amale kpakpa aba shi.

english: Ultrasound is a safe and non-invasive imaging technique that can be used to identify abnormalities in the breast.
ga: Ultasound ji mfonirifeemɔ gbɛ ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ehii kwraa ni abaanyɛ akɛtsu nii ni akɛyoo nɔ ko ni ejaaa yɛ nu mli.

english: A typical day for a person in Nigeria might start with a cup of tea or coffee and a breakfast of bread, eggs, and plantains.
ga: Gbi ko ni mɔ ko yeɔ yɛ Nigeria lɛ baanyɛ aje shishi kɛ tii loo kɔfe kɛ leebi niyenii ni ji bloodo, wɔji, kɛ amadaŋ.

english: The workday typically starts around 8am and ends around 5pm, with a lunch break in the middle of the day.
ga: Nitsumɔ gbi lɛ jeɔ shishi leebi aaafee leebi ŋmɛji kpaanyɔ ni egbeɔ naa aaafee shwane ŋmɛji enumɔ, kɛ shwane niyeli hejɔɔmɔ yɛ mli yɛ gbi lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: After work, people might relax at home with their families, go out to dinner, or attend a cultural event.
ga: Kɛ agbe nitsumɔ naa lɛ, gbɛmɛi baanyɛ ajɔɔ amɛhe yɛ shia kɛ amɛ wekui, amɛ yaa gbɛkɛ niyeli, loo amɛ yaa kusum nifeemɔ ko.

english: The evening is often spent socializing with friends and family.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ayeɔ gbɛkɛ be lɛ kɛ nanemɛi kɛ wekumɛi.

english: The daily routine of a Nigerian can vary depending on their location and lifestyle.
ga: Anagonyo daa gbi nifeemɔi baanyɛ atsake yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ kɛ amɛshihilɛ gbɛ nɔ.

english: In rural areas, people may wake up earlier to tend to their farms or livestock.
ga: Yɛ akrowai amli lɛ, mɛi baanyɛ ate shi mra koni amɛkwɛ amɛ ŋmɔji loo kooloi.

english: In urban areas, people may have more time for leisure activities.
ga: Yɛ maŋ wuji amli lɛ, gbɛmɛi baanyɛ ana be babaoo kɛha hiɛtserɛjiemɔ nifeemɔi.

english: However, some aspects of daily life are common across Nigeria, such as the importance of family and community.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, daa gbi shihilɛ mli nibii komɛi ji nɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ yɛ Nigeria fɛɛ, tamɔ bɔ ni weku kɛ akutso he hiaa ha.

english: Nigeria is a diverse country with a rich culture, and the daily lives of its people reflect this diversity.
ga: Nigeria ji maŋ ni srɔtoi yɔɔ mli ni kusumii babaoo yɔɔ mli, ni emli bii lɛ ashihilɛ jieɔ srɔtofeemɔ nɛɛ kpo.

english: From the bustling cities of Lagos and Abuja to the more rural areas of the country, there is no one-size-fits-all description of what a typical day in Nigeria is like.
ga: Kɛjɛ Lagos kɛ Abuja maji ni yɔɔ hoo lɛ amli kɛyashi maŋ lɛ akrowai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli lɛ, no ko bɛ ni tsɔɔ bɔ ni gbi ko ni afɔɔ feemɔ yɛ Nigeria lɛ ji.

english: But one thing is for sure: no matter where you are in Nigeria, you will find people who are warm, welcoming, and eager to share their culture with you.
ga: Shi no kome ji nɔ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ: he fɛɛ he ni oyɔɔ yɛ NIgeria lɛ, obaana mɛi ni yɔɔ miishɛɛ, ni hereɔ bo hiɛmɛɛ, ni miisumɔ waa ni amɛkɛ bo agba amɛ kusum he sane.

english: The Nyasaland African Congress (NAC) was founded in 1944 by Dr. Hastings Kamuzu Banda and other Malawian nationalists.
ga: Dr. Hastings Kamuzu Banda kɛ Malawi maŋhedɔɔ he mɛi krokromɛi to Nyasaland Afrikabii Akuu lɛ shishi yɛ afi 1944 mli.

english: The NAC was the first political party in Malawi to advocate for African independence from British colonial rule.
ga: NAC ji maŋkwramɔŋ kuu klɛŋklɛŋ ni yɔɔ Malawi ni fi Afrika heyeli kɛjɛ Britania maŋkwramɔŋ nɔyeli shishi.

english: In 1953, the NAC was banned by the British colonial authorities, but it continued to operate underground.
ga: Yɛ 1953 mli lɛ, Britania nɔyeli lɛ tsi NAC lɛ naa, shi etee nɔ etsu nii yɛ teemɔŋ.

english: In 1961, the NAC was legalized and renamed the Malawi Congress Party (MCP).
ga: Yɛ afi 1961 lɛ, aha NAC lɛ wo mla shishi, ni atsɛ lɛ Malawi Congress Party (MCP).

english: The MCP won the first general elections held in Malawi in 1964, and Dr. Banda became the first Prime Minister of Malawi.
ga: MCP lɛ ye kunim yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ oshikifɔɔ ni afee yɛ Malawi yɛ afi 1964 lɛ mli, ni Dr. Banda bafee Malawi maŋsɔɔlɔ nukpa klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: In 1966, Malawi became a republic, with Dr. Banda as the first President.
ga: Yɛ afi 1966 lɛ, Malawi batsɔ maŋ ni yeɔ nɔ, ni Dr. Banda ji klɛŋklɛŋ maŋ onukpa.

english: Dr. Banda ruled Malawi as a one-party state for 30 years.
ga: Dr. Banda ye Malawi nɔ akɛ kuu kome maŋ afii 30 sɔŋŋ.

english: He was a controversial figure, but he is also credited with modernizing Malawi and bringing it independence.
ga: Eji mɔko ni ŋwanejee yɔɔ he, shi akɛ yijiemɔ hu haa lɛ akɛ ekɛ Malawi fee ŋɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ nɔ ni ekɛ heyeli ba.

english: The physicians, who are members of the Southern Medical Association, say that the firm's building was not properly ventilated and that the employees were exposed to harmful chemicals.
ga: Datrɛfoi lɛ, ni ji Southern Medical Association lɛ mli bii lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ nitsumɔhe lɛ tsu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ, ni nitsulɔi lɛ kɛ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui kpeɔ.

english: "We were concerned about the health of the employees at this firm," said Dr. Raymond Neal-Kennedy, a spokesman for the SMA.
ga: Dr. Raymond Neal-Kennedy, ni ji SMA lɛ najiaŋdmɔlɔ lɛ kɛɛ akɛ: "Wɔhao yɛ nitsulɔi ni yɔɔ nitsumɔhe nɛɛ hewalɛ he."

english: "The building was not up to code and the employees were being exposed to dangerous chemicals. We had no choice but to shut the firm down."
ga: "Tsu lɛ kɛ mlai lɛ kpaaa gbee ni nitsulɔi lɛ kɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara miitsu nii. Wɔbɛɛɛ nɔ ko ni wɔbaafee akɛ ja wɔŋa nitsumɔhe lɛ."

english: The architecture firm, which has not been named, has denied the allegations.
ga: Tsumaa nitsumɔhe ni atsɛko amɛgbɛi lɛ ekpoo naagbai ni awieɔ ashiɔ amɛ lɛ.

english: The firm's owner, Mr. Ishq Kasawa, says that the building was properly ventilated and that the employees were not exposed to any harmful chemicals.
ga: Nitsumɔhe lɛ nuŋtsɔ, Mr. Ishq Kasawa kɛɛ akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ tsu lɛ mli, ni tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ko kwraa bɛ nitsulɔi lɛ amli.

english: "We are disappointed by the actions of the SMA," said Mr. Kasawa.
ga: "Wɔnijiaŋjewui yɛ SMA lɛ nifeemɔi lɛ ahe," Mr. Kasawa kɛɛ.

english: "We believe that we have been unfairly targeted. Our building is safe and our employees are healthy."
ga: "Wɔheɔ wɔyeɔ akɛ atswa wɔ ojo yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Wɔ tsu lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni wɔ nitsulɔi lɛ hu yɛ hewalɛ."

english: The SMA says that it will continue to investigate the matter and that it will take further action if necessary.
ga: SMA lɛ kɛɛ akɛ ebaaya nɔ ekpɛi sane lɛ mli, ni ebaatsu he nii kɛ ehe miihia.

english: The Libyan Civil War is an ongoing armed conflict in Libya that began in 2011 with the overthrow of Muammar Gaddafi's government.
ga: Libya maŋ ta lɛ ji tawuu nii ni yaa nɔ yɛ Libya ni je shishi yɛ afi 2011 kɛ Muammar Gaddafi nɔyeli lɛ shigbeemɔ.

english: After the fall of Tripoli, the Libyan National Transitional Council (NTC) proclaimed the establishment of the Libyan Interim Government, but the country descended into a state of lawlessness with two rival governments, the NTC and the Libyan National Army (LNA), and a number of militias vying for power.
ga: Beni Tripoli shigbeemɔ sɛɛ lɛ, Libya Maŋ Tsakemɔ Kuu lɛ jaje akɛ ato Libya Be-Fɛɛ Nɔyeli lɛ shishi, shi maŋ lɛ ba shi kɛtee mlakwamɔ shihilɛ mli ni nɔyeli enyɔ ni kɛ amɛhe wuɔ ta, NTC kɛ Libya Maŋ Asraafoi lɛ, kɛ asraafoi akui babaoo ni miitao nɔyeli hegbɛ lɛ yɔɔ mli.

english: In 2014, the Libyan House of Representatives (HoR) was elected in the eastern city of Tobruk, but the HoR has been unable to exercise effective control over the country.
ga: Yɛ afi 2014 lɛ, ahala Libya Najiaŋ damɔlɔi Akuu lɛ yɛ Tobruk maŋ lɛ bokagbɛ, shi HoR lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye maŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: In 2016, the Government of National Accord (GNA) was formed in Tripoli under the auspices of the United Nations, but the GNA has been unable to gain control of the country's eastern regions.
ga: Yɛ afi 2016 lɛ, ato maŋ nɔyeli ni ji National Accord lɛ shishi yɛ Tripoli yɛ Jeŋmaji Ekomefeemɔ lɛ shishi, shi GNA lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye maŋ lɛ bokagbɛ kpokpai lɛ anɔ.

english: The LNA, led by Khalifa Haftar, has been fighting against the GNA and its allies in the west of the country.
ga: LNA ni Khalifa Haftar nyiɛɔ hiɛ lɛ kɛ GNA kɛ ehefatalɔi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ anaigbɛ lɛ ewuu.

english: The conflict has led to a humanitarian crisis, with hundreds of thousands of people displaced from their homes.
ga: Tawuu lɛ kɛ adesai ayelikɛbuamɔ he naagba eba, ni gbɔmɛi akpei ohai abɔ eshi amɛshiai amli.

english: The United Nations has called for an immediate ceasefire and the start of a political dialogue.
ga: Jeŋmaji Ekomofeemɔ lɛ etsɛ koni akpa tutswaa amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni aje maŋkwramɔŋ sanegbaa shishi.

english: The soap opera centers around the lives of the residents of a small town.
ga: Soap opera lɛ kɔɔ maŋ bibioo ko mli bii ashihilɛ he.

english: The main character, Constance, is a young woman who is struggling to come to terms with the recent death of her husband.
ga: Mɔ titri ni awieɔ ehe yɛ mli lɛ, Constance ji oblayoo ko ni miitao ni ekɛ ewu ni gbo nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ atsu nii.

english: She is left to raise her two young children on her own, and she is struggling to find a way to handle her grief.
ga: Eshi koni eyatsɔse ebii bibii enyɔ lɛ yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ, ni eebɔmɔdɛŋ ni ena gbɛ etsɔɔ nɔ etsuɔ awerɛho ni eyɔɔ lɛ he nii.

english: One day, Constance meets a man named Frederick at the grocery store.
ga: Gbi ko lɛ, Constance kɛ nuu ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Frederick kpe yɛ shwapo ko mli.

english: Frederick is a kind and compassionate man, and he offers Constance his support.
ga: Frederick ji nuu ni mli hi ni musuŋ tsɔɔ lɛ, ni ekɛ esɛɛ fimɔ haa Constance.

english: Constance begins to develop feelings for Frederick, but she is hesitant to start a new relationship because she is still grieving the loss of her husband.
ga: Constance je henumɔi naa eha Frederick, shi eshashaoo akɛ ebaaje wekukpaa he shishi ejaakɛ eeye ewu ni gbo lɛ awerɛho lolo.

english: Eventually, Constance decides to give Frederick a chance.
ga: Yɛ naagbee lɛ, Constance kpɛ eyiŋ akɛ ebaaha Frederick hegbɛ.

english: She starts dating him, and she quickly falls in love with him.
ga: Ebɔi lɛ nyiɛmɔ, ni eba sumɔ lɛ oya.

english: Frederick helps Constance to heal from her grief, and he gives her the strength to raise her children on her own.
ga: Frederick bua Constance ni etsaa awerɛho ni eyɔɔ lɛ, ni eha hewalɛ ni ekɛtsɔse ebii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Constance and Frederick get married, and they have a happy life together.
ga: Constance kɛ Frederick bote gbalashihilɛ mli, ni amɛfee ekome kɛhi shi yɛ miishɛɛ mli.

english: They raise their children together, and they support each other through good times and bad.
ga: Amɛ tsɔse amɛ gbɛkɛbii lɛ ekome, ni amɛ wa amɛ he kɛ tsɔ bei ni hi kɛ bei ni ehiii fɛɛ mli.

english: Constance is grateful for Frederick's love and support, and she knows that she will never be able to thank him enough for everything he has done for her.
ga: Constance miidashi eha Frederick suɔmɔ kɛ esɛɛ nyiɛmɔ, ni ele akɛ enyɛɛɛ eda lɛ shi bɔ ni sa ha nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni efee eha lɛ.

english: The soap opera ends with a message of hope.
ga: Soap opera lɛ gbeɔ naa kɛ hiɛnɔkamɔ sane.

english: As the twentieth century drew to a close, computers and electronics were becoming increasingly intertwined.
ga: Beni afii ohai 20 lɛ miiba naagbee lɛ, kɔmpiutai kɛ tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tsɔne mli lɛ mifee ekome babaoo.

english: In the early days of computing, these two fields were largely separate.
ga: Yɛ kɔmpiuta he nitsumɔ shishijee gbii lɛ amli lɛ, nɛkɛ nitsumɔi enyɔ nɛɛ amli este amɛhe babaoo.

english: Computers were large, expensive machines that were used for scientific and military purposes.
ga: Kɔmpiutai ji tsɔnei wuji ni jara wa ni akɛtsuɔ jeŋ nilee kɛ asraafoi anitsumɔi ahe nii.

english: Electronics were used in a variety of consumer products, such as radios, televisions, and telephones.
ga: Akɛ elɛtrɔnik nibii tsu nii yɛ nibii srɔtoi ni mɛi yeɔ lɛ amli, tamɔ redio, tɛlɛvishiŋ, kɛ tɛlifoŋ.

english: However, as computers became smaller and more affordable, they began to be used in a wider variety of applications.
ga: Shi beni kɔmpiutai lɛ bafee bibii ni amɛjara hu waaa lɛ, akɛ amɛ bɔi nitsumɔ yɛ nibii srɔtoi babaoo amli.

english: This led to a blurring of the lines between computers and electronics.
ga: Enɛ ha srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ kɔmpiutai kɛ tsɔnei ateŋ lɛ bafee mlɛo.

english: One of the most significant developments in the history of computers and electronics was the invention of the personal computer (PC).
ga: Nɔ kome ni sa kadiɔmɔ waa yɛ Kɔmpiutai kɛ tsɔnei ahe yinɔsane mli ji mɔ diɛŋtsɛ kɔmpiutai ni afee.

english: The PC was first introduced in the 1970s, and it quickly became a popular tool for both personal and business use.
ga: Ajie PC lɛ kpo klɛŋkɛŋ kwraa yɛ 1970 afii lɛ amli, ni oya nɔŋŋ lɛ ebatsɔ dɛŋ dade ni ale waa kɛha aŋkroaŋkroi kɛ jarayeli nitsumɔi fɛɛ.

english: PCs were originally designed for use in homes and offices, but they soon found their way into other settings, such as schools and libraries.
ga: Shishijee lɛ, afee PC koni akɛtsu nii yɛ shiai kɛ nitsumɔhei, shi etsɛɛɛ ni amɛna gbɛ kɛtee hei krokromɛi, tamɔ skul kɛ wojiatoohei.

english: The PC's portability and versatility made it an ideal tool for a wide range of tasks, from word processing to gaming.
ga: PC lɛ ni akɛyaa he fɛɛ he kɛ bɔ ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii yɛ srɔtoi lɛ ha efee dɛŋdade ni hi ojogbaŋŋ kɛha nitsumɔi srɔtoi, kɛjɛ wiemɔi ahe nitsumɔ nɔ kɛyashi shwɛmɔ nɔ.

english: The development of the PC also led to the development of a new industry: the software industry.
ga: PC lɛ feemɔ hu ha nitsumɔhe hee ko ba: tsɔne ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ sɔftwɛɛ nitsumɔhe lɛ.

english: Software companies created programs that could run on PCs, and these programs quickly became essential tools for PC users.
ga: Sɔftwɛɛ nitsumɔhei fee gbɛjianɔtoi ni baanyɛ atsu niii yɛ PC nɔ, ni nɛkɛ gbɛjianɔtoi nɛɛ batsɔ dɛŋdadei ni he hia oya kɛha mɛi ni kɛ PC tsuɔ nii.

english: The satisfaction of a perfect touch was something that Aida had never experienced before.
ga: Tsui ni nyɔɔ mɔ mli jɛɔ nine ni yeɔ emuu mli baa lɛ ji nɔ ko ni Aida enako daŋ.

english: She had been with many men, but none of them had ever been able to give her the kind of pleasure that she craved.
ga: Ekɛ hii babaoo ehi shi pɛŋ, shi amɛteŋ mɔ ko mɔ ko nyɛko aha lɛ miishɛɛ ni esumɔɔ waa lɛ pɛŋ.

english: She had often wondered if she was simply too demanding, or if she was just meant to be alone.
ga: Esusu he shii abɔ akɛ ebiɔ nibii babaoo kɛkɛ, loo eji nɔ ni afee lɛ koni ekome pɛ ahi shi kɛkɛ.

english: But then she met Hakim.
ga: Shi ekɛ Hakim kpe.

english: Hakim was different from any man she had ever met before.
ga: Esoro Hakim yɛ nuu fɛɛ nuu ni ekɛkpe daŋ.

english: He was kind, gentle, and he seemed to understand her in a way that no one else ever had.
ga: Emli hi, ehe ejɔ, ni etamɔ nɔ ni enu lɛ shishi yɛ gbɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko nuuu shishi pɛŋ nɔ.

english: He took his time with her, exploring her body with a tenderness that made her melt.
ga: Eŋmɛ etsui shi eha lɛ, ekpɛ egbɔmɔtso kɛ mlihilɛ ni ha egbɔjɔ.

english: And when he finally touched her in that special way, she felt a wave of pleasure wash over her that was unlike anything she had ever felt before.
ga: Ni beni naagbee lɛ eta ehe yɛ nakai gbɛ krɛdɛɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, enu he akɛ miishɛɛ ko ni tamɔɔɔ nɔ ko ni enu he pɛŋ lɛ miiho ehe.

english: It was as if her body had been waiting for his touch all along.
ga: Etamɔ nɔ ni egbɔmɔ lɛ miimɛ ni eta ehe be fɛɛ be.

english: She felt complete, whole, and for the first time in her life, she knew what it was to be truly satisfied.
ga: Enu he akɛ eye emuu, eyɛ muu fɛɛ, ni no ji klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa yɛ eshihilɛ mli akɛ ele nɔ ni ji tsui ni nyɔɔ mɔ mli diɛŋtsɛ.

english: As Hakim continued to touch her, she felt herself losing control.
ga: Beni Hakim yaa nɔ eta ehe lɛ, enu he akɛ enyɛɛɛ eye ehe nɔ dɔŋŋ.

english: Her body was on fire, and she could feel the tension building inside of her.
ga: Egbɔmɔtso lɛ miitso la, ni enyɛ enu shoofeemɔ ni miitswa yɛ emli lɛ he.

english: She knew that she was about to come, and she wanted it more than anything she had ever wanted before.
ga: Ele akɛ ebaaba, ni etao nakai fe nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni etao pɛŋ.

english: The hajj is a once-in-a-lifetime pilgrimage to Mecca, Saudi Arabia, that is required of all Muslims who are physically and financially able to make the journey.
ga: Hajj ji gbɛfa ni afeɔ shikome yɛ shihilɛ mli kɛyaa Mecca,Saudi Arabia, ni abiɔ ni Muslimbii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ kɛ shika baanyɛ aya gbɛfaa lɛ.

english: The pilgrimage is one of the five pillars of Islam, and it is considered to be the most important spiritual journey a Muslim can make.
ga: Gbɛfaa lɛ ji Islam shishitoo mlai enumɔ lɛ atɛŋ ekome, ni abuɔ lɛ akɛ eji mumɔŋ gbɛfaa ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ ni Muslimnyo baanyɛ aya.

english: The hajj takes place over five days in the Islamic month of Dhu al-Hijjah.
ga: Hajj lɛ yaa nɔ yɛ gbii enumɔ mli yɛ Islam nyɔŋ ni ji Dhu al-Hijjah lɛ mli.

english: During the hajj, pilgrims perform a series of rituals that commemorate the life of Prophet Muhammad and the prophets who came before him.
ga: Yɛ hajj be lɛ mli lɛ, gbɛfalɔi feɔ kusumii srɔtoi ni kaiɔ Gbalɔ Muhammad kɛ gbalɔi ni tsɔ ehiɛ lɛ ashihilɛ.

english: These rituals include walking around the Kaaba, the sacred black stone that is the center of the Great Mosque in Mecca; drinking from the Zamzam Well, which is believed to have healing powers; and standing on Mount Arafat, where Prophet Muhammad gave his final sermon.
ga: Nɛkɛ kusumii ni Kaaba he nyiɛmɔ, krɔŋkrɔŋ tɛ diŋ ni ma Great Mosque yɛ Mecca teŋ; nu ni anuɔ kɛjɛɔ Zamzam nubu lɛ mli, ni aheɔ ayeɔ akɛ eyɛ helatsamɔ hewalɛ; kɛ Mount Arafat nɔ damɔmɔ, heni Prophet Muhammad ha enaagbee shiɛmɔ wiemɔ fɛɛ fata he.

english: The hajj is a physically and emotionally demanding journey, but it is also a time for Muslims to come together in worship and to reflect on their lives.
ga: Hajj ji gbɔmɔtsoŋ kɛ henumɔ gbɛfaa, shi eji be hu kɛha Muslimbii ni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ jamɔ mli ni amɛsusu amɛshihilɛ he.

english: It is a chance to renew their faith and to reaffirm their commitment to Islam.
ga: Eji hegbɛ ni akɛbaafee amɛ hemɔkɛyeli lɛ ehee ni amɛkɛ ma amɛhe ni awɛwo lɛ nɔ mi ekoŋŋ.

english: For many Muslims, the hajj is a life-changing experience.
ga: Kɛha Muslimbii babaoo lɛ, hajj ji niiashikpamɔ ko ni tsakeɔ wala.

english: It is a time to leave behind the stresses of everyday life and to focus on their spiritual journey.
ga: Be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛshi daa gbi shihiɛ mli haomɔi lɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama amɛmumɔŋ gbɛfaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Freedom of the press is the freedom of communication and expression through mediums including printed media and the internet.
ga: Heyeli ni adafitswaa woji yɔɔ ji heyeli ni akɛgbaa sane kɛ wiemɔi ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsɔɔ nɔ ni fata he ji adafitswaa woji ni akala kɛ intanɛt lɛ.

english: It is a fundamental human right recognized by Article 19 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and reaffirmed in Article 19 of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights.
ga: Eji adesai ahegbɛ ni he hiaa waa ni jɛ adesai ahegbɛi ahe Jajemɔ lɛ mli kuku 19 lɛ mli, ni ama nɔ mi ekoŋŋ yɛ Majimaji Ateŋ Kpaŋmɔ ni kɔɔ Maŋbii kɛ Maŋkwramɔŋ Hegbɛi ahe lɛ mli kuku 19.

english: The right to freedom of expression is recognized as a necessary precondition for the enjoyment of all other human rights.
ga: Ayɔseɔ hegbɛ ni yɔɔ heyeli ni akɛwieɔ he lɛ akɛ eji nɔ ko ni he hiaa dani adesai ahegbɛi krokromɛi fɛɛ ana he miishɛɛ.

english: Freedom of the press is essential for a healthy democracy.
ga: Woji akalamɔhe lɛ heyeli he hiaa waa kɛha maŋ anɔyeli ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: It allows citizens to access information and to hold their government accountable.
ga: Ehaa maŋbii lɛ naa ni amɛbuɔ amɛ nɔyeli lɛ he akɔntaa

english: It also helps to ensure that all voices are heard, and that the public is informed about important issues.
ga: Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni akwɛɔ koni anu gbeei fɛɛ, ni aha maŋbii lɛ ale saji ni he hiaa.

english: In recent years, there have been growing threats to freedom of the press around the world.
ga: Yɛ nyɛsɛɛ afii nɛɛ amli lɛ, adafitswaa woji ni yɔɔ je lɛŋ he fɛɛ he lɛ ahe gbeyeishemɔ miiya hiɛ waa.

english: Governments have been using laws to restrict the media, and journalists have been harassed and attacked.
ga: Nɔyeli lɛ kɛ mlai miitsu nii koni ekɛtsi adafitswaa woji anaa, ni atutaa adafitswaa woji aŋmalalɔi ni atutuaa amɛ.

english: These threats are a serious concern, and they need to be addressed.
ga: Hegbeyeiwoo nɛɛ ji sane ko ni hiɛdɔɔ yɔɔ mli, ni ehe miihia ni atsu he nii.

english: We must all stand up for freedom of the press.
ga: Esa akɛ wɔ fɛɛ wɔdamɔ adafitswaa woji ahe heyeli.

english: We must defend the right of journalists to report the news without fear of reprisal.
ga: Esa akɛ wɔfa hegbɛi ni adafitswaa woji aŋmalalɔi yɔɔ lɛ he koni wɔkɛ adafitswaa lɛ abɔ he amaniɛ ni wɔsheee gbeyei akɛ abaawo wɔ nyɔmɔ.

english: We must also support independent media outlets, and we must encourage people to read and share news from a variety of sources.
ga: Esa akɛ wɔfi adafitswaa woji ni yɔɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ hu sɛɛ, ni esa wɔwo mɛi hewalɛ ni amɛkane ni amɛja adafitswaa kɛjɛ hei srɔtoi.

english: Freedom of the press is a precious right.
ga: Adafitswaa he heyeli ji hegbɛ ni jara wa waa.

english: We must all do our part to protect it.
ga: Esa akɛ wɔ fɛɛ wɔtsu wɔgbɛfaŋnɔ he nii koni wɔkɛbu he.

english: The rising temperatures and changing precipitation patterns are making it more difficult to grow crops in some areas, while at the same time creating new opportunities for agriculture in other areas.
ga: Nibii ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni tsakeɔ lɛ miifee nɔ ni wa waa akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hei komɛi, yɛ be mli ni yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa hegbei heii baa okwaayeli mli yɛ hei krokromɛi.

english: The overall effect is that the global agricultural system is becoming more complex and less predictable.
ga: Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa fɛɛ ji akɛ, jeŋ muu fɛɛ okwaayeli gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ miifee nɔ ni waa ni anyɛɛɛ atsɔɔ nɔ ni baaba.

english: One of the most direct effects of climate change on agriculture is the increase in the frequency and severity of extreme weather events.
ga: Nɔ kome ni kɔvyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛbaa yɛ okwaayeli mli lɛ ateŋ ekome ji bɔ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni naa wa waa lɛ yaa hiɛ shii abɔ kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ mlɛo ha lɛ.

english: Heat waves, droughts, floods, and storms can all damage crops and livestock, and make it difficult for farmers to get their crops to market.
ga: Dɔlɛ, hɔmɔ, nu afua, kɛ ahum fɛɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ kooloi, ni eha ewa aha okwaafoi akɛ amɛaaha amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya jara nɔ

english: In some cases, these events can cause entire crop yields to be lost, leading to food shortages and price increases.
ga: Yɛ shihilɛi komɛi amli lɛ, nibii nɛɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ afite, ni niyennii ni faaa kɛ jara ni yaa hiɛ.

english: In addition to extreme weather events, climate change is also leading to changes in the average temperature and precipitation patterns.
ga: Kɛfata kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa waa lɛ ahe lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ hu ke tsakemɔi baa hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ mli.

english: These changes are making it more difficult to grow some crops in certain areas, while at the same time creating new opportunities for agriculture in other areas.
ga: Nɛkɛ tsakemɔi nɛɛ miiha ewa waa akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi yɛ hei komɛi, yɛ be mli ni yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa hegbɛi heei baa okwaayeli mli yɛ hei krokromɛi.

english: For example, the warmer temperatures in some areas are making it possible to grow crops that were previously not possible, while the increased precipitation in other areas is making it possible to grow crops that were previously not feasible.
ga: Akɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ yɛ hei komɛi lɛ miiha ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsutsu lɛ anyɛɛɛ adu, yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ ni yaa hiɛ yɛ hei krokromɛi lɛ miiha ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsutsu lɛ anyɛɛɛ adu lɛ afee nɔ ni anyɛɔ akwɛɔ nɔ.

english: I was driving home from work one day when I got cut off by another driver.
ga: Mikɛ mitsɔne lɛ miijɛ nitsumɔ mli gbi ko kɛn ya shia beni tsɔne kudɔlɔ krokro fo mi.

english: I was so angry that I started tailgating him and flashing my lights.
ga: Mimli fu waa aahu akɛ mibɔi esɛɛ nyiɛmɔ ni mikanei lɛ tswaa.

english: He just kept driving slower and slower, and I was getting more and more frustrated.
ga: Etee nɔ ekudɔɔ tsɔne lɛ blɛoo kɛkɛ, ni minijiaŋ jeɔ wui babaoo.

english: Finally, I couldn't take it anymore.
ga: Yɛ naagbee lɛ, minyɛɛɛ ma fee dɔŋŋ.

english: I pulled up next to him and started yelling at him.
ga: Migbala kɛtee emasɛi ni mibɔi lɛ gbee.

english: He rolled down his window and started yelling back at me.
ga: Ekɛ esamflɛ lɛ shwie shi ni ebɔi mi bolɔmɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: We were both so angry that we were shaking.
ga: Wɔ fɛɛ wɔmli fu waa akɛ wɔmiikpokpo.

english: The other driver pulled over to the side of the road, and I followed him.
ga: Tsɔnekudɔlɔ krokro lɛ gbala kɛtee gbɛ lɛ he, ni minyiɛ esɛɛ.

english: We got out of our cars and started yelling at each other even louder.
ga: Wɔje wɔtsɔnei lɛ amli ni wɔbɔi bɔlɔmɔ awo wɔhe.

english: I was so close to hitting him that I could smell his breath.
ga: Mibɛŋkɛ lɛ waa akɛ manyɛ manu emumɔ lɛ he.

english: Just when I thought it couldn't get any worse, a police car pulled up.
ga: Beni misusu akɛ enyɛŋ efee nɔ ni ehiii kwraa lɛ, polisifoi atsɔne ko ba.

english: The officer got out of his car and asked us what was going on.
ga: Polisifonyo lɛ shi etsɔne lɛ mli ni ebi wɔ nɔ ni yaa nɔ.

english: We both told him our sides of the story, and he started writing us a ticket.
ga: Wɔ fɛɛ wɔ gba lɛ wɔ fai yɛ sane lɛ mli, ni ebɔi wɔ tikiti ŋmaa.

english: As I was walking back to my car, I realized that I had learned my lesson.
ga: Be ni mikuɔ misɛɛ kɛyaa mitsɔne lɛ, min akɛ mikase minikasemɔ lɛ.

english: Road rage is never worth it.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛ mli mlifu lɛ ehe ehiaaa kɔkɔɔkɔ.

english: It's not worth getting angry over, and it's not worth getting a ticket.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa ni mlifu aba, ni esaaa akɛ anaa tikiti.

english: Once upon a time, there was a beautiful river that flowed through a lush forest.
ga: Gbi ko lɛ, faa fɛɛfɛo ko ho kɛ yi koo fɛɛfɛo ko mli.

english: The river was home to many creatures, including fish, frogs, turtles, and birds.
ga: Faa lɛ ji shia ha kooloi pii, loo, odaaklɔ, akpokpolonto, kɛ okpo fata he.

english: The river was also a popular spot for humans to swim, fish, and relax.
ga: Faa lɛ hu ji he ko ni gbɛmɛi ba wuɔ nu, shaa loo, ni amɛ jɔɔ amɛhe.

english: One day, a young girl named Lily was playing near the river when she saw a turtle caught in a fishing net.
ga: Gbi ko lɛ, oblayoo ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Lily miishwɛ yɛ faa lɛ he masɛi ni ena akpokpolonto ni eka wuoyaa ko mli.

english: Lily knew that she had to help the turtle, so she ran home to get her father.
ga: Lily le akɛ sani ewa akpokpolonto, nohewɔlɛ ejo foi kɛtee shia koni etsɛ epapa.

english: Lily's father helped her to free the turtle, and the two of them returned to the river.
ga: Lily papa wa lɛ ni amɛ jiee akpokpolonto lɛ, ni amɛ enyɛ ku amɛ sɛɛ kɛtee faa lɛ.

english: The turtle thanked Lily for saving her life, and Lily promised to always be kind to animals.
ga: Akpokpolonto lɛ da Lily shi akɛ ehere ewala, ni Lily he ewo shi akɛ ebaa na kooloi fɛɛ mɔbɔ daanɛ.

english: Lily continued to visit the river often, and she always made sure to look out for any animals that might be in danger.
ga: Lily tee nɔ ni esara faa lɛ yɛ bei ako mli, ni ebɔ ehe mɔdɛɛ ekwɛ akɛ kooloi komɛi bɛ oshraa mli.

english: One day, Lily saw a group of boys throwing rocks at the fish in the river.
ga: Gbi ko lɛ, Lily na hii kuu komɛi ni amɛ fɔ tɛɛi kɛŋ tswa loo lɛ yɛ nu lɛ mli.
